Mediterranean Angel Sharks Regional Action Plan Phase 2 Implementation. Coordinates delivery of Regional Action Plan for 3 Critically Endangered angel shark species in Mediterranean. Focuses on Turkey, Cyprus, and Tunisia to protect Sawback, Smoothback & Angelshark species.

Supporting the Sustainable Management of Gulper Sharks. Reducing mortality of 15 deep-sea Gulper Shark species threatened by overfishing for liver oil (squalene). Working globally across 119 nations to ensure sustainable catch levels for these slow-reproducing sharks.

Guardians of the Blue. Documentary advocating CITES Appendix I protection for whale sharks & mobulids in Honda Bay, Philippines. Highlights marine biodiversity, ecotourism benefits, and sustainable community development through stakeholder interviews.

Angel Shark Project: Coordinated Action for the Protection of Angel Sharks Across Their Ranges. Protecting 3 Critically Endangered angel shark species in Eastern Atlantic/Mediterranean across 7 countries through legislation support, community engagement to identify key habitats, and sharing conservation toolkits via network.

Improving the Conservation Status of Sharks and Rays in the Southwest Indian Ocean. Protecting sharks/rays in SWIO hotspot through scientific research, CITES trade controls, and policy development across Madagascar, Mozambique, Tanzania & Kenya's artisanal fisheries where shark populations face severe decline.

Important Shark & Ray Areas: A Tool to Optimize Marine Protected Areas to Benefit Sharks and Rays. IUCN delineates Important Shark and Ray Areas (ISRAs) globally to optimize marine protected areas. Addresses inadequate protection by identifying scientifically-based discrete regions for threatened species conservation.

Bridging the Gap: Promoting Treaty Implementation to Recover Atlantic Sharks. Securing science-based fishing limits for Atlantic sharks (shortfin makos, blue sharks) through ICCAT management measures and aligning CITES obligations across Atlantic shark fishing nations.

Sharks International 2022. Quadrennial shark conference in Valencia, Spain (2022) with online platform. Offers talks, workshops, exhibitions for international audience. Supports shark conservation knowledge sharing globally.

The Critically Endangered Sand Tiger Shark as an Umbrella Species in the Southwestern Atlantic Ocean. Advocacy for sand tiger shark protection via CMS Appendix I listing & recreational fishing legislation in Argentine maritime provinces. Protects multiple shark species in SW Atlantic. 12-month campaign by Vida Silvestre Argentina.

Turning CITES Listings into Conservation Action. WCS project implementing CITES regulations for shark and ray species protection. Focuses on translating international trade agreements into practical conservation measures for threatened elasmobranch species.

Safeguarding Atlantic Mediterranean Elasmobranchs through RFMOs. Protects sharks/rays from finning/overfishing in Mediterranean & Atlantic via regional fishery orgs. Implements catch limits, enforces existing rules, bans at-sea fin removal. 2-year effort by Ocean Foundation & partners.

Close-Kin Mark-Recapture Methods: Designing a Scientific Study to Increase the Use of Fisheries Independent Data in Management for Atlantic Mako Sharks. Feasibility study using genetic Close-Kin Mark-Recapture methods to estimate shortfin mako abundance in Atlantic Ocean, supporting sustainable management through fisheries-independent population data.

CITES: Delivering Comprehensive Trade Regulation to Drive Global Shark Conservation. WCS works with governments in 15 countries to implement CITES shark/ray listings, improve fisheries management, enhance catch/trade data collection, and support additional species protections at CoP 19 to regulate global shark fin trade.

Improving the Understanding of Threatened Wedgefish and Guitarfish to Inform CITES Assessments. Studies biology of threatened wedgefish/guitarfish globally, focusing on Indonesia/SE Asia. Collects life history, distribution, abundance data to inform CITES conservation and local fishery management for these overfished species.

Enhancing the Conservation of Endangered Sharks and Rays in the Mediterranean. Identifies gaps in bycatch data collection for Mediterranean sharks/rays in Italy. Addresses enforcement of EU/GFCM retention bans. Targets vulnerable species facing extinction from high fishing effort and bycatch.

Global Shark Trends. IUCN Shark Specialist Group creates global dashboard tracking 1,250 shark/ray species conservation status. Combines Red List data with distribution maps to identify priority locations and policy interventions for decision-makers.

Concerted Action for the Atlantic Blue Shark (Prionace glauca). Marine Research and Conservation Foundation works with partners to achieve sustainable management of Atlantic blue sharks through CMS Concerted Actions. North Atlantic stock declined 50% in 3 generations.

Assessing the Risk of Overexploitation of the Most Traded Species of Sharks and Rays. Uses M-Risk assessment to identify heavily traded shark/ray species at overexploitation risk and determine needed management interventions. Works with Global Shark Trends project to inform managers.

Mitigating Devil Ray Bycatch from Artisanal Gillnet Fisheries in the Southwestern Gulf of California. Testing LED lights on gillnets to reduce devil ray bycatch in artisanal fisheries. Assessing survival rates and developing mitigation measures with fishing communities in Gulf of California, Mexico.

SharkTraits – A Global Life History Trait Database for Sharks and Rays. Global database compiling shark/ray life history traits (maturation, reproduction, lifespan) to support CITES listings and IUCN Red List assessments for data-deficient species. Now available as SharkiPedia.

Global Mobuild Conservation Programme. Reduces fisheries threats to manta and mobula rays in Indonesia, Sri Lanka, and Peru through policy development, community engagement, and protective measures in countries with major mobulid fisheries.

Identifying and Communicating the Ecological Importance of Sharks. Global scientists analyze datasets to determine when/why sharks matter for ocean health, how to restore populations amid rapid declines, and communicate findings to decision makers and public for better ecosystem management.

ICCAT Protections for Sharks and Rays in the Turks and Caicos Islands. Implementing ICCAT regulations banning retention of 14 shark species and mobulid rays through multilingual outreach and education campaigns for commercial and recreational fisheries stakeholders in Turks and Caicos Islands.

Responsible Coastal Fisheries Management for Shark Conservation and Marine Sustainability in Panama. Participatory planning with communities in Gulf of Chiriquí to reduce fishing impacts on sharks and marine habitats through improved regulations and voluntary measures for ocean conservation and fisheries sustainability.

Finalizing Sawfish Protection in the Bahamas. Securing national regulations to protect Critically Endangered smalltooth sawfish from fishing threats in the Bahamas, promoting enforcement and safe release practices, and expanding Caribbean-wide protections.

It's More Than Just Fins: Reducing Trade of Elasmobranch Products in Honduras. Reduce shark/ray trade in Honduras via supply chain analysis, species assessment, capacity building, and regulatory framework development for incidental captures through National Shark Working Group collaboration.

Global Shark Conservation Campaign. Implements CITES shark/ray listings in Bangladesh & Senegal through mortality controls. Supports additional species listings at 2019 CITES meeting. Focuses on South Asian & West African conservation efforts.

eDNA: A New Way to Assess Sharks for Conservation. FIU tests environmental DNA sampling vs traditional surveys at 20 Caribbean, Indian & Pacific Ocean sites to validate eDNA as cheaper, easier method for measuring shark abundance & diversity at unprecedented scales.

Maximizing Outcomes for Shark and Ray MPAs. Research to provide decision-makers tools for effective shark/ray MPAs. Develops spatial models, analyzes past MPA successes/failures, creates socio-economic criteria. Scales: national to global, coastal to open ocean.

Dangerous or Endangered? Sharks in Uruguay - Phase 2. Protecting 50 shark species in Uruguay's coastal waters through research, management plans for Isla de Lobos MPA, establishing new Restinga Pez Limón MPA, and stakeholder collaboration to promote sustainable blue economy.

Protecting the Bahamas Shark Sanctuary. Assessing 10-year impact of Bahamas' 2011 shark sanctuary across their EEZ. Doctoral student repeats 2015/16 Global FinPrint survey to evaluate protection effects on shark populations and human ocean users.

Contributing to the Declaration of Tiquisate-Sipacate an Important Site for Sharks and Rays. Collaborating with government and communities to declare Sipacate and Tecojate nursery sites as Important Shark and Ray Areas (ISRAs) through monitoring and workshops in Guatemala's coastal waters.

Implementing the National Plan of Action of Sharks and Rays in Guatemala's Pacific Coast and CITES. FUNMZ implements Guatemala's 2021-2026 NPOA for sharks, rays & chimaeras, collaborating with authorities & fishing communities to ensure elasmobranch protection & sustainable management through CITES compliance.

Closing the Triangle: A New MPA for Sharks and Rays in the Nicoya Peninsula. Establishing a new marine protected area in Costa Rica's Nicoya Peninsula to protect critical shark and ray habitats, particularly for hammerhead nursery grounds in the Eastern Tropical Pacific.

Updating the Zoning of the Galapagos Marine Reserve as a Tool for Sustainable Management and Shark Conservation. Developing enforceable zoning plan for Galapagos Marine Reserve through participatory process with fishing communities, using latest science to protect sharks and marine biodiversity in one of world's largest MPAs.

Enhancing Elasmobranch Conservation through the Convention on Migratory Species (CMS). Expert report documenting CMS Parties' performance on 34 shark/ray species obligations. Engages countries on Atlantic shortfin Mako protection, informs sawfish conservation, highlights shortfalls and solutions.

Strengthening Fisheries Management and Conservation Strategies for the Brazilian Guitarfish in its Southern Distribution Boundary. Protecting critically endangered Brazilian guitarfish in El Rincón, Argentina through policy reform, research, and stakeholder engagement. Targets mating aggregations threatened by recreational fishing tournaments along Patagonian coast.

Identifying the Last Remaining Areas of the Critically Endangered Largetooth Sawfish in Costa Rica. Research to identify and monitor critical habitats of Critically Endangered largetooth sawfish in Costa Rica, working with government to develop a Sawfish Conservation Plan for Central America population recovery.

Sharks of Ilha Grande Bay: Safeguarding Critical Habitats for Sharks in Brazil. Protecting shark habitats in Ilha Grande Bay, Brazil through conservation efforts focused on safeguarding critical marine areas for shark populations.

Assessing Elasmobranch Nurseries on a Global Conservation Hotspot for Improved Management. Investigating Brazil's North Coast as communal nursery for threatened sharks/rays using vertebrae microchemistry to analyze habitat use and develop conservation areas amid artisanal fishing pressures.

Strengthening Sharks and Rays Fisheries Management Regulation and Improving Catch Monitoring. Influence public policies for elasmobranch conservation in Guatemala. Establish Technical Group to update National Plan of Action for Chondrichthyes. Monitor landings to provide data for sustainable fisheries management.

Assessing the Effectiveness of Jardines de la Reina National Park in Shark and Ray Conservation. Investigates movement patterns and habitat use of hammerhead sharks and rays in Cuba's Jardines de la Reina MPA to inform effective management of IUCN endangered and CITES regulated species.

Stopping Costa Rican Exports of Endangered Shark Species. Media & policy advocacy to stop threatened shark exports from Costa Rica. Addresses scientific gaps in fisheries authority decisions, promotes Executive Decree for multisectoral, science-based shark management & conservation.

Protecting Nursery Areas for the Scalloped Hammerhead Shark in the Colombian Pacific Coast. Protect scalloped hammerhead nursery in Colombian Pacific by delimiting areas, reducing angler-shark interaction, promoting better fishing practices, training anglers in resuscitation techniques and data collection for authorities.

Dangerous or Endangered: Sharks in Uruguay. Pilot project creating Uruguay's first shark/ray database combining fisher & scientific data. Works with fisheries, communities, schools to shift perception from 'dangerous' to 'endangered' & inform MPA policies.

Developing a Science-Based Approach to Scale Up Transboundary Marine Policy and Management: The Designation of the Galapagos-Cocos Swimway. Establishing legal protection for Cocos-Galapagos swimway corridor between MPAs. Creating first protected transboundary swimway in Eastern Tropical Pacific with binational governance structure between Costa Rica & Ecuador.

Reducing Catch and Post-Release Mortality of Elasmobranchs in Small-Scale Fisheries of Colombia. Reducing shark/ray bycatch in Colombian Pacific artisanal fisheries through gear modifications and practice changes with fishermen via participatory workshops to decrease elasmobranch mortality.

Enhancing Morphological Tool to Identify Shark Fins Combating the International Illegal Trade. Develops software/app using digital image analysis to identify CITES-listed shark species from fins, enabling enforcement officers to combat illegal trade through fast, reliable species identification at ports.

Sustainable Shark and Ray Management Regulations and Continued Population Monitoring in Tobago. Develop sustainable shark/ray management regulations in NE Tobago's 60,000ha nominated MPA through government-civil society collaboration. Monitor populations to inform policy against commercial longline threats.

Protecting Endangered Shark Species in Argentina: A Flagship for Coastal Environments Conservation. Fish Ecology Lab in Patagonia develops critical shark conservation knowledge and direct initiatives using holistic strategy for shark and coastal habitat protection in Argentina.

Restoring the Pacific Angelshark Population in Peru. Collecting biological & fisheries data on Pacific angelshark (97% decline 2001-2015) to develop management strategies for sustainable use in Peru. Species is Near Threatened with no current protection measures.

Largetooth Sawfish in the Amazonian Coast: Presence and Improving Enforcement in this Twilight Zone. Protecting endangered Largetooth Sawfish on Amazonian Coast through enforcement training, fisher safe-release guidance, ID guides, and eDNA analysis to confirm presence in this critical stronghold region.

Saving Oceanic White-tips in their Final Atlantic Stronghold. Protecting Critically Endangered oceanic whitetip sharks in Western Atlantic. Relic population in Bahamas sanctuary studied for decade. Aims to reduce mortality from targeted/bycatch fisheries in Bahamas, Dominican Republic, Haiti, Cuba.

Sharks from the Interjurisdictional Marine Coastal Park Patagonia Austral PIMCPA: A Research and Conservation Initiative. Research large sharks in central Patagonia using underwater video, tagging, and fishermen knowledge to guide conservation. Aims to ban shark killing and raise awareness among fishermen in South West Atlantic.

Reconstruction of Historical Catches for Shark CITES Species in Mexico to Strengthen NDF Issuance. Reconstructs historical catch data of CITES-listed sharks in Mexico to assess population status and support Non-detriment findings. Addresses data gaps in a top shark fishing nation and leading fin exporter.

Reduce Fishing Efforts Over Endemic Imperiled Sharks in Uruguay Using a Sustainable Haul System. Prevent extinction of endemic Angelshark & smooth-hound in Uruguay by reducing bycatch mortality. Testing Sustainable Haul Gear System in 2 communities, targeting valuable bony fish instead of threatened sharks.

CITES Sharks Management Workshop for Guatemalan Customs, Fisheries Officers and Private Exporters. Two-day workshop training 60+ Guatemalan officers on shark fin identification to implement CITES trade restrictions, addressing illegal shark fin trade threatening endangered species through capacity building in species ID.

Campaign to Restore America's Sharks and Rays. Coalition raises shark/ray conservation profile with US federal government and Congress. Restores US leadership in science-based shark conservation and strengthens fisheries management through advocacy.

Ensuring the Recovery of Endangered U.S. Sawfish. Track & accelerate recovery of Florida's smalltooth sawfish through outreach, enforcement of safeguards, research under ESA Recovery Plan, NGO partnerships for habitat conservation & fisheries management.

Conservation Actions for Sharks and Skates in Patagonia. WCS-Argentina protects endemic sharks/skates in Argentine waters via Patagonian Coastal Corridor MPA for critical life phases & action plan for Critically Endangered tope shark in key MPA. 3-year project in Patagonia.

Hammerhead Shark (Sphyrna lewini) Nursery Areas in the Eastern Colombian Pacific. Acoustic & satellite tagging of 11 hammerhead sharks to identify nursery areas in Colombian Pacific. 3 acoustic receptors deployed along coast. Provides data for management plans to protect endangered species.

Strengthening the Implementation of CITES in Mexico for Appendix II Listed Sharks. Training local champions in Pacific fishing camps to improve CITES arrival notices reliability for 9 commercially relevant shark species, supporting sustainable export management in areas with 70% of shark landings.

Assessing the Recovery of the Smalltooth Sawfish: A Kin-Based Approach. Evaluates smalltooth sawfish population recovery using kin-based genetic analysis. Assesses conservation effectiveness in US waters where species is critically endangered. Applies innovative DNA methods to track population trends.

Sharks & Rays Conservation Initiative: Shark Fin Transit Project Phase 1. Investigates shark fin transit through US ports from Central America to Asia. Assesses volumes, routes, species, ports, and US legal authority to monitor and seize illegal shipments. Addresses poorly understood fin trade problem.

Closing the Gap in U.S. Caribbean Scalloped Hammerhead Protections. Earthjustice works to close regulatory loopholes allowing unregulated catch of juvenile scalloped hammerheads in Puerto Rico, using science to identify nursery areas and legal strategies to secure comprehensive ESA protections for threatened sharks.

Strengthening Shark and Ray Conservation within the Western and Central Pacific Fisheries Commission. Analysis of regulatory gaps in WCPFC shark/ray fisheries management. Provides recommendations to strengthen framework implementing CITES/CMS requirements for directed fisheries and bycatch in Western-Central Pacific.

Implementing a Transboundary Swimway in the Eastern Tropical Pacific Ocean. Establishing first transboundary swimway between Galapagos and Cocos Islands MPAs to protect migrating sharks, turtles and marine wildlife in the Eastern Tropical Pacific.

Can eDNA be used to track changes in shark populations?. Comparing aerial shark counts with water DNA concentration to develop cheap, easy population monitoring. Testing if environmental DNA can replace expensive fishing/video surveys for tracking shark numbers and conservation success.

Saving Caribbean Sawfishes. Improving scientific understanding and legal protection of endangered sawfish populations in Bahamas and Cuba. Addressing local extinctions through research and conservation partnerships to reverse declines of these rays.

Sharks & Rays Conservation Initiative: Shark Fin Transit Project Phase II. NRDC reviews U.S. laws and international treaties to strengthen provisions against shark fin trafficking. Develops strategies to leverage U.S. legal framework and enforcement to combat illegal shark fin trade globally.
Protecting Scalloped Hammerhead Nurseries in Puerto Rico. Conservation of scalloped hammerhead shark nursery habitats in Puerto Rico's coastal waters through research and protection measures.

Balloon-Busting Crew. Educates public about balloon debris harming sea turtles and marine life through ingestion and entanglement. Promotes alternatives to balloon releases. Active in Texas coastal areas where balloons frequently wash ashore.

Adopt-A-Block Program. Community litter prevention in Galveston where residents/businesses adopt 1-5 blocks (500 sq yards) for year-round cleanup. Supplies provided, data tracked via NOAA Marine Debris app to combat plastic pollution.

Bring the Bag. Partnership with Surfrider Galveston to reduce single-use plastic bags in Galveston, TX. Installing reminder signs at stores, declaring Bring the Bag Day, promoting reusable bags to protect sea turtles from plastic pollution.

Save the Leatherback. Preventing Pacific leatherback extinction through fishing restrictions, habitat protection, and policy advocacy. Implemented Pacific Leatherback Conservation Area reducing deaths from 112 to near zero. Focus: California/Oregon coast.

Hold On To Your Butt. Turtle Island & Surfrider tackle cigarette butt pollution in Galveston by installing 50+ butt cans, recycling via TerraCycle, public education, and citizen science to protect marine life from plastic filter ingestion and toxic contamination.

California Set Gillnet Bycatch Reduction Campaign. Campaign to ban set gillnets in Southern California offshore waters (3-200 miles). Nets catch 125 species with 64% discarded; threaten sea turtles, sharks, marine mammals. Advocacy for selective fishing methods.

The Cocos-Galapagos Swimway. Protecting marine corridor between Costa Rica's Cocos Island & Ecuador's Galapagos where sea turtles, whale sharks, hammerhead sharks migrate. Urging governments to establish protected swimway against industrial fishing threats.

Stop Expanded Offshore Drilling and Protect Cordell Bank National Marine Sanctuary. Opposing offshore drilling expansion & fishing in Cordell Bank Sanctuary (50mi NW San Francisco). Protects whales, sea turtles, seabirds, rockfish from industrial threats through advocacy & science-based policy.

Take Action to Stop Offshore Drilling. Opposition campaign against Trump's offshore drilling plan covering 1.27B acres. Threatens Alaska, Gulf of Mexico, California, Florida coasts. Protects marine wildlife, coastal communities from drilling risks.

Rice's Whale Conservation in the Gulf of Mexico. Urging federal protection for critically endangered Rice's whale (<100 remaining) in Gulf of Mexico through 28,000 sq mi critical habitat designation, vessel speed limits, opposing oil/gas expansion threatening the species with strikes and pollution.

The Final Straw Galveston. Campaign to eliminate single-use plastic straws in Galveston Island restaurants/bars to protect sea turtles from plastic pollution. Provides resources for businesses to switch to reusable/paper straws. Started March 2020.

Oppose Restarting Sable Offshore's Pipeline That Caused Devastating 2015 Oil Spill. Campaign opposing Trump admin's use of Defense Production Act to restart failed offshore oil pipeline that spilled 500k gallons across 150 miles of California coast in 2015, bypassing state safety laws

Speak Up for Northeast Canyons and Seamounts Marine National Monument. Advocacy campaign to protect Northeast Canyons and Seamounts Marine National Monument, a deep-sea ecosystem off New England coast with unique marine biodiversity including sea turtles, whales, and corals.

Protect Harbor Porpoises from Atlantic Gillnet Fisheries. Advocacy to prevent NMFS deregulation of gillnet twine size from 0.90mm to 0.81mm in Atlantic waters. Aims to reduce harbor porpoise bycatch through stricter regulations, acoustic pingers, and better monitoring. Comment deadline Feb 2.

Uphold the Clean Water Act: Protect Our Waters & Wetlands. Advocacy campaign opposing EPA's proposed WOTUS rule weakening Clean Water Act protections for streams and wetlands. Focuses on preventing pollution in watersheds affecting coastal areas like Galveston. Public comment period through Jan 2026.

Uphold the Legacy of the Marine Mammal Protection Act. Advocacy campaign opposing Congressional bill weakening Marine Mammal Protection Act. Protects whales, dolphins, seals from industrial impacts, offshore drilling. Maintains healthy populations vs survival standard.

Prevent Deep-Sea Mining Near the Mariana Trench Marine National Monument. Campaign to prevent deep-sea mining near Mariana Trench Marine National Monument, protecting unique seamount ecosystems and marine biodiversity in the Pacific Ocean's deepest waters.

Protect Marine National Monuments from Commercial Fishing. Campaign opposing Executive Order 14276 that threatens to open U.S. marine national monuments to commercial fishing. Advocates for ocean protection from industrial fishing gear that harms sea turtles, whales, and marine ecosystems through bycatch.

Deep-Sea Mining: Stop the Race to the Bottom. Campaign opposing NOAA rule allowing simultaneous deep seabed exploration and mining permits. Advocates for moratorium to protect fragile deep-sea ecosystems from irreversible harm caused by mining operations.

A Call to the Sea - Art & Science Residency. Art-science residency at Vasco da Gama Aquarium, Lisbon, exploring more-than-human geographies, multispecies narratives, water intelligence. 3-month projects Jul-Dec 2024, €10k funding, access to marine sites, Tagus estuary.

Ressonâncias. Sound art project exploring aquatic ecosystems through sonic practices with migrant students in Esposende. Combines field recording, composition, and ecological materialities to amplify aquatic environments and their social manifestations.

Mare Liberum. Youth sailing program on replica caravel Vera Cruz combining navigation with creative workshops (writing, photography, cinema, theater) exploring themes of sea, horizon & freedom. Lisboa/Oeiras 2019-2022, 74 youth participants.

Gulbenkian Carbono Azul. Maps & characterizes blue carbon ecosystems (seagrass, salt marshes, kelp forests) across Portugal to enable conservation/restoration investments. Pioneers voluntary blue carbon market, starting with pilot project to offset foundation's 2021 emission

Blue Bio Value. Accelerator for marine bioeconomy startups using ocean resources sustainably. Addresses food security, climate change, aging population, resource scarcity. Aims to make Portugal a global leader in marine biotechnology.

5 Gyres Institute - Marine Plastic Pollution Research. Research on ocean plastic pollution sources including microfibers, textiles, fishing gear. Studies microplastic contamination in oceans, coastal zones. Tests alternatives, nature-based solutions like floating wetlands. Global scope, ongoing.

Do Less for the Planet - Textile Microfiber Pollution Reduction. Campaign to reduce marine microplastic pollution from textiles through lifestyle changes: buying less fast fashion, washing clothes less frequently, and repairing garments. Textiles are the largest source of marine microfibers.

5 Gyres Institute Advocacy for Microplastic Pollution Policy. Leading microplastic pollution research org drives policy to reduce plastic harm. Campaigns include #MicroplasticFreeUS & #PlasticFreeParks. Passed Microbead-Free Waters Act 2015, CA foodware laws. Ongoing since 2015.

Plastic Smog: 40-Year Ocean Plastic Pollution Trend Analysis. Analysis of 10,000+ ocean samples showing plastic particle trends from 1970s-present. Post-2005 data reveals skyrocketing plastic levels correlating with shift from binding maritime laws to voluntary policies.

Trash Academy. Virtual educational series in English/Spanish on plastic pollution. Covers plastic origins, environmental harm, solutions, and industry sectors using plastic. Integrates education, advocacy, and community science.

5 Gyres Ambassador Network - Global Plastic Pollution Action. Global network of 1,952 ambassadors across 95 countries combating plastic pollution through science, advocacy, and TrashBlitz cleanups. Includes Action Fund supporting marine conservation research and community mobilization.

Strengthening Marine Enforcement in the Eastern Tropical Pacific Seascape. Launched 2024 to combat IUU fishing across Ecuador, Costa Rica, Colombia, Panama. Enhances monitoring, surveillance, regional cooperation. Protects biodiversity hotspots including 4 UNESCO sites. Benefits 15,000+ coastal residents.

Protecting marine biodiversity and coastal communities in the Philippines. Strengthening fisheries law enforcement in Coral Triangle through 16 community patrol teams, 3 patrol boats delivered Oct 2024. Partners: Rare, Canada, local governments. Combats IUU fishing, supports 1.9M fishers.

Microfibers & Textiles Research and Solutions. 5 Gyres addresses microfiber pollution from synthetic clothing through scientific research, expeditions, symposiums, and policy advocacy. Focuses on filtration solutions and industry supply chain strategies to reduce microfibers in oceans.

Pemba Channel Conservation Area Protection. Protecting Pemba Channel's diverse coral reefs & endangered species. WildAid Marine partners with local communities since 2019, providing patrol boats & training to combat illegal fishing in 1,200 km2 protected area.

Galapagos Marine Reserve Protection. Protecting 51,000 sq mi reserve off Ecuador since 2002. Combating illegal fishing of sharks & sea cucumbers through enforcement, VMS/AIS monitoring, ranger training, & Navy partnerships. Now world's densest shark population.

Arctic Ocean Conservation. Protecting Arctic Ocean biodiversity through science-based advocacy. Opposing offshore oil drilling, regulating shipping, establishing marine protected areas. Addressing climate change impacts on wildlife and Indigenous communities.

Coastal Ecuador Marine Conservation. Protecting 19 coastal MPAs & mangrove concessions in Ecuador since 2015. Strengthening enforcement, training rangers, equipping patrols to protect sea turtles, mantas, sharks & support 87k artisanal fishers.

Protecting Africa's Last Eden - Gabon Marine Conservation. WildAid partners with DGPA since 2022 to combat illegal fishing in Gabon's 200,000 km2 EEZ. Provides patrol vessels, surveillance equipment, training for fisheries inspectors to protect leatherback turtles, dolphins, whales.

Better Alternatives 3.0: Bioplastics Environmental Degradation Study. 64-week study testing 22 bioplastic items across marine & terrestrial environments in FL, CA, ME. Found environment, thickness, polymer type affect degradation. Aims to provide transparency on bioplastic alternatives to single-use plastics.

Bahamas Marine Protection System. Partnership to combat IUU fishing in Bahamas' EEZ. Developing comprehensive Marine Protection System Plan for 630,000 km2 sanctuary protecting 40+ shark species, lobster, conch fisheries. Started 2018 with TNC & govt agencies.

Protecting the Yucatan Peninsula's Sustainable Fisheries. WildAid & Impact Blue support fishing federations in Yucatan Peninsula to transition to sustainable lobster & octopus fisheries. Provides enforcement equipment, training, patrol strategy. Started Nov 2020, working with 3 federations.

5 Gyres Research Expeditions - Global Plastic Pollution Investigation. 19 research expeditions across 50,000 nautical miles investigating plastic pollution in ocean gyres. Citizen science trawls, microplastic sampling, marine mammal health studies. Global coverage: Arctic, Atlantic, Pacific, Galapagos, Belize.

Protecting Palau's Coral Reefs, One of the Seven Underwater Wonders of the World. Strengthening enforcement for 29 MPAs in Palau since 2014. Training rangers, providing patrol equipment, developing Marine Protection System plans. Protecting 500+ coral species, 1,300 reef fish species in Coral Triangle waters.

Greywater from Passenger Vessels in Alaska. Reviews greywater contents, volumes & management from passenger vessels in Alaska. Analyzes 19 years of ADEC sampling data to improve greywater management practices in Alaska & internationally.

How Do Oil Spills Effect the Arctic?. Ocean Conservancy partnered with Dr. Suprenand to model oil spill impacts in Beaufort Sea Arctic ecosystem, evaluating effects on polar bears, seals, fish, and indigenous communities from platform, pipeline, and vessel spills.

Plastic Free Cities. Youth-led program engaging students, businesses & local governments to eliminate single-use plastics in Florida. 240+ students trained, 100+ businesses engaged, preventing 1.2M+ plastic items annually in Miami-Dade, expanding to Orlando & Tampa Bay.

Navigating the North: An Assessment of the Environmental Risks of Arctic Vessel Traffic. Assessment of Arctic vessel traffic environmental risks: oil spills, air emissions, invasive species, marine mammal disturbance, sewage discharge. Provides recommendations for Arctic marine protection.

Protecting Central Arctic Ocean. International accord bans commercial fishing in 1.1M sq mi Central Arctic Ocean for 16+ years while scientists research marine life impacts from climate change. 10 parties signed Oct 2018.

Healthy Fisheries - Magnuson-Stevens Act Implementation. US fishery management via MSA (1976-present). Eight regional councils govern federal waters (3-200 nautical miles offshore). Reduced overfishing to all-time low through science-based management and diverse stakeholder input.

Sea Level Rise in Florida. Protecting Florida's 1,350-mile coastline from 3-8 ft sea level rise by 2100. Restoring coastal ecosystems as nature-based solutions. Supporting 7.4M residents within 6 ft of sea level through habitat conservation.

Ensuring the magic of Florida's coasts lasts forever. Comprehensive conservation addressing harmful algal blooms, pollution, sea level rise, coral disease, and seagrass loss across Florida's coasts through policy advocacy, community engagement, and beach cleanups. Ongoing statewide effort.

Central Arctic Ocean Sea Ice Protection. Protecting Central Arctic Ocean from fishing, shipping & deep-sea mining as ice melts. 10 countries agreed to ban commercial fishing until 2037. Monitoring dramatic ice loss: thickness down 52%, 20% now open water in summer.

Restoring the Gulf of Mexico's Red Snapper Fishery. Rebuilding Gulf red snapper from 2% historic biomass through 27-year recovery plan to 2032. Addresses overfishing challenges, supports sustainable fisheries management for fishermen and communities in Gulf of Mexico region.

e-Navigation in Arctic Waters: Enhancing Safe and Environmentally Sound Maritime Operations. Advancing navigation & communication tech to enhance shipping safety & environmental protection in U.S. Arctic waters. Partnership with Marine Exchange of Alaska using real-time GPS, AIS & e-charting.

The Arctic Ahead. Addressing rapid Arctic environmental changes: rising temps, ocean acidification, diminishing sea ice, thawing permafrost, coastal erosion. Protecting Arctic wildlife & peoples from unprecedented climate impacts in U.S. Arctic.

Global Ghost Gear Initiative. Global alliance combating abandoned fishing gear (ghost gear) through removal, prevention, policy development, and stakeholder collaboration. Active worldwide since 2015, hosted by Ocean Conservancy since 2019.

Arctic Corporate Shipping Pledge. Voluntary pledge by companies to avoid Arctic shipping routes to protect rapidly melting sea ice and ecosystems. Promotes precautionary practices including heavy fuel oil bans and pollution controls.

Healthy Fisheries. Why: Sustain fish populations for ecosystems, food security & economy. What: Science-based fishery management across US waters. How: Policy advocacy, data collection, POSEIDON AI tool. Where: US coasts, Gulf of Mexico, Pacific. When: 25+ years ongoin

Ocean to Everglades (O2E) Initiative - Super Bowl LIV Miami Partnership. Partnership with Miami Super Bowl Host Committee (Feb 2019-Feb 2020) to reduce ocean plastic and promote sustainability. Removed 54 tons of waste from Florida coasts through cleanups, reduced plastics at Hard Rock Stadium, featured sustainable seafoo

North American Net Collection Initiative (NANCI). First transboundary initiative addressing ghost fishing gear in Mexico, US & Canada waters. Removes abandoned nets, creates predictive hotspot maps, recycles 14+ tons into products, trains 800+ fishers across 17 Mexican states.

100% Clean Ocean Energy by 2050. Transition from fossil fuels to responsible clean ocean energy through offshore wind, wave/tidal energy. Focuses on responsible planning, ending oil/gas leases, marine-safe development, policy reform. By 2050 target.

Considering Deep-Sea Source Minerals and Rare Elements. Reviews climate implications of deep-sea mining for critical minerals. Identifies knowledge gaps in environmental risks, ocean carbon storage, biodiversity impacts. Concludes mining should not proceed until uncertainties resolved.

Decarbonizing Shipping. Reducing shipping emissions globally. Shipping emits 1B tons CO2/year (3% global GHGs). Solutions: IMO emissions plan targeting 50-100% reduction by 2050, slow steaming, fossil fuel elimination. US leadership to set international standards.

Climate-Smart Marine Protected Areas for Mitigation and Adaptation Policy. Policy brief on MPAs for climate mitigation/adaptation. Reviews carbon sequestration, ecosystem resilience, biodiversity preservation. Guides policymakers on climate-smart MPA design. Global ocean-climate policy.

Ocean-Based Climate Solutions. Global initiative promoting ocean solutions for climate: offshore wind, clean marine transport, blue carbon wetlands protection. Targets 1/5 of GHG cuts by 2050. Includes UK offshore wind, Marshall Islands shipping proposals, Costa Rica wetlands.

Ocean Carbon Dioxide Removal Research. Research program studying ocean CDR techniques to remove atmospheric CO2 via biological, physical & geochemical processes. Develops code of conduct, assesses effectiveness & biodiversity impacts. Global ocean focus.

Ocean-Climate Guide to Action. Guide for countries to include ocean-based climate mitigation & adaptation in Paris Agreement plans. Addresses ocean's role in fighting climate change through economic activities worth $1T+ annually.

Models for Ocean-Climate Action Along the Pacific Coast of North America. Pacific Coast Collaborative (WA, CA, OR, BC) shares climate mitigation/adaptation policies addressing local ocean impacts. Aims to guide others via documented experience and best practices.

Action Plan for Blue-Green Shipping Investment in the Pacific. Decarbonize Pacific shipping/ports via clean fuels, renewable energy, climate-ready infrastructure. 4 pillars: finance clean ships, develop port renewables, build resilient ports, foster connectivity. Targets midcentury zero emissions.

Blueprint for International Ocean-Climate Action. Global framework addressing ocean-climate linkages through marine protected areas, blue carbon restoration, and policy recommendations. Targets governments and stakeholders at international summits for holistic ocean-climate solutions.

Ocean-Climate Actions to Support the Biden-Harris Decarbonization Plan. Ocean-based climate solutions for US decarbonization: offshore renewables, shipping emissions cuts. Targets 6-21% global emissions reductions to limit warming to 1.5°C. Focus on first 100 days.

Overlooked Ocean Strategies to Address Climate Change. Advocates for ocean integration in Paris Agreement climate plans via 4 strategies: sustainable ocean mitigation, CO2 reduction for acidification, ocean-based mitigation research, and ocean adaptation.

All Aboard: How the Biden-Harris Administration Can Help Ships Kick Fossil Fuels. Policy report by Ocean Conservancy & Pacific Environment on eliminating shipping industry greenhouse gas emissions. Recommends US set emissions reduction timeline before 2050 to combat climate change from 50,000+ ocean vessels.

Future Maritime Fuels USA. Transitioning US shipping from fossil fuels to scalable zero emission fuels (SZEF) to meet Paris Agreement goals. Report analyzes energy sources, propulsion tech, and pathways for maritime decarbonization this decade.

Analysis of Liquefied Natural Gas as a Marine Fuel in the United States. Research analyzing LNG marine fuel risks for shipping emissions. Examines policies, engine tech, vessel fleets, health impacts. Concludes LNG not climate solution due to methane potency. Published 2024.

State Climate Action - Ocean Climate Solutions. State-level ocean climate solutions for mitigation & adaptation. Integrates climate planning into coastal management, builds coalitions, shares best practices across jurisdictions for emissions reduction & resilience.

Ocean-Based Climate Solutions in Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs). Tracks ocean-based climate actions in Paris Agreement NDCs. 93 of 100 coastal countries include ocean elements. Monitors blue carbon ecosystems & marine solutions in national climate goals updated every 5 years since 2023.

Zero-Carbon Shipping North America. Explores zero-carbon electrofuels (green hydrogen, ammonia) adoption at 5 major west coast ports. Aims to transition maritime shipping to emission-free future through renewable-powered fuels and port investments.

Green Shipping Corridors. Maritime routes testing zero-emission fuels/tech to decarbonize shipping by 2040. Aims for 5% zero-emission fuels by 2030 to meet Paris Agreement goals. Addresses shipping's 1+ gigatonne annual CO2 emissions.

Propelling investment in South and Central America with hydrogen-based shipping fuels. Report identifies ports in Central & South America ready to develop green electrofuels from renewable energy to enable zero-carbon maritime shipping. Published 2020 by Ocean Conservancy to accelerate low-carbon fuel adoption.

Gulf of Mexico Alliance. Regional partnership of 5 Gulf states addressing ocean-climate challenges through Priority Issue Teams. Tackles water quality, HABs, microplastics via Gulf Star Program funding. Established 2004, Gulf Coast region.

Maritime Fleet USA Decarbonisation. US shipping fleet decarbonisation via zero-emission fuels & energy efficiency to meet Paris Agreement targets. Data-driven approach identifies opportunities across US coastal regions for maritime climate action.

Ocean-Based Climate Solutions Act. First comprehensive U.S. bill on ocean-climate action. Reduces shipping emissions, supports offshore wind, protects 30% ocean waters by 2030, creates climate-ready fisheries, funds living shorelines, addresses acidification.

Transitioning the Shipping Industry to Green Hydrogen. Why: Eliminate shipping emissions by 2050. What: Green hydrogen fuel transition. How: Renewable energy electrolysis, green shipping corridors, US govt support. When: 2022-2050. Where: US ports & international routes.

Action Agenda for a Blue-Green Future. Federal ocean-climate policy recommendations addressing greenhouse gas pollution threats. Focuses on blue carbon, offshore renewables, MPAs, fisheries, reducing shipping emissions. Targets midcentury decarbonization.

Ocean-Climate Actions to Support the Biden-Harris Plan to Build Back Better. Ocean-based climate solutions for Biden-Harris first 100 days addressing coastal flooding, ocean acidification, water quality, fisheries & ecosystem loss to build physical, economic, social & ecological resilience

Opportunities for Ocean-Climate Action in the American Jobs Plan. Policy advocacy urging US federal investment in ocean-climate solutions, clean energy tech, and coastal community adaptation through the American Jobs Plan to reduce emissions and address climate inequities.

Plastic Everywhere Except One Place: Climate Commitments. Ocean Conservancy examined 28 companies, 12 investors, and 15 climate frameworks to address gaps in plastic-climate commitments. Develops 10 First Principles to incorporate plastics into climate goals.

Principles of a Blue-Green Recovery. Climate-smart economic recovery leveraging ocean solutions for job creation, climate mitigation & adaptation. Targets US stimulus legislation to protect economy long-term while benefiting frontline communities.

California's Ocean-Climate Contribution. California's ocean-climate contribution supporting Paris Agreement at COP24. Addresses climate mitigation and adaptation strategies for ocean resilience, submitted as part of Nationally Determined Contributions framework.

Fibers to Filters: A Toolkit for Microfiber Solutions. Addresses microplastic pollution from washing clothes through microfiber filtration in washing machines. Coauthored by Ocean Conservancy, 5 Gyres Institute, and The Nature Conservancy to prevent microfibers entering oceans.

Ocean-Based Solutions Contribute to Net Zero - Global Climate Summit. Why: Address climate crisis through ocean solutions. What: Global commitments on offshore wind, zero-emission shipping, 30% ocean protection, blue carbon. How: MPAs, renewable energy, habitat restoration. When: April 2021. Where: Global

Federal Actions to Deliver on America's Offshore Wind Potential. Policy recommendations to scale US offshore wind 700x by 2030, preventing 78M metric tons CO2 emissions. Addresses regulatory challenges via BOEM, NOAA, USCG coordination to achieve climate goals with minimal ecosystem impact.

International Coastal Cleanup®. Global volunteer program removing trash from beaches/waterways. 19M+ volunteers collected 400M+ lbs since 1986. Uses Clean Swell app to track debris data. Ongoing cleanups worldwide to combat plastic pollution.

Elements of a Blue-Green Foreign Policy. US ocean-climate diplomacy integrating marine issues into global climate action: Paris Agreement, emissions targets, shipping decarbonization, marine protected areas, offshore renewables. Policy brief for Administration.

Plastics Policy Solutions for Ocean Conservation. Advancing evidence-based policies to reduce plastic pollution at source. Focuses on eliminating single-use packaging, microplastics through EPR, state legislation, filters for microfibers. Ongoing US-wide advocacy.

Ocean Acidification: Confronting our ocean's changing chemistry. Why: CO2 pollution acidifies oceans, threatening marine life. What: Research & advocacy to protect shellfish, coral, fisheries. How: Collaborate with communities, scientists, policymakers. Where: US coasts (Chesapeake, West Coast, Florida)

Collective Currents: Global Solutions to End Ocean Plastics. Global initiative tackling ocean plastic pollution through zero waste systems, extended producer responsibility policies, and strategic cleanup. Provides roadmap for communities, governments, companies to end plastic pollution worldwide.

Tackling Plastic Pollution Through Producer Accountability. Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) policy toolkit holding plastic producers financially accountable for product lifecycle. Requires reduction of single-use plastics, redesign for reusability, investment in recycling infrastructure across US state

Modeling Wildlife Mortality Risk From Ingested Plastics. Quantifies marine wildlife death risk from macroplastic ingestion using 10,000+ necropsy datapoints. Models mortality likelihood for sea turtles, seabirds, mammals. Published PNAS Nov 2025. Includes Wildlife Impact Calculator tool.

Working towards a legally binding instrument to end plastic pollution. UN-led global treaty negotiations (INC-5.2, Aug 2025, Geneva) to create legally binding agreement addressing plastic pollution lifecycle: source reduction, ghost gear, microplastics, circular design, waste collector inclusion

Pandemic Pollution: The Rising Tide of Plastic PPE. Volunteers removed 107,219 PPE items from beaches/waterways in late 2020. Tracks COVID-19 pandemic's impact on plastic pollution via Clean Swell app. Provides recommendations for responsible PPE waste management.

Ocean Plastics Research Program. Why: Plastic pollution threatens 1,300+ marine species. What: Research on wildlife impacts, human exposure, pollution prevention. How: Risk assessments, monitoring protocols, tracking trash movement. Where: Global, North America rivers, American Samo

Indonesia Longline Tuna Swordfish Fishery: Enhancing Observer Monitoring. Training onboard observers to monitor 364 longline vessels in Indonesia's Indian Ocean EEZ. Improves data on bycatch, ETP species interactions, aligns with IOTC regulations and MSC standards for sustainable tuna fishery.

What the Foam - National Plastic Foam Ban Campaign. Campaign to ban single-use plastic foam foodware nationally. Foam containers ranked 7th most collected item in 2022 coastal cleanups. Advocates for Congressional action to eliminate non-recyclable foam polluting beaches and waste streams.

Western and Central Pacific Ocean Tuna: Handling Sharks and Rays. Evaluating post-release survival of shark/ray bycatch in WCPO tuna fisheries. Tagging 30 specimens, training fishers in handling techniques, analyzing mortality data to develop improved release guidelines for regional application.

South African Hake: Trialling Technologies for Improved Environmental Performance. SA hake trawl fishery trials tech to meet MSC v3.1: recycling nets via micro-pods, electronic monitoring for bird scaring lines, AI video analysis for bycatch. Aims: reduce ghost gear, verify seabird protection, automate species ID.

South Atlantic Albacore Tuna Harvest Strategy Project. Five S Atlantic albacore fisheries develop science-based harvest strategy via MSE framework. Ensures long-term tuna stock sustainability, ICCAT compliance. 24-month roadmap: data analysis, workshops, performance testing.

Mexican North Pacific brown shrimp 2025. Brown shrimp fishery in Baja California improving stock assessment, harvest strategy, trawling impact monitoring, and stakeholder awareness to reach MSC certification by 2027. April 2025 start.

Adapting Management Iberian Sardine Stocks. Ecosystem-based management for Iberian sardine fishery. Assessing predator consumption impact, developing robust harvest control rules. PhD research integrating ecosystem considerations into stock management for Atlantic sustainability.

Improving Sustainability and Management Gulf of California Hake. Gulf of California hake trawl fishery developing robust harvest strategy & control rules for MSC certification by 2026. Aims to be first certified industrial trawl fishery in region, improving stock management & ETP species protection.

Namibia Hake: Targeted Acoustic Startle Technology for Cape Fur Seals. Testing acoustic startle tech to deter Cape fur seals from hake trawls/longlines in Namibia. Uses low-frequency sound triggering brainstem response without hearing damage. Starts April 2025.

Chile Demersal Crustacean Harvest Control Rules. Evaluating management strategies for MSC certified Chilean squat lobster and nylon shrimp fisheries. Developing stock assessment models and testing harvest control rules to prevent overfishing along south-central Chile coast.

Plastic Free Beaches. Global initiative using 35+ years of International Coastal Cleanup data to reduce ocean plastics through banning polluting items, redesigning products, and revamping recycling. Targets 11M metric tons/year entering oceans.

Age-structured production model harvest control rules New Zealand orange roughy 2024. Developing age-structure models & harvest control rules for orange roughy sustainability. Collating 1990s-2010s data on fish age/size to inform catch limits & ensure stock replenishment in Chatham Rise deepwater fishery.

California Market Squid: Improving Understanding of Populations. Study squid hatchlings to assess population dynamics, validate harvest control rules, and monitor ETP species interactions. Digital e-logs improve data collection for sustainable management of this short-lived species.

Tropical Tuna Purse Seine Fisheries Shark Bycatch Project. French tuna fisheries deploy shark enumerators to correct bias in bycatch estimates. Compares observer vs enumerator counts across Indian & Atlantic Oceans to improve IRD protocols & shark conservation.

Indonesia Central Java prawn environmental DNA project. eDNA metabarcoding assesses bycatch species diversity in Central Java prawn fishery. Identifies IUCN status & abundance to develop action plan minimizing ecosystem impacts toward MSC certification by 2026.

Aegean Longline Tuna & Swordfish: Minimising Interactions with Endangered Species. Research to reduce bycatch of endangered species in Aegean Sea longline fisheries. Literature review of mitigation tech, consultation with fishers, testing bycatch reduction devices. Starts April 2025.

Improving Fishery Knowledge Nicaragua Spiny Lobster. Census of Nicaragua Caribbean spiny lobster trap fishery to improve data on fishing effort, catch data for stock assessments, and develop Harvest Control Rules. Targets artisanal fleet in Corn Islands, Bluefields area.

Improvements in practices and governance North Peru eel trap 2024. North Peru eel trap fishery strengthens monitoring via logbooks, improves eel population understanding, develops harvest control rules, and enhances fisheries management to work toward MSC certification by early 2025.

Indonesia Central Java size and genetics project. Research on white prawn size & genetics in Wedung to assess stock health. Collects morphometric data, genetic connectivity samples along fishing routes. Informs sustainable management strategy for prawn fishery.

Continued Research Sustainability of Deep-Sea Shrimp Kerala India. Kerala deep-sea shrimp trawl fishery developing harvest strategy, reducing bycatch via square mesh nets, protecting ETP species in Arabian Sea. Aims for MSC certification 2025. Targets 3 shrimp species for US/EU export.

Reducing sawfish and sea snake bycatch in the Australia Northern Prawn fishery. Study analyzing 2012-2022 bycatch data to identify sawfish interaction patterns by vessel, gear, location & season. Designs mitigation trials testing gear modifications & underwater lights. Evaluates sea snake escape hatches added 2020.

Tagging silky sharks to identify post-release survival rates. Electronic tagging of silky sharks in Eastern Pacific tuna fishery to monitor 60-day survival rates post-release, analyze stress markers, and develop improved handling practices to reduce bycatch mortality in purse seine operations.

Knowledge sharing to reduce dolphin interactions in Australia-UK sardine fisheries. South Australian and Cornish sardine fishery managers share bycatch mitigation strategies through workshops and fishing trips, focusing on marine mammal detection, deterrence, and release techniques in purse seine operations.

Improving brown pelican population estimates Mexico Pacific sardine fishery. Research on brown pelican populations at Isla Todos Santos, Baja California to assess sardine fishery bycatch impacts. Field surveys measure breeding success, survival rates. Modeling analyzes population trends vs environmental/fishing mortality.

Seabird bycatch reduction Greenland lumpfish fishery. Testing LED lights on gillnets and fishing season delays to reduce seabird bycatch in Greenland lumpfish fishery. Focuses on common eider, long-tailed duck protection. Studies migration-spawning overlap. April 2023 start.

Training observers minimising sardine fishery impacts Mexican Pacific biodiversity hotspot. Training onboard observers to monitor bycatch, ETP species interactions in Pacific sardine fishery off Baja California. Data collection informs management strategy to minimize environmental impacts on biodiversity hotspot.

Kerala Deep-Sea Shrimp Trawl Bycatch Reduction Devices. PhD research verifying cod-end mesh devices reduce bycatch & emissions in Kerala shrimp trawl fishery. Testing gear efficacy, documenting biodiversity, measuring fuel savings in Arabian Sea. Supports MSC certification pathway.

Improving data on seabird interactions in Alaskan salmon fishery. Alaska salmon fishery trials SkipperScience app for fishers to record endangered murrelet bycatch, identify hotspots, develop mitigation methods. Indigenous Sentinel Network expansion supports data collection from remote locations.

Predicting Silky Shark Hotspots to Mitigate Bycatch in Papua New Guinea. Statistical model predicts silky shark hotspots in PNG purse seine tuna fishery. Assesses area/time-based management to reduce vulnerable shark bycatch. Replicable approach for other Pacific tuna fisheries. Started April 2023.

Genetic testing to identify octopus species Madagascar. DNA barcoding of 100+ octopus samples from SW Madagascar fishery to identify species composition, enable accurate stock assessments, and improve sustainable management for coastal communities dependent on octopus fishing.

Identifying distinct squid populations in Indonesia. Genetic analysis of Indian squid in Malacca Strait to identify distinct populations, enabling better stock management and harvest strategies for sustainable fishery development in North Sumatra.

Reducing turtle bycatch in Réunion longline swordfish fishery. Training Réunion Island swordfish fishers to identify, handle and release turtle bycatch, especially vulnerable loggerheads. Using environmental data to minimize bycatch. Collaboration with scientists to improve survival rates.

Managing Skate Bycatch Australian Toothfish Fishery. Monitoring sandpaper skate post-release survival in Heard Island toothfish fishery via satellite tagging and blood stress markers to improve bycatch management in southern Indian Ocean.

Improving scientific knowledge Mexico barred sand bass student research 2024. PhD research on barred sand bass stocks in Baja California to create age-structure models, establish stock assessments, and inform harvest strategies for sustainable fishery management and MSC certification by 2026.

Suriname: Smartphone technology to understand ETP species. Corvina/acoupa weakfish trawl fishery uses smartphone app to collect geo-tagged images of endangered species, building database to develop management strategies minimizing bycatch interactions in Western Atlantic waters off Suriname.

Improving management of squid North Sumatra 2023. Research analyzing 100+ squid samples in North Sumatra to understand population dynamics and reproductive capacity, developing sustainable stock management strategies to prevent overfishing of mitre squid (Uroteuthis chinensis).

Monitoring Crab Baits and Ecosystem Effects Mexican Yucatan Octopus Fishery. Monitors octopus catch & crab bait species in Yucatán fishery. Uses genetic testing to prevent endangered species use. Develops sustainable bait strategy. Supports 15,000+ jobs. Started April 2024.

Identifying how environmental factors impact the abundance and distribution of deep-water Cape hake. PhD research analyzing 2003-2019 survey data on Cape hake distribution vs temperature, salinity, oxygen. Compares with monkfish, kingklip. Supports SA-Namibia joint stock management in Benguela region.

Investigating interactions of South African longline fisheries with orcas and Cape fur seals. Student research analyzing 20 years of observer data to quantify orca and seal depredation rates in hake longline fishery, informing management decisions to minimize marine mammal interactions and improve stock assessments.

Mexican Barred Sand Bass Cooperatives Project 2024. Artisanal barred sand bass fishery in Baja California developing harvest strategy, stock assessment, and management framework to achieve MSC certification by 2026. Implements monitoring systems and harvest control rules.

Safeguarding Future India Shrimp and Squid Fisheries. Developing management strategy evaluation framework for Kerala trawl fishery targeting shrimp and cephalopods to achieve MSC certification by 2024, ensuring sustainable stock management.

Further improvements Mexico red rock lobster fishery 2023. Baja California red rock lobster fishery transitioning to MSC certification. Improving stock assessments, harvest protocols, ETP monitoring, habitat impact studies. Strengthening community surveillance and management for 2025 assessment.

Innovative DNA methods to age blue swimming crabs in Indonesia. DNA methylation testing of blue swimming crabs to determine age structure for sustainable stock management in Madura Island fishery. Supports harvest strategy development and MSC assessment progress.

Improving and Promoting Best Practice in Yucatan Octopus Fishery. Helps Yucatan octopus fishery monitor catch data, prevent endangered crab use as bait, and develop sustainable practices. Targets red & common octopus supporting 15,000 jobs. Includes genetic testing and ecosystem impact assessment.

Minimising Fishing Impacts on Indonesian Squid Stocks. Developing fishery management plan for mitre squid in Belawan, Medan. Research spawning areas, harvest strategies to protect stock health. Supporting small-scale fisheries toward MSC certification in Indonesian FMA 571.

Climate models to predict crab survival in Indonesian fisheries. Develops climate model predicting blue swimming crab survival in Indonesian fisheries. Creates color-coded maps identifying climate impacts on crab life stages to inform fishery management decisions and prevent overfishing.

Strengthening Traceability in Kotabaru Shrimp Fishery. Improves data collection and traceability for South Kalimantan white/spot prawn fishery. Installs cameras, tracking devices on vessels, registers hundreds of boats. Enables MSC certification by 2026. Started 2022.

Mapping Risks to Endangered Species North Sea Wash Brown Shrimp Fishery. GIS mapping to assess impacts on endangered species from beam trawl shrimp fishery in North Sea. Literature review & risk assessment to identify ETP species interactions, create mitigation measures for MSC-certified Wash fishery.

Testing Novel Seabird Bycatch Mitigation in Iceland Lumpfish Fisheries. RSPB & ISF test 'looming-eyes buoy' device in Icelandic lumpfish gillnet fishery to reduce seabird bycatch by 25%, protecting endangered species like black guillemots. Trials funded to develop effective mitigation strategy.

Using genetic markers to identify snapper stocks in Makassar Strait. PhD research collecting 350+ tissue samples from malabar blood & goldband snapper in Makassar Strait to identify distinct stocks, enabling sustainable management plans for Indonesian snapper fisheries through genetic analysis.

Investigating Artificial Bait Use in Australian Tuna Fisheries. Research sustainable bait alternatives for Australian Eastern Tuna and Billfish Fishery to replace Argentine shortfin squid. Testing artificial/alternative baits on fishing trips and developing responsible bait sourcing code.

Growing Supply of Sustainable Mexican Red Octopus to Meet Demand. Research to improve Yucatan red octopus stock assessments using CPUE methodology. Addresses TAC enforcement issues where catches exceed limits by 50%. Monthly sampling and fisher surveys to propose better management strategies.

Improving Understanding of Stocks in Mexico Pacific Artisanal Shrimp Fishery. Stock assessment for 3 shrimp species in Southern Gulf of California to ensure sustainable fishing levels, monitor ETP species interactions, and study seabed gear impacts. Aims for MSC certification by 2023.

Making Kerala's Deep-Sea Shrimp Fishing Sustainable. WWF-India supports Kerala deep-sea shrimp fishery toward MSC certification by 2025. Stock assessments, bycatch reduction devices, harvest control rules development. Targets Arabian red shrimp in Kollam Bank using trawl gear.

Boosting Gonad Health Mexico Red Sea Urchins. Evaluating red sea urchin translocation from low to high kelp areas in Baja California to improve gonad quality while monitoring ecosystem impacts. Divers harvest urchins for Asian export markets.

Creating a Fisheries Communication Platform to Enhance Observer Safety. Developing one-touch satellite communication platform for at-sea fisheries observers in Alaska. RockSTAR device with open-source software enables 24hr check-ins, SOS alerts, improving observer safety and data collection quality.

Safeguarding Indonesian Blue Swimming Crab Fisheries. Rebuilding depleted crab stocks in Madura Island fishery through harvest strategy, gear modifications, ghost fishing awareness, ETP species training, and regional management councils. Aims for MSC certification by Dec 2024.

Using DNA to identify bycatch species in Java Sea blue swimming crab fishery. eDNA techniques identify bycatch species in Java Sea crab fishery. Collected 825 crab samples & seawater from 13 points to assess stock status & distribution of vulnerable crustaceans caught in traps, supporting sustainability assessment.

Reducing bycatch of diving birds in Greenland lumpfish gillnets. Quantifying and reducing seabird bycatch in West Greenland lumpfish fishery by testing modified gillnets with white mesh. Modified nets reduced bycatch by ~50% but decreased catch by 21%. Protects common eiders while sustaining livelihoods.

Empowering Indonesian Shrimp Fishers to Improve Practices. Training Central Java banana shrimp fishers in sustainable practices, data collection, habitat protection, and endangered species handling. Builds fisher cooperatives to strengthen community voice and implement improvements toward MSC certification b

WWF South Africa and the South African albacore tuna pole and line fishery. Supporting SA albacore tuna pole-line fishery to meet MSC standards via harvest control rules, observer monitoring, and ETP species protection. Off Cape Town to Namibian border. Aims to ensure sustainable tuna stock management.

Improving the Safety of Fishery Observer Programmes. Global review of fishery observer programmes to ensure safe working conditions. Interviews with observers & industry across Pacific, Indian, Atlantic tuna fisheries. Develops safety guidelines for at-sea monitoring.

Keep Our Oceans Amazing Campaign. Disney contributed $1M to The Nature Conservancy to protect 10 ocean animals and habitats, supporting TNC's goal of protecting 10% of world's oceans by 2030. Linked to Avatar: The Way of Water film.

Disney Conservation Fund Helps Sea Turtle Conservancy Protect Florida's Sea Turtles. Sea Turtle Conservancy protects sea turtles at Archie Carr National Wildlife Refuge, FL through satellite tracking, education via Tour de Turtles, and community engagement to address threats like pollution and lighting.

Tour de Turtles - Sea Turtle Migration Tracking. Annual sea turtle migration tracking at Vero Beach using satellite telemetry. Monitors nesting, studies migration patterns, educates public. 20yr program tracked 1.5M hatchlings, 2000 nests/year.

Wildlife at Lookout Cay. Disney Cruise Line's Bahamas destination protects 100+ bird species, relocated 50 giant barrel sponges, built artificial reefs for 74 fish species, monitors land crabs, preserves 200 plant species via elevated structures on <16% of land.

Disney's Moana 2 Ocean Conservation Campaign. Disney partners with Pristine Seas and Polynesian Voyaging Society to protect oceans. Supports 29 marine protected areas covering 6.8M km² and traditional wayfinding practices. Campaign launched Nov 2024 for Moana 2 film release.

Ocean Oxygen Loss Joint Action. Enhances ocean oxygen measurement, data accessibility & monitoring to address oxygen loss impacts on marine ecosystems. Focuses on biogeochemical observations in vulnerable areas affected by climate change & eutrophication.

Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation. Review report on AMOC state of knowledge, assessing ocean current weakening impacts on ecosystems, climate tipping points, and sea level rise across the Atlantic. Expert synthesis for policymakers.

European Marinas Network. Network of ~10,000 European marinas as ocean monitoring hubs. Installs low-cost sensors measuring temperature, sea state, dissolved gases, phytoplankton, microplastics. Fills coastal data gaps, supports marine management.

JPI Oceans Joint Action on Blue Carbon. Knowledge Hub addressing blue carbon gaps in coastal ecosystems (marshes, mangroves, seagrass). Creates carbon stock maps, data platform, and joint research calls across 7 European countries. May 2023-Apr 2027. Led by Ireland.

Perry Institute for Marine Science - Bahamian Reef Protection. Protecting shrinking Bahamian reefs through study, training, limiting harmful human contact, promoting ecosystem resilience, coral nurseries, and reef rehabilitation in The Caribbean.

Tour de Turtles - Sea Turtle Conservation at Disney's Vero Beach Resort. Disney & Sea Turtle Conservancy track sea turtle migration via satellite, monitor 2,800+ nests yearly along 5-mile beach. Year-round protection of loggerhead, green & leatherback turtles. Vero Beach, FL since 2008.

Ocean Carbon Capacities Knowledge Hub. Multi-country initiative measuring ocean CO2 absorption (25% of emissions). Develops European reference materials hub, enhances vessel observations, evaluates surface CO2 monitoring to improve carbon sink data for policymakers.

Ecological Aspects of Deep-Sea Mining. Assesses long-term impacts of polymetallic nodule mining on deep-sea environment. Three phases (2015-2028) studying seafloor disturbances, monitoring mining robots, informing ISA Mining Code policy with €22.9M funding across 8 countries.

Changing Marine Lightscapes. Studies ocean darkening from runoff & artificial light at night pollution in European seas. Two projects (ISOLUME, ALANIS) investigate impacts on marine ecosystems, biodiversity & fisheries. Pan-European collaboration across 7 countries.

Blue Bioeconomy ERA-NET Cofund (BlueBio). ERA-NET funding 49 projects across Europe to develop sustainable aquatic biomass products, zero-waste fisheries/aquaculture solutions, marine biotechnology, and blue circular economy innovations. Dec 2018-Jun 2026.

Joint Action Underwater Noise in the Marine Environment. Pan-European partnership studying underwater noise impacts on marine life from genes to ecosystems. Five funded projects assess soundscapes, population effects, and cumulative noise impacts across European seas (2019-2026).

Science for Good Environmental Status (S4GES). Knowledge Hub coordinating research to assess Good Environmental Status in European marine waters via MSFD. Uses adaptive sampling, satellites, e-DNA, contaminants analysis. Proof-of-concept in Belgium/Netherlands 2022. Ongoing 2019-2027.

Knowledge Hub on Sea Level Rise. Joint JPI Climate-Oceans effort providing periodic assessments of sea level rise drivers, impacts & policy options for Europe's ocean basins. Phase 1 completed 2024 First Assessment Report; Phase 2 scoping begins 2026.

Offshore Freshened Groundwater. Exploring sub-seafloor freshwater in sediments/rocks near coasts as alternative water source. Interdisciplinary research on technological feasibility, environmental impacts, legal framework. Focus on passive continental margins within 50km of coast.

Transdisciplinary Research for Ocean Sustainability. 13 international consortia funded €14.25M to develop transdisciplinary solutions for sustainable ocean use and climate mitigation under SDG 14, integrating natural/social sciences with stakeholders globally.

Integrated Assessment of New Pollutants. Knowledge Hub network of experts developing methodological improvements for marine chemical status assessment, focusing on chemicals of emerging concern. Published policy paper on integrated assessment approaches.

Intercalibration for Water Framework Directive. Scientific intercalibration exercise for EU WFD bringing experts to analyze phytoplankton and benthic fauna, ensuring comparable ecological status assessments across European coastal/transitional waters. 9 countries jointly funded 2014-2017.

Multi Use of Infrastructure for Monitoring in the North Sea. Pilot testing integrated monitoring for MSFD descriptors during International Bottom Trawl Surveys across North Sea. 7 countries tested additional monitoring during IBTS cruises in 2014, assessing costs and limitations.

European Marine Sensor Calibration Network. Pan-European network establishing calibration standards for marine sensors measuring pH, salinity, fluorescence. Created working group and strategic plan to support marine observatories across Europe.

Climate Science for Oceans. Joint JPI Oceans-JPI Climate action funding research on ocean-climate interactions to improve climate models and inform adaptation policies. Four projects studying mixed layer dynamics, ocean-atmosphere interactions, and coastal impacts.

Cumulative Effects of Human Activities Knowledge Hub. Developed guidelines for assessing cumulative effects of human activities on marine environments. Published 2024 Handbook to help European countries implement Marine Strategy Framework Directive and achieve Good Environmental Status.

Ecological Aspects of Microplastics. Pan-European research studying sources, distribution & impact of microplastics in marine environments. 10 projects across 15 countries analyzing ecotoxicological effects, weathering, nano-particles & reduction concepts. €18.2M funding.

Resilient Protected Areas and Parks. Coastal Quest manages public-private partnerships to strengthen coastal protected areas and parks, supporting 30x30 targets, climate adaptation, and community access through grants and planning along California coast.

MPA Outreach and Education Small Grants Program Round 1. Pilot grants to 14 CA MPA regional collaboratives for outreach, education, enforcement & monitoring. Achieved 48 events, 12 workshops, educational materials. Increased stewardship, compliance & citizen science.

Coastal 30x30 - Protecting and Restoring Coastal Ecosystems. Accelerates coastal nature-based solutions to protect 30% of lands/waters by 2030. Provides grants, technical assistance, webinars for conservation, restoration projects building coastal resilience in vulnerable communities.

Resilient California State Parks San Diego Coast District Pilot. Sea level rise vulnerability assessments and adaptation pathways for San Diego Coast District state parks. Holistic planning for coastal access, recreation, cultural/natural resources through 2050. Community engagement and toolkit development.

Protecting and Restoring Coastal Ecosystems. Global blue carbon initiative protecting/restoring coastal ecosystems for climate solutions. Convenes dialogues, provides technical assistance/funding, builds partnerships with Ocean Protection Council in California.

Munition in the Sea Knowledge Hub. Multi-national expert group assessing risks from legacy underwater munitions across Europe. Shared practices, technologies, expertise on mapping, remediation, and environmental impacts. Launched information portal in 2024.

MPA Outreach and Education Small Grants Program. Statewide CA program funding $25k-$100k grants to increase MPA compliance, ocean stewardship, and engagement. Targets fishing communities, underserved groups, and tribes through education and outreach since 2017.

Blue Carbon Collaborative. International community advancing blue carbon initiatives through policy integration, partnerships, research, and coastal ecosystem conservation. Focuses on carbon capture in coastal plants/algae for climate mitigation and adaptation.

MarTERA - ERA-NET Cofund on Marine Technologies. EU-funded ERA-NET coordinating 16 countries to develop marine technologies through 4 transnational calls (2017-2022). Funded 48 projects totaling €69.5M for maritime innovation, monitoring, offshore activities, and Blue Growth.

Piloting Tools to Assess State Water Quality Protection Areas. Coastal Quest partners with CA Water Resources Control Board to pilot GIS tool assessing Central Coast areas for State Water Quality Protection Area nominations, strengthening water quality enforcement since 2022.

SWQPA Assessment Tool. ArcGIS database mapping California coastal resources across 6 categories: infrastructure, managed areas, species, habitats, water quality, renewable energy. Tool helps assess State Water Quality Protection Areas.

Fish Forever in Mozambique. Combating overfishing along Mozambique's 1,500-mile coastline through community-led fisheries management. Small-scale fishers protect biodiversity and restore declining fish stocks using sustainable techniques.

Fish Forever in Brazil. Sustainable fisheries management in Brazil's northern/northeastern coastal states. Addresses unsustainable fishing, habitat degradation in mangrove forests. Supports small-scale fishers' livelihoods and food security.

From Bomber to Protector: A Story of Change in North Sulawesi Indonesia. Rare partners with North Sulawesi fishers to end destructive fishing, establish no-take zones, and restore reefs. Former destructive fisher Sofian Gondang now champions Managed Access program, rebuilding livelihoods.

Fish Forever in the Mesoamerican Reef. Community-based fisheries management across 600 miles of Mesoamerican Reef (Mexico-Honduras). Addresses overfishing through local governance, supporting 2M+ people dependent on reef health for livelihoods and food security.

Fish Forever in Indonesia. Addresses unsustainable fishing, poor governance, habitat degradation in Indonesian coastal fisheries. Partners with 1,700 communities, 160,000 fishers, local governments to ensure sustainable fisheries and food security.

Fish Forever in Palau and the Federated States of Micronesia. Community-led coastal fisheries management in Palau & FSM to combat overfishing, protect biodiversity, ensure food security. Partners with 1,700 communities, 160,000 fishers. Target: 50% marine resources managed by 2030.

Coastal 500. Global network of 500+ mayors/local leaders across 8 countries committed to thriving coastal communities through sustainable fisheries management, promoting responsible fishing, advocating fishers' rights. Finalist 2023 Earthshot Prize.

UN Decade of Ocean Science for Sustainable Development. IOC-UNESCO coordinates global ocean science cooperation across 152 nations through capacity development, observations, tsunami warnings, and literacy programs. Leads UN Ocean Decade 2021-2030 for sustainable ocean management.

Where Land Meets Sea: Building Climate Resilience with Honduras's Coastal Fishers and Farmers. Rare links sustainable fishing with regenerative agriculture in Trujillo and Santa Fe, Honduras. Empowers fisher-farmers to restore mangroves, reduce runoff, protect coral reefs, and build climate resilience through community-led conservation.

Local Fishers on Buton Island Turn Everyday Ice Needs into Coastal Resilience. Fishers in Dongkala Village operate ice-making business to reduce post-harvest loss & fund marine surveillance. Launched Feb 2026 in Pasarwajo Bay, profits support PAAP Ngapatoowa fisheries management & conservation.

Expanding Community-Led Conservation in Honduras. Rare partnered with Honduran communities to place 14,000+ sq km of Mesoamerican Reef waters under sustainable management, addressing fishery decline and building community-led ocean conservation movement along Caribbean coast.

30x30 Campaign - Fish Forever Community-Led Marine Conservation. Rare's Fish Forever program advances 30x30 goals through community-led co-management of territorial seas (12 nautical miles from shore). Uses Managed Access with Reserves (MA+R) combining fishing rights with no-take zones.
