Ban Butts from Our Beaches, Monroe County. Ban cigarette smoking on Monroe County beaches/parks to reduce plastic pollution and cigarette litter harming marine life. Ordinance passed Aug 2022 with Surfrider support, effective countywide.

Ban Butts from Our Beaches, St. Pete. Ban cigarette smoking on St. Petersburg's beaches, parks, and piers to reduce plastic pollution and prevent toxic cigarette butt litter from harming Gulf Coast marine life and waterways.

Ban Butts from Our Beaches, Miami Beach. Ban cigarette smoking on Miami Beach beaches and parks to reduce plastic pollution and prevent cigarette litter from harming marine life. Ordinance passed Sept 2022, effective 2023.

Congress Increases NOAA's Budget for 2023. Surfrider campaign secured increased 2023 federal funding for NOAA coastal programs including $81.5M for Coastal Zone Management, $68M for Marine Sanctuaries, $80M for Sea Grant, protecting coasts from climate change and pollution.

Protected Maritime Forest at McLean-Spell Park. Prevented development of 30-acre maritime forest in Emerald Isle, NC. Forest protects homes from hurricanes, aids stormwater absorption & erosion prevention. Town abandoned dog park plan, will maintain trails instead.

Solana Beach Balloon Ban. Ban on sale, use & release of lighter-than-air balloons to protect marine life from plastic pollution. Surfrider San Diego volunteers campaigned Mar-May 2022, City Council unanimously approved ordinance in Solana Beach, CA.

Laguna Beach Balloon Ban. Ban on retail sales, release and use of mylar and latex balloons in Laguna Beach to prevent beach litter and protect marine life from plastic pollution. Ordinance enacted Feb 2023, first in Orange County.

Protect Our Mangroves, Miami!. Campaign to prevent Miami from banning mangrove planting in waterfront parks. Mangroves protect coasts from flooding, erosion, sea level rise. Victory: ordinance withdrawn May 31, 2022 after advocacy.

Reduce Cigarette Butt Litter in Encinitas. Ban smoking in public spaces to reduce toxic plastic cigarette filter pollution. Butts are #1 littered item, 20-30% of beach cleanup finds. Ordinance approved April 2023 in Encinitas, CA coastal city.

Litigation to Defend Denial of Exxon Oil Trucking Plan. Surfrider defended Santa Barbara County's denial of Exxon's oil trucking plan to transport crude from offshore rigs. Victory achieved Feb 2024 when Exxon dismissed lawsuit, protecting coastal waters from spill risks.

Stop Kīkīaola Ditch Pollution. Lawsuit settlement requiring water quality testing, cleanup of wastewater/asphalt plant pollution, and NPDES permits for Kīkīaola ditch discharging sediment and pesticides into Kekaha Beach waters, protecting coral reefs and fishing grounds.

Urge Congress to Invest in Ocean-Based Climate Solutions. Advocacy campaign resulting in $3B+ for coastal restoration, blue carbon ecosystems, and climate resilience through the Inflation Reduction Act. Includes grants for states/tribes and NOAA facilities.

Strengthen Florida Keys National Marine Sanctuary. Surfrider supports NOAA's Restoration Blueprint for Florida Keys National Marine Sanctuary, advocating for expanded boundaries, cruise ship discharge bans, water quality improvements, and climate protections for coral reefs and marine habitat.

Protect Access to Cherry Point. Campaign to repeal Gulf Rd closure ordinance and maintain public viewing access to Cherry Point beach for water recreationists, community science, and mobility-limited visitors in Whatcom County.

Fund Enforcement of the Coastal Act!. Secured $5M in CA 2022-23 budget for Coastal Act enforcement to resolve 3,000 violations including illegal wetland destruction, habitat loss, blocked public access. Supports CA Coastal Commission enforcement personnel.

California Seabed Mining Prevention Act. Law banning seabed mining in CA waters to protect marine habitats, fisheries, wildlife. Prevents hard mineral extraction leases. Signed Sept 2023 by Gov. Newsom after unanimous bipartisan passage.

Papahānaumokuākea National Marine Sanctuary. Marine sanctuary designation in Northwestern Hawaiian Islands adds protections to existing monument. Co-managed by NOAA, State of Hawaii, Office of Hawaiian Affairs. Effective March 2025.

Stop Shrimp Farm Water Pollution. Surfrider Kauai secured stronger water permit for shrimp farm eliminating 6,000ft mixing zone, imposing end-of-pipe pollutant limits to protect nearshore waters from fish kills and pollution flowing to Pacific Ocean. Victory Dec 2024.

Limit the Use of Emergency Shoreline Hardening Permits for Chronic Erosion. Hawaii DLNR updated 2023 policy to stop emergency permits for seawalls/sandbags causing beach loss. Enforces removal of expired structures. Protects public beaches from chronic erosion hardening (230+ exemptions in 20 years).

Save the Waves at Bob Hall Pier in Corpus Christi, TX. Secured two-piling pier design for Bob Hall Pier after Hurricane Hanna damage to preserve quality sandbars and surfing waves. Texas Coastal Bend Chapter advocated for design that maintains wave formation at this premiere Gulf Coast surf spot.

Save Public Access at Keawakapu. Protecting free public beach parking at Keawakapu Beach, Maui. County took over state land management in 2022 after private operator harassment issues. Community advocating for permanent county control of half-acre lot.

Balloons and Lanterns Blow, Broward!. Broward County Chapter campaign to ban balloon/lantern releases and regulate single-use plastics on county property. Prevents wildlife deaths from ingestion. Victory: lanterns, confetti banned Feb 2023.

Plastics Ordinance Passed in Lauderhill. Lauderhill, FL banned single-use plastics by city vendors and balloon releases to protect marine wildlife. Ordinance passed unanimously 5-0 on Jan 10, 2022 to reduce beach pollution and microplastics.

Hillsborough County Fertilizer Ordinance. Fertilizer ban to prevent runoff fueling red tide, fish kills, and seagrass loss in Tampa Bay. Passed 7-0 by County Commissioners on November 17th 2021 after 11-year advocacy effort.

Party Ocean-Friendly Campaign - Palm Beach Gardens Resolution 69. Surfrider supported Resolution 69 prohibiting balloons, confetti, glitter on public property to protect wildlife and marine environment. Passed 4-1 Dec 2021. Promotes eco-friendly alternatives like native plants, flower petals.

Comprehensive Solution Selected to Stop Border Sewage. EPA selected Alternative I-2 to address Tijuana River transboundary sewage pollution affecting San Diego beaches. River diversion system for US treatment aims to reduce pollution 95% in summer, 76% overall. Needs $625M funding.

Protect Beach Access in Scarborough. Campaign opposing parking fee increases at Scarborough beaches to maintain equitable public access. Advocates against raising rates from $5 to $10 for reduced hours and $1 to $2/hr for metered spots.

Encinitas Balloon Ban. Campaign to ban sale, use, and release of lighter-than-air balloons in Encinitas, CA. Surfrider SD activists supported effort from environmental commission through unanimous City Council approval. Model ordinance for other cities.

Victory! Increase funding for Oʻahu Natural Resources. Honolulu passed Bill 40 allocating 0.25% of County TAT (3% hotel tax) to natural resources, providing $7M/year for beach/park conservation, visitor impact mitigation, and coastal resilience on Oʻahu. Passed Dec 14, 2021.

City of St. Augustine Beach Balloon Ordinance. Surfrider First Coast Chapter successfully campaigned for St. Augustine Beach to ban intentional balloon releases to protect marine wildlife from balloon litter pollution along Florida's coast.

Atlantic Beach Polystyrene Ordinance. Ban on polystyrene foam sale/distribution on Atlantic Beach city property and beach. Passed Dec 2021 to reduce plastic pollution, protect marine life, and prevent microplastics from entering ocean ecosystems.

Plan For Sea Level Rise and Resiliency, Florida. Establish statewide Office of Resilience, develop flood vulnerability & sea level rise data, create state resilience action plan for Florida roadways. Victory: CS/SB7053 signed May 2022.

Protect Dunes in Miami Beach. Surfrider Miami Chapter restores dunes, removes invasive plants since 2014. Advocated for 2021 ordinance protecting coastal dune system from unauthorized activities threatening integrity, health and habitat in Miami Beach.

St. Johns County Balloon and Lantern Release Ordinance. First Coast Surfrider led coalition to ban balloon/lantern releases in St. Johns County, FL (first in state). Protects marine life from ingesting balloon litter mistaken for jellyfish. Passed unanimously Jan 2022 after petition campaign.

SB 474 - Sea Level Rise Disclosure. Hawaii law requiring sellers to disclose if properties are in sea level rise exposure areas (3.2ft by 2050). Protects homebuyers from climate risks and limits harmful seawalls. Passed June 6, 2021.

Fund the California Coastal Commission!. Advocacy campaign to secure $40M funding for CA Coastal Commission's sea level rise unit and Whale Tail grants. Protects beaches from erosion, ensures coastal access, oversees local coastal programs. Signed July 2021.

Pass a Comprehensive Foodware Ordinance in Newport, OR. Newport, OR banned single-use plastic/foam foodware to reduce ocean pollution. Plastic utensils are top 10 coastal cleanup items. Ordinance 2178 passed Dec 6, 2021 restricting EPS foam and plastic foodware.

Banned the Sale of Balloons in East Hampton, NY. Eastern Long Island Chapter banned helium balloon sales in East Hampton to prevent beach/ocean litter, wildlife harm, and power outages. Passed unanimously Dec 2021 after advocacy with local trustee and 30+ organizations.

Ban Balloon Releases in City of St. Augustine. Surfrider First Coast Chapter successfully campaigned to ban intentional balloon releases in St. Augustine to protect marine wildlife from balloon litter. City commissioners approved the ban on August 9th.

Strengthened Delaware's Bag Law. Delaware Chapter helped pass HB-212 in 2021, closing plastic bag thickness loopholes and expanding store coverage. Worked with Plastic Free Delaware through testimony and advocacy to strengthen weak existing bag law.

Reducing Plastic Pollution in Delaware. 3-year campaign by Surfrider Delaware Chapter to ban EPS foam foodware and plastic stirrers/straws. Senate Bill 51 passed June 2023, signed Aug 2023. Reduces common beach cleanup items harming marine life.

Protect Humboldt Bay from Fish Factory Impacts. Campaign opposing Nordic Aquafarms' massive land-based salmon factory on Samoa Peninsula. Project would intake 10M gallons/day from Humboldt Bay and discharge 12M gallons to Pacific, requiring full Environmental Impact Report.

Surfing, other wave-riding exempted from MI water entry prohibition. Surfrider testimony influenced Michigan DNR to amend water entry prohibition during hazardous conditions, exempting surfing, skimboarding, and bodyboarding, preserving wave-riding access at state parks.

Oxnard EPS Foam Ban. Oxnard City Council unanimously banned expanded polystyrene (EPS/Styrofoam) to protect marine life, oceans, and beaches. Ordinance prohibits use, manufacturing, distribution of single-use EPS foodware. Effective Feb 16, 2023.

Polystyrene Foam, Balloon and Confetti Ordinance in Boca Raton. Boca Raton banned foam, balloons & confetti at beachside parks to protect sea turtles & marine wildlife from dangerous litter. Ordinance passed June 8th by city commission to remove these items from city property.

Keep National Parks Free From Fees in San Francisco and Marin. Successfully opposed NPS parking fees at 7 Bay Area beaches (Baker, Lands End, Rodeo, Stinson etc). Generated 379+ comments. Protects equitable coastal access for all, especially low-income visitors. Completed 2021.

HB 243 - Sea Level Rise Adaptation. Hawaii law requiring state agencies to identify facilities vulnerable to sea level rise, assess mitigation options, coordinate adaptation efforts, and report annually. Signed July 7, 2021 to protect beaches and coastal communities.

Support Senate Bill 1 (Atkins) - Address Sea Level Rise. California law addressing sea level rise through planning, physical adaptations, and governance structures to protect coastal ecosystems and communities. Signed Sept 2021 to address $150B property risk.

NOAA's Coastal Management Budget Increased for 2022. Surfrider campaign secured increased 2022 federal funding for NOAA coastal programs including zone management, resilience, estuarine reserves, and Sea Grant through grassroots advocacy and 125 Congressional visits.

Supported construction of the South Fork Wind Project. Surfrider's Eastern Long Island Chapter supported South Fork Wind offshore wind project after environmental review, advocating for BOEM approval with high environmental and recreational protections. Project completed.

Puerto Rico Foam Ordinance. Law 51 bans expanded polystyrene foam food containers (cups, plates, clamshells) throughout Puerto Rico to reduce marine plastic pollution from single-use foam products entering coastal waters and beaches.

Ban Balloon and Sky Lantern Releases in Tequesta. Surfrider Treasure Coast Chapter campaigns to ban intentional balloon and sky lantern releases in Tequesta to protect marine wildlife from ingestion and entanglement hazards in this coastal Florida community.

Stop Sewage Spills at the Beach. Campaign to stop 850B+ gallons annual raw sewage spills into US waterways via wastewater infrastructure upgrades. Secured $27.35B EPA CWSRF funding through 2021 Infrastructure Act. Nationwide coastal protection effort.

City of Boynton Beach Polystyrene Ordinance. Ban polystyrene foam food-ware on Boynton Beach city property to reduce plastic pollution. Polystyrene is a major beach litter source. Ordinance passed April 20th by city commission.

City of Boynton Beach Balloon and Confetti Ordinance. Prohibits balloons and plastic confetti at beachside parks and city property to protect sea turtles and marine wildlife from ingesting dangerous litter. Passed by city commission April 20th.

Smoke Free Beaches and Parks, Florida!. Campaign to allow Florida counties/municipalities to regulate smoking on beaches/parks. Addresses cigarette butt pollution (most abundant coastal debris). HB 105 signed June 2022, enabling local smoke-free ordinances statewide.

Banned EPS Foam Food Containers in Virginia. Virginia banned EPS foam food containers by 2025. Surfrider VA advocated for HB1902, signed March 2021, protecting marine life from non-recyclable foam pollution that leaches toxins and harms coastal ecosystems.

Atlantic Beach Coal Ash Resolution. Campaign to stop coal ash shipments through Jacksonville Ports after 2021 barge spill released thousands of tons into ocean near Mayport surf break. Resolution 21-82 passed Dec 2021 banning coal ash receipt at Atlantic Beach ports.

LA County Foodware Accessories Upon Request - Skip The Stuff!. Campaign to reduce plastic pollution by requiring LA County restaurants and delivery services to ask customers before providing single-use takeout accessories like utensils, napkins, and condiments rather than automatically including them.

Banned the Intentional Release of Balloons in Delaware. Surfrider Delaware Chapter passed Bill SB24 banning intentional balloon releases to protect marine life from choking/entanglement. Signed Sept 20, 2021 by Gov. Carney with Plastic Free Delaware.

Laguna Beach Plastic Foodware Ordinance. Ordinance banning plastic straws, cutlery, disposable foodware & takeout bags at restaurants citywide. Includes EPS foam ban at beaches/parks. Passed June 2021 to reduce ocean plastic pollution in Laguna Beach, CA.

City of LA Foodware Accessories Upon Request - Skip the Stuff!. LA ordinance requiring single-use utensils, straws, condiments, napkins only upon request from food vendors. Reduces waste polluting waterways. Passed April 2021, signed May 2021 by Mayor Garcetti.

Florida Sea Level Rise Rule-making. Surfrider worked with coalition to ensure Florida institutes robust regulations requiring sea level rise analysis for state-funded coastal construction projects, effective July 2022.

Keep Del Mar Rail Relocation on Track. Surfrider advocated to relocate 1.7 miles of railroad off Del Mar's eroding bluffs and prevent rail agencies from bypassing California Coastal Act review, protecting beach access and coastal environment (2020-2024).

Re-open Public Beach Parking in Bal Harbour. Restore 60 public parking spaces at Bal Harbour Jetty, a prime surfing location in Miami Dade. Activists coordinated with local officials to restore public beach access for surfing and swimming. Successfully restored Sept 2020.

Save Biscayne Bay. Campaign to protect Biscayne Bay after 2020 fishkill. Organized meetings, rallies to address pollution and dumping. Secured $20M funding from state and county for bay restoration and protection.

City of Miami Beach Fertilizer Ordinance. Surfrider Miami advocated for fertilizer restrictions to reduce nutrient pollution in Biscayne Bay. Successful campaign led to unanimous ordinance passage in Jan 2021 to regulate fertilizer use and prevent algal blooms.

Federal Board Ruling Ensures Coastal Railroad Projects Must Adhere to the Coastal Act. Federal Surface Transportation Board denied NCTD's exemption from environmental review for Del Mar railroad bluff stabilization, protecting coastal regulations and supporting rail relocation by 2035.

Water Notice Sign at South Pointe Outfall. Miami Chapter detected elevated enterococcus levels at South Pointe Park outfall through weekly testing in 2020. City installed permanent warning sign advising against swimming/recreation after activists presented findings.

City of Sunny Isles Beach Polystyrene Ordinance in Public Parks, Offices and Beaches. Ban polystyrene foam food-ware on Sunny Isles Beach city property. Addresses major beach litter source found in cleanups. Ordinance passed March 18th prohibiting foam on all municipal property including beaches and parks.

Funding for New Wastewater System Technology to Reduce Cost of Cesspool Conversion. Hawaii project to eliminate 83,000 cesspools discharging 52M gallons/day sewage into coastal waters. UH pilot program tests affordable wastewater tech; DOH staffing for conversion support. Goal: cesspool elimination by 2050.

Restore Public Beach Access at Koʻolina. Restored public parking and beach access to Ko'olina Lagoons after resort blocked 180 public parking spots citing COVID. City violation notice issued Oct 2020, full access restored Feb 2021 through community advocacy.

Protect Coral Reefs in the City of Key West by Limiting Cruise Ships. Limit cruise ships to 1,500 passengers/day in Key West to protect coral reefs from sediment damage that blocks light and kills marine life. Ballot measure passed Nov 2020, reducing cruise visits 95%.

Ban Seabed Mining in Washington. Washington passed SB 5145 prohibiting seabed mining in state waters to protect marine ecosystems, fisheries, and coastal communities from destructive mining practices. Signed into law May 3rd, 2021 by Governor Inslee.

Regulate Fertilizer Use in Miami Dade County. Surfrider Miami advocates for fertilizer restrictions to reduce nutrient flow into Biscayne Bay, preventing algal blooms and fishkills. County passed ordinance April 20th to protect the bay.

Protect Wāwāmalu Sand Dunes. Coalition stopped illegal off-roading at Wāwāmalu Beach, Oʻahu by installing barriers in 2021. Protects Hawaiian Monk Seal habitat, native plants, and sensitive sand dune ecosystems at Kaiwi State Scenic Shoreline.

Protect Oregon's Seafloor. Strengthen policies protecting Oregon's seafloor and beaches from undersea cable impacts. Advocates for environmental standards, financial assurance, and planning for telecommunication projects after abandoned cable left equipment.

Solana Beach Seawall Denied. California Coastal Commission denied seawall application for Pacific Avenue gap in Solana Beach to prevent beach narrowing and protect public access. Property owners attempted to bypass deed restrictions through neighboring applications.

Orange County Beach Access. Surfrider urged Orange County to develop COVID-19 beach access plan for 42 miles of coast, balancing public health with active recreation (surfing, swimming, walking). Advocating equitable coastal access.

Court Victory for Beach Access Rights in California Lent Case. Surfrider defended CA Coastal Commission's $4.2M fine against Malibu homeowner blocking public beach access for 9 years. CA Supreme Court denied appeal July 2021, setting precedent for beach access enforcement.

Sharp Park Beach Saved From Hazardous Development. Pacifica beach protected from 7-unit condo development relying on seawall. California Coastal Commission denied project 6-5, preventing beach loss from armoring. Surfrider argued against loophole allowing new development on hazardous coastal sites.

Defend the Federal Clean Water Act. Surfrider won Supreme Court case stopping Lahaina Wastewater Facility from discharging 3-5M gallons daily of treated sewage into Pacific via groundwater, devastating reef at Kahekili Beach, Maui since 2012.

A Portion of Pleasure Point Saved From Never Ending Seawalls. Surfrider Santa Cruz appealed permit for 8,200 sq ft blufftop house at Opal Cliffs relying on illegal seawalls. CA Coastal Commission denied development in May 2023, preventing beach erosion and creating path to coastal resiliency.

City of Neptune Beach Balloon Ordinance. Surfrider First Coast advocates for Neptune Beach to ban intentional balloon releases to protect marine wildlife from balloon litter. Promotes alternatives like tree planting and beach cleanups.

Remove Fencing from Pacific City Beach. Surfrider campaign to remove unpermitted fencing installed by homeowners on Pacific City beach that violated Oregon's Beach Bill public easement. Victory achieved May 2020 when all property owners removed fencing.

Help Designate the Chumash Heritage National Marine Sanctuary. Advocacy to designate 140-mile sanctuary from Cambria to Santa Barbara. First sanctuary focused on indigenous culture and ocean habitat protection. Nominated 2015, remains in inventory until 2025.

Save the Avila Coast. Campaign opposing luxury resort overdevelopment at Avila Beach, CA. Protects coastal access, sacred Chumash sites, and marine recreation from traffic/crowds. Reduced resort from 5,000 to 3,000 capacity after advocacy.

Santa Barbara Oil Trucking Proposal STOPPED!. Stopped Exxon's proposal to truck oil from offshore platforms, preventing risk to coastal economy & marine ecosystems. Coalition effort protected Santa Barbara's beaches from potential spills after 2015 Refugio disaster.

BEACH Act Funding Saved for FY2021. Surfrider Foundation led campaign to save EPA BEACH Grant Program funding for coastal states' beach water quality monitoring and public notification programs, preventing elimination proposed in 2021 federal budget.

Increased Water Quality Testing in Ft. Lauderdale, FL. After 125M+ gallons sewage spilled 2019-2020, Surfrider Broward advocated for expanded water testing at recreation sites. City allocated $100K in Nov 2020 for testing 10 sites in coastal waters and rivers.

Halt the Shoreline Armoring at Puʻuloa Rifle Range. Surfrider Oʻahu demanded EIS for 1,500ft barrier at ʻEwa Beach firing range. Navy relocated berms inland in 2023 after community pressure. Concerns: coral reefs, erosion, lead contamination from bullets eroding into ocean.

Oppose Shoreline Armoring at Breakers Point. Prevented sheet pile wall installation at Ecola Creek Estuary, Cannon Beach OR. Protected essential salmon habitat from accelerated sediment transport and beach erosion. Victory achieved May 2020.

Allow Ocean Recreation Access When & Where It's Safe. COVID-19 beach access advocacy in NH. Surfrider successfully campaigned to reopen seacoast beaches June 1, 2020 for all ocean recreation (not just walking/swimming), while ensuring safety protocols and equitable parking access.

Follow Mass Beach Reopening Guidelines in COVID-19. Advocated for clear public noticing of beach access rules during COVID-19 reopening. Worked with MA DCR to ensure consistent parking and amenity information across state beaches, particularly Nahant Beach, achieving updated guidance June 2020.

Stop Plastic Bag Pollution in Virginia. Coalition passed VA legislation allowing local governments to tax single-use plastic bags up to 5 cents, protecting Chesapeake Bay waterways and beaches from common pollution. Effective Jan 1, 2021.

EPA requires Hawaii to account for plastic pollution under Clean Water Act. EPA ordered Hawaii DOH to evaluate plastic pollution data for state waters. Lawsuit by Surfrider, CBD, and Sustainable Coastlines Hawaii challenged EPA's failure to declare waters impaired under Clean Water Act section 303(d).

City of Hollywood Single Use Plastic and Polystyrene Ordinance in Public Parks, Offices and Beaches. Ban polystyrene foam food-ware & single use plastics on Hollywood city property. Ordinance passed Feb 2020 to reduce plastic pollution found in beach cleanups. Applies to city offices, buildings, events.

Improve the Hawaii Department of Health's beach monitoring program. Campaign to enhance Hawaii beach water quality testing. Achieved 2024 victory: HDOH now continues testing popular Tier 1 beaches during Brown Water Advisories, improving public health protection through better monitoring.

Stop the Flood of Takeout Food Plastics in NYC!. NYC law requiring food delivery apps & restaurants to let customers opt-in for single-use plastics (utensils, napkins). Reduces plastic pollution flowing from streets to waterways & ocean. Passed Jan 2023.

Ban the Foam on Kauai. Kauai banned polystyrene foam food containers in 2020 to prevent marine pollution. Foam breaks into pieces, harms wildlife, persists indefinitely. Ban effective Jan 1, 2022, making Hawaii 5th foam-free US state.

Pass Foodware and Single-use Beverage Ordinance for the City of Arcata. Surfrider Humboldt advocates for Arcata ordinance banning single-use plastic foodware and beverage containers at city facilities to reduce 10M metric tons annual ocean plastic pollution through source reduction.

Ban Single-Use Plastic Foodware on Maui. Maui County banned single-use plastic foodware (containers, cups, straws, utensils) effective Jan 1, 2022. Businesses must use paper or compostable alternatives, reducing ocean plastic pollution and fossil fuel dependence.

Foam Free Washington. Washington state legislation (SB5022) bans expanded polystyrene products, mandates recycled content in plastics, requires opt-in for single-use items. Bipartisan support. Tackles plastic pollution in coastal waters.

Say NO to Offshore Oil Drilling in Virginia Waters. Ban oil drilling in Virginia state waters (3 miles from shore). Surfrider Virginia Chapter worked with coalition to pass SB795 and HB706, protecting tourism, recreation jobs, and marine wildlife. Effective July 1, 2020.

City of Atlantic Beach Balloon Ordinance. Surfrider First Coast Chapter campaigns for Atlantic Beach to ban intentional balloon releases to protect marine wildlife from balloon litter. Promotes alternatives like tree planting and beach cleanups.

Oregon Ocean Climate Action. Advancing Oregon legislation for ocean climate science, adaptation & mitigation. Secured $2M for Ocean Science Trust (HB 3114, 2021) to address ocean acidification, hypoxia & evaluate marine reserves along Oregon coast.

Help Ban Polystyrene in SLO County. Campaign to ban polystyrene in San Luis Obispo County to reduce plastic pollution entering waterways and coastlines. Targets microplastics harming marine life. Urges support for ordinance No. 2019-1.

Support the CT Blue Plan!. Connecticut's Long Island Sound Blue Plan protects ecosystems and traditional uses through science-based ocean management. Identifies Ecologically Significant Areas and Human Use Areas. Unanimously approved 2021.

NOAA's Budget Saved for 2021. Surfrider campaign defended NOAA from proposed budget cuts targeting coastal zone management, resilience, estuarine reserves & Sea Grant. Grassroots advocacy & 125 Congressional visits secured 2021 funding.

Ban Single-Use Plastic and EPS Foam Products in LA County. LA County ordinance banning EPS foam and single-use plastics in foodware to reduce waterway/beach pollution. Requires compostable/recyclable items and reusables at restaurants. Protects marine wildlife from plastic debris.

Long Beach Plastics Reduction Ordinance. Long Beach banned retail EPS foam & plastic straws in Feb 2020 to reduce ocean plastic pollution. Surfrider Long Beach advocated 10+ years after witnessing plastic at beach cleanups. Builds on existing restaurant foam ban.

Stopping Intentional Balloon Releases in Maryland. Surfrider's Ocean City Chapter passed MD bills HB391/S716 banning intentional balloon releases. Balloons end up in oceans, choking marine life like turtles and whales. Law effective Oct 1, 2021.

Banned Intentional Balloon Releases in Virginia. Surfrider VA worked with partners to ban intentional balloon releases statewide, closing loophole allowing <50 balloons. Prevents marine debris harming ocean wildlife. Governor signed HB 2159 into law March 30, 2021.

Made Straws By Request Only in NYC. NYC legislation requiring bars/restaurants to provide plastic straws only upon request. Addresses top beach cleanup pollutant that harms marine wildlife and enters food chain through waterways.

Mickler Beach Beach Access. Campaign to keep Mickler Beach in St. Johns County open to public. In Nov 2019, beach was closed for geo-thermal tube installation by homeowners. First Coast activists rallied and successfully kept beach open.

Help California Address Nonfloating Oil Spills Before It's Too Late!. Campaign urging CA Senate to pass AB 936 establishing contingency plans for non-floating oil spills that sink below water. Bill requires response orgs, research funding, transport notices, and raises liability caps to $10B.

Save Santa Cruz Beaches and Waves from Sea Level Rise. Surfrider opposes Santa Cruz County's coastal program allowing seawalls for new development at Pleasure Point/Opal Cliffs. Advocates managed retreat, living shorelines over armoring that drowns beaches as seas rise.

Redondo Beach Plastics Reduction Ordinance. Surfrider South Bay advocated for ordinance banning polystyrene food ware, plastic straws/utensils, and balloon releases in Redondo Beach. Passed Jan 2020 to reduce top plastic pollution sources entering ocean.

Trestles and San Onofre Saved from Road Construction. 15-year campaign to protect San Onofre State Beach and Trestles from toll road construction. Coalition of activists prevented damage to watershed, surf break, endangered species, and Indigenous sites. Secured permanent protection via AB 1426.

Carlsbad Plastic Foodware Reduction Ordinance. Carlsbad banned single-use plastic foodware & polystyrene from restaurants (July 2023). Includes 'Skip the Stuff' requiring utensils/straws only on request. Protects ocean from plastic pollution in San Diego County.

Ormond Beach Plastic Straw Ordinance. Surfrider's Volusia/Flagler Chapter worked with Ormond Beach, FL to pass a single-use plastic straw ordinance in Sept 2019, eliminating straws to reduce fossil fuel use and marine plastic pollution.

Pass the Coronado Plastics Reduction. Surfrider San Diego supported Emerald Keepers to pass comprehensive plastic ordinance in Coronado, restricting single-use plastics, foam, bags, balloons, water bottles. Adopted 2024 after 6-month advocacy campaign.

Say NO to polystyrene, Norwalk!. Connecticut Chapter worked with residents to ban single-use polystyrene food service wares in Norwalk. Ordinance passed Sept 2019, effective Earth Day 2020, prohibiting foam containers and packaging peanuts.

Redondo Beach Outdoor Smoking Ban. Citywide smoking ban in public places approved Sept 2019 to reduce cigarette butt litter in beach areas and ocean. Butts contain plastic filters with toxins that wash into waterways. Surfrider volunteers advocated at council meetings.

City of Key West Single Use Plastic Straw Ordinance. Key West passed ordinance banning single-use plastic straws to prevent marine pollution. Surfrider Florida Keys Chapter advocated summer 2019, city voted September 4, 2019.

Make Intentional Releases of Balloons Illegal in the Town of Hempstead, NY. Surfrider's Central Long Island Chapter worked with coalition partners to pass a law banning intentional balloon releases in Hempstead, NY to prevent ocean litter and protect coastal wildlife. Passed Nov 2019.

Protect ʻAliomanu Beach Access. Restored public beach access at ʻAliomanu South, Kauai. Community fought blockage of 50-year traditional path used for beach cleanups, fishing, limu gathering, and ancient Ala Loa Trail. Access secured Oct 2023.

Say NO to Straws, Norwalk!. Norwalk, CT passed straw mitigation ordinance Sept 2019. Ask-first policy for straws, ban on plastic stirrers. Youth-led advocacy after coastal cleanup. Addresses plastic pollution and climate crisis connection.

Satellite Beach Single Use Plastic and Polystyrene Measures. Ban polystyrene foam & single-use plastics at Satellite Beach city facilities & events. Passed July 17th resolution to stop foam/plastic use at city parks, venues, permitted events, reducing beach litter found in cleanups.

Gaviota State Beach Pier approved to rebuild without shoreline armoring. Pier reconstruction at Gaviota State Park approved without 1700-ton riprap seawall. Metal grated design protects Kashayit Marine Conservation Area habitat and beach access. Surfrider Foundation advocacy changed Coastal Commission recommendation.

Stopped the Williams Transco Pipeline -- Round 2!. Blocked NESE fossil fuel pipeline from crossing NY-NJ Harbor to Rockaway Beach. Protected benthic communities, sturgeon, whales from construction impacts and reduced greenhouse gas emissions. Coalition advocacy led to permit denials in May 2020.

Bill 40 Passes on Oahu, One of the Strongest Plastic Laws in the Nation. Surfrider's Oahu Chapter passed Bill 40 banning single-use plastics island-wide. Phases out plastic bags, polystyrene, containers, straws & utensils over 2 years. Approved Dec 2019, affects 72% of Hawaii's population.

Solana Beach Plastics Reduction. Comprehensive ordinance banning single-use plastics, polystyrene foam, plastic straws/utensils at food establishments and city facilities in Solana Beach. Passed unanimously Sept 2019, phased implementation May-Nov 2020.

Pacific Grove Says No to Single-Use. Pacific Grove, CA banned single-use plastics including straws, to-go containers, bags, and toiletries. Requires BPI certified compostable alternatives and 100% recycled paper bags. Strongest ordinance in region.

Ban Intentional Balloon Releases in Suffolk County. Ban intentional balloon releases in Suffolk County, NY to protect marine life from balloon debris found at beach cleanups. Passed Sept 2019 after public hearings. Prevents marine wildlife ingestion and entanglement.

Save North Strands Beach. Campaign to deny 1,200+ft rock revetment protecting private homes at Strands Beach, Dana Point. Opposed shoreline armoring threatening public beach access. Successfully blocked Feb 2020 at CA Coastal Commission.

Wilton Manors Single Use Straw Ordinance. Ordinance eliminating single-use plastic straws in Wilton Manors, FL to reduce fossil fuel use and prevent plastic litter in marine environments. Passed October 14, 2019 after advocacy by Surfrider chapters.

North Myrtle Beach, SC Bans Plastic Bags. North Myrtle Beach banned retail plastic carryout bags including bioplastics to reduce ocean pollution. Ordinance passed April 2019 protecting coastal waters and marine life from plastic waste.

Florida Sunscreen Preemption. Campaign to stop Florida bills preempting local bans on reef-damaging sunscreen chemicals oxybenzone and octinoxate. Key West passed local ban; Surfrider activists defeated state preemption bills May 2019.

City of West Palm Beach Plastic Straw Ordinance. Ordinance passed March 2019 to ban single-use plastic straws in West Palm Beach, reducing fossil fuel use and preventing plastic pollution in marine environments through local policy advocacy.

Imperial Beach Plastics Reduction Ordinance. Ordinance bans plastic straws, stirrers, utensils and polystyrene products in Imperial Beach restaurants/retailers. Surfrider San Diego volunteers advocated at council meetings. Effective Nov 2019.

Banning the Intentional Release of Balloons in Long Branch, NJ. Surfrider activists worked with Long Branch, NJ to pass ordinance banning intentional balloon releases in April 2019, protecting Atlantic Coast from plastic pollution at this major boardwalk destination with hundreds of thousands of visitors.

NOAA Funding Saved for 2020. Surfrider campaign defended NOAA from Trump admin budget cuts targeting coastal zone management, resilience, estuarine reserves & Sea Grant. Congress passed FY2019 budget with level/increased funding for ocean & coastal programs.

Manhattan Beach Balloon Release Ban. Manhattan Beach banned balloon releases and distribution on public property to prevent marine plastic pollution. Surfrider volunteers advocated at city council meetings, resulting in stricter ordinance passed March 2019.

Help Us Ban Foam in Maryland. Statewide ban on expanded polystyrene (EPS) food containers in Maryland to reduce marine litter and toxin exposure. Law passed May 2019, effective July 2020. Led by Ocean City Chapter and Trash Free Maryland coalition.

Hollywood Balloon Release Ban. Surfrider Broward County Chapter successfully campaigned for Hollywood, FL to ban intentional balloon releases to protect marine life and endangered ocean species from balloon litter and ingestion deaths. Ordinance passed Feb 2020.

Ban single-use foam food containers, Maine!. Campaign to ban polystyrene foam food packaging statewide in Maine. After multiple attempts, LD289 passed in 2019, making Maine first US state to ban foam containers. Effective Jan 1, 2021. Prevents ocean pollution from non-recyclable foam.

Manhattan Beach Polystyrene Tray Ban. Ban on polystyrene meat trays passed March 2019 to eliminate EPS foam pollution in Manhattan Beach. Targets hard-to-collect beach cleanup items that break into small pieces. Surfrider volunteers advocated at council meetings.

City of Stuart Single Use Plastic and Polystyrene Ordinance in Public Parks, Offices and Beaches. Ban on polystyrene foam food-ware and single use plastics in Stuart city beaches and parks. Passed Oct 28 to reduce plastic pollution found in beach cleanups, diverting tons of waste from landfills.

Banning Foam in Suffolk County, NY. Suffolk County polystyrene foam food container ban led by Surfrider's Eastern Long Island Chapter. Law prohibits foam to-go containers and packaging peanuts, effective Jan 1, 2020. Signed Earth Day 2019.

Surfrider Hawaii Helps Pass 4th Cesspool Bill. Hawaii law extends Cesspool Conversion Working Group funding to address 88,000 cesspools leaching 53M gallons daily of sewage. Coalition secured Act 170 to extend deadline to 2022 for conversion plan by 2050.

Protect Sawyer's Beach in Rye, NH!. Surfrider NH defeated porta-potty placement at Sawyer's Beach to prevent pollution from human waste, chemicals entering eel pond and ocean. Town vote passed 1209-404 in March 2019, permanently banning porta-potties at this location.

Prohibit Drilling Activity in New Hampshire State Waters. Law prohibiting offshore oil/gas drilling in NH state waters and related infrastructure. Passed unanimously through legislature, signed Sept 2019 at Rye Harbor State Park, protecting coastal waters from drilling.

San Clemente Foam Ban Defended. Surfrider's South Orange County chapter successfully defended San Clemente's 2004 EPS foam foodware ban from being weakened, preventing thousands of foam pieces from littering coastal beaches through advocacy and testimony.

Straw Ban in Suffolk County, NY. Suffolk County plastic straw ban led by Surfrider's Eastern Long Island Chapter. Law prohibits single-use plastic straws, requires paper/biodegradable alternatives by request only. Exceptions for disabilities. Effective Jan 1, 2020.

City of Stuart Single Use Plastic Straw Ordinance. Ordinance passed Oct 2019 banning single-use plastic straws in Stuart city limits to prevent marine pollution. Complements existing beach property ordinances, reducing fossil fuel use and plastic litter in marine environments.

ReWild Mission Bay Wetland Restoration. Wetland restoration in Mission Bay to improve water quality, sequester carbon, buffer storms/sea level rise. Study planning options for restoring <1% remaining historic wetlands. Coalition led effort.

Florida Plastic Straw Preemption. Surfrider activists opposed 2019 FL bills preempting local plastic straw ordinances. Through emails, opeds, phone banks, they defeated initial bills. Governor DeSantis vetoed HB 771 moratorium, preserving local control.

Village of Pinecrest Polystyrene Ordinance. Ban on polystyrene foam foodware in Pinecrest to reduce beach litter. Approved Jan 8, effective Apr 1, 2019. Led by Surfrider Miami Chapter to eliminate major pollution source found in beach cleanups.

Del Mar Plastic Straw and Stirrer Ban. Ban on plastic straws/stirrers in Del Mar, CA. Surfrider San Diego volunteers advocated at city council, raised awareness. Ordinance passed March 2019, effective April 2019 with 6-month grace period. Ocean Friendly Restaurants program aids implementa

Bellingham Polystyrene Ordinance. Ban on polystyrene takeout containers & single-use plastics in Bellingham, WA. Ordinance passed May 2021, effective July 2022. Led by Surfrider chapters with local partners to reduce plastic pollution entering marine waters.

Lauderdale by the Sea Plastic Straw Ordinance. Surfrider Broward Chapter advocated for single-use plastic straw ban in Lauderdale by the Sea to prevent marine pollution. Town unanimously passed ordinance Feb 2019, reducing fossil fuel use and ocean litter.

Protect Dunes Beach from development. Opposing 200-room hotel & 170-site RV park at Dunes Beach, Half Moon Bay. Threatens 50-acres pristine habitat, agriculture, recreation, coastal views. Urging City Council denial due to sea level rise risk.

Washington Reusable Bag Act. Statewide legislation eliminating single-use plastic bags in Washington, effective Jan 2021. Retailers charge 8¢ for paper/reusable bags. Addresses 2B bags used yearly, <6% recycled, harming marine life in Salish Sea.

No Porta-Potty at Sawyer's Beach!. Surfrider NH opposed porta-potty at Sawyer's Beach, Rye due to pollution risks from waste/chemicals near eel pond and ocean. Board voted to remove funding 1/14/19. Article 35 seeks permanent ban at March 2019 election.

Protecting Florida Keys Coral Reefs by Banning Oxybenzone. Key West banned oxybenzone and octinoxate sunscreen chemicals to protect coral reefs. These chemicals cause genetic damage, disease susceptibility, and bleaching in corals. First Florida city ban, Feb 2019.

Expand Paddleboard and Surfing Zone at Hollywood Beach. Surfrider's Broward Chapter advocates to remove stand up paddle restrictions at Hollywood Beach, FL. Currently illegal on most of beach. Campaign promotes water recreation, eco-tourism access to cafes/businesses.

Washington Oil Spill Prevention. Preventing oil spills in Puget Sound and Washington coast through advocacy for tug escort requirements for smaller oil tankers near San Juan Islands, protecting salmon, orcas, and local economies.

Prohibit Drilling Activity in Maine State Waters. LD955 law prohibits oil/gas exploration in Maine waters. Protects coastal communities from spills, pollution. Safeguards tourism, fishing, beaches. Signed June 2019 by Governor Mills after legislative victory.

Ft. Lauderdale Straw Ordinance. Surfrider's Broward Chapter successfully campaigned for a single-use plastic straw ordinance in Ft. Lauderdale to prevent plastic pollution in marine environments. Passed January 22, 2019.

Let's Reduce Foam on California Beaches. Campaign to ban expanded polystyrene (EPS/Styrofoam) food packaging at California state parks and beaches. SB 1335 signed requiring reusable, compostable, or recyclable food service packaging to reduce ocean pollution.

Deerfield Beach Straw Ordinance. Surfrider Broward Chapter successfully passed ordinance banning single-use plastic straws in Deerfield Beach to prevent marine pollution and reduce fossil fuel dependency. Ordinance passed Sept 2018.

Protect Our Coasts from Harmful Algal Blooms. Advocacy campaign to reauthorize federal harmful algal bloom research & prevention program after expiration in 2018. Victory: Congress passed reauthorization Dec 2018, signed into law Jan 2019.

Solana Beach Geologic Setback Line Upheld. Surfrider's San Diego Chapter successfully defended blufftop setback policies, preventing bluff-edge development that would require future shoreline armoring and threaten public beach access as sea levels rise.

Ban Foam in Southampton Town. Ban expanded polystyrene foam in Southampton Town, Long Island to protect marine life from petroleum-based plastic pollution. Law passed Feb 2019, effective May 2019, prohibits foam food containers, packaging, coolers.

Ban Straws in Southampton Town. Surfrider Eastern Long Island worked with Southampton Town to ban plastic straws. 164 straws removed from beaches. Ban passed Feb 2019, effective May 2019. Restaurants provide straws only on request, non-plastic materials.

Melbourne Beach Single Use Plastic and Polystyrene Ordinance in Public Parks, Offices and Beaches. Ban polystyrene foam foodware & single-use plastics in Melbourne Beach parks & beaches. Addresses major litter source found in cleanups. Works within FL state law limiting bans to municipal property only.

Isle of Palms, SC Expands Single-Use Plastics Ban. Isle of Palms City Council expanded plastic bag ban to include straws, stirrers, and foam containers at food/grocery establishments. Passed March 26 to reduce marine litter from single-use plastics.

Hallandale Beach Plastic Straw Ordinance. Surfrider Broward Chapter successfully passed ordinance banning single-use plastic straws in Hallandale Beach to reduce marine plastic pollution and fossil fuel use. Enforced Jan 1, 2019.

Darien Ditching Single-Use Plastic Bags!. Surfrider CT helped pass Darien ordinance banning single-use plastic bags and adding paper bag fee. Reduces pollution, saves taxpayer cleanup costs, incentivizes reusables. Passed June 2019, effective Jan 2020-2021.

Monterey Plastics Ordinance. Coalition effort to ban single-use plastics in Monterey, CA. Passed Dec 2018, effective Earth Day 2019. Bans plastic straws, requires recyclable/compostable containers, prohibits disposable dine-in ware.

Banning Intentional Balloon Releases in East Hampton, NY. Ban on intentional balloon releases in East Hampton, NY to protect beaches and marine life. 774 balloons found in cleanups 2017-2018. Law passed Feb 7, 2019 prohibiting balloon releases town-wide.

Illegal Seawall Ordered Removed, Owners Fined $1 Million. Surfrider supported CA Coastal Commission order to remove illegal seawall at Victoria Beach, Laguna Beach. Owners rebuilt home without permits, losing seawall rights. Removal protects beach from erosion and sea level rise.

Straws Upon Request in California. California law AB 1884 requires full-service restaurants to provide plastic straws only upon request. Prevents straws from reaching ocean via storm drains, protecting marine life like sea turtles from ingestion harm.

Miami Beach Straw Ban Expansion. Surfrider Miami Chapter successfully expanded Miami Beach's 2012 beach straw ban to all city beaches, parks, docks, marinas, boat ramps. Includes plastic stirrers. Adopted July 25th to reduce ocean plastic pollution.

Addressing Microplastic Pollution in California. California legislation (SB 1422 & SB 1263) requires testing microplastics in drinking water and developing a statewide strategy to understand risks and solutions for microplastic pollution in marine environments.

Ban Plastic Bags in Stone Harbor, NJ. South Jersey Chapter advocates for plastic bag ban in Stone Harbor. Members educate Borough Council on marine pollution. Town passes local ordinance before state law takes effect, protecting coastal waters from plastic waste.

Bag Legislation in Asbury Park, NJ. Jersey Shore Chapter advocated for plastic bag ban in Asbury Park using beach cleanup data. City Council passed legislation banning single-use plastic bags with paper bag fees, effective January 1, 2020.

Hueneme Beach Saved from Incompatible Toxic Sediment. Prevented 30,000 cubic yards of potentially toxic, fine-grained Port of Hueneme dredged sediment from being deposited on Hueneme Beach. Would have caused poor water quality, steep beach profile, harming recreation and surf quality.

No Straws for Portland, Maine. Campaign to ban single-use plastic straws, stirrers & splash sticks in Portland, Maine. Advocacy led to unanimous city council passage in Oct 2019, with ban effective Jan 2021 to reduce ocean plastic pollution.

Stamford Steps it up to Reduce Single-Use Bags!. Stamford, CT banned single-use plastic bags & added 10¢ fee on paper bags (Oct 2018, effective Apr 2019). Reduces pollution, saves cleanup costs, incentivizes reusables. Surfrider CT Chapter supported advocacy.

St. Petersburg Straw Ordinance. Surfrider's Suncoast Chapter advocated for eliminating single-use plastic straws in St. Petersburg, FL to reduce fossil fuel use and marine litter. Ordinance passed Dec 14, 2014 by Mayor and Commissioners.

NO on California AB 2921!. Surfrider successfully opposed AB 2921, an industry-led voluntary polystyrene recycling program, advocating instead for policies that ban harmful foam and limit single-use plastic pollution at the source in California.

Santa Monica Plastics Reduction. Santa Monica banned single-use plastics (straws, utensils, containers) for prepared foods in Aug 2018. Surfrider LA rallied support at City Council. Ordinance effective Jan 2019, supports zero waste goal by 2030.

Block Offshore Oil Drilling in New York Waters. Ban oil drilling in NY state waters and pipelines from federal waters. Protects jobs, economy dependent on clean beaches. Law signed April 29, 2019 by Gov. Cuomo after campaign by Surfrider chapters and partners.

Bag Legislation in Avalon, NJ. South Jersey Chapter worked with Avalon, NJ to pass local ordinance banning single-use plastic bags, styrofoam, and plastic straws. Legislation introduced July 2018 after activists began advocacy in June.

Bag Legislation in Somers Point, NJ. South Jersey Chapter urged Somers Point to pass plastic bag ordinance. City passed 5 cent fee on plastic bags in June 2018, with fees going to merchants rather than state, to reduce plastic pollution.

Del Mar Expanded Polystyrene Foam Ban. Ban on EPS foam foodware in Del Mar restaurants, city facilities & events. Surfrider San Diego advocated & provides educational outreach. Ordinance passed Dec 2018, effective June 2019.

Ventura EPS Foam Ban. Surfrider Ventura's Plastic Free Ventura campaign launched Earth Day 2018 to reduce single-use plastic litter from beach cleanups. Ventura City Council banned EPS foam foodware at restaurants/stores Nov 2020.

Kahala Beach Access Preserved!. Surfrider Oahu opposed Kahala Resort's permit for commercial activities on public shoreline. BLNR declined permit renewal Sept 14, preserving public beach access in front of resort in Honolulu.

Ban Intentional Balloon Releases In Southampton Town, NY. Southampton Town banned intentional balloon releases in June 2019. Balloons threaten marine life and cause power outages. Eastern Long Island Chapter shared beach cleanup data with local government.

Ban Foam in East Hampton, NY. Eastern Long Island Chapter campaign to ban expanded polystyrene foam in East Hampton food establishments. Beach cleanup data from 2017-2018 supported ordinance passed Jan 2019, effective Earth Day 2019.

Surfrider Asked to Join Hawaii Cesspool Working Group. Surfrider joined Hawaii's Cesspool Working Group to develop plan converting 88,000 cesspools releasing 53M gallons/day untreated sewage into groundwater. Working Group creates conversion plan by 2050, reports due 2019-2020.

Prevent Oil and Gas Drilling In Oregon's Ocean. Oregon banned oil/gas drilling in state waters (0-3mi) via SB 256 signed March 2019. Blocks infrastructure for offshore drilling. Protects coast tourism, recreation, fishing industries along Oregon coast.

Support New Public Access to Miami Beach. Secured 15-foot public beach access pathway in Miami Beach condo development. Working with developers on dune restoration with native plants. Ensures community beach access and lifeguard safety coverage.

Ban oil and gas exploration in Florida's state waters!. Amendment 9 prohibits oil/gas drilling in FL state waters (shoreline to 3 miles offshore). Approved Nov 2018 with 69% voter support after Surfrider advocacy through Constitution Revision Commission process.

Remove Trash Cans From Shinnecock Inlet Beach. Eastern Long Island Chapter removed overflowing trash cans at Shinnecock Inlet beach that attracted seagulls and illegal dumping, causing more plastic pollution than they prevented. Completed Jan 2018.

San Diego Plastics Reduction. Ban on polystyrene containers & single-use plastics at San Diego restaurants/retailers to stop ocean plastic pollution. Includes straws/utensils on request only, foam cooler/beach toy ban. Adopted Jan 2019, effective Feb 2019.

Stop Obstruction of Miami Beach Public Waterways. Surfrider Miami Chapter fought private security blocking public access to Miami Marine Stadium Park for kayaking/paddleboarding. Victory: City acknowledged overreach, issued memo clarifying public access rights.

Parking Restrictions at Surfrider Beach in Malibu. Defeated Malibu's 2-4am parking restrictions at Surfrider Beach/Malibu Pier. California Coastal Commission denied permit, preserving 24/7 coastal access for swimming, surfing, stargazing. Protects public beach rights under Coastal Act.

Surfside Beach, SC Plastic Bag Ban. Surfside Beach banned single-use plastic bags in 2018. Businesses must provide reusable or recycled paper bags. Ban effective June 1, 2018, covering all businesses and town events to reduce ocean plastic pollution.

City of Malibu Plastic Straw and Utensils Ban. Malibu banned plastic straws & utensils at restaurants in Feb 2018, effective June 1. Surfrider LA Chapter advocated for this ordinance to reduce plastic pollution found at beach cleanups that harms marine wildlife.

Defend Access to the Miami Marine Stadium Lagoon. Successfully opposed 49-vessel mooring field at Virginia Key that threatened mangroves, dolphins, marine species & public access for rowing, swimming, paddleboarding. City Commission dropped plan after protests.

Manhattan Beach Plastic Pollution Reduction Ordinance. Manhattan Beach banned single-use plastic straws, utensils, stirrers & polystyrene items at food/retail locations. Ordinance adopted June 2018, enforced Jan 2019. Part of city's 4th plastic reduction measure since 2008.

New Beach Access for Miami Beach. Miami Chapter partnered with developers to add public beach access at 5775 Collins Avenue. Supported proposal through letters and testimony at Miami Beach Design Review Board. Approved December 5th, 2017.

Stop the LNG Terminal in Coos Bay. Surfrider Coos Bay Chapter opposed Jordan Cove LNG export facility threatening 400+ waterways and critical estuarine habitat in Coos Bay, Oregon. Project defeated December 2021 after decade-long campaign.

Ban the Bag, Greenwich!. Greenwich, CT banned single-use plastic bags in March 2018. Local citizens and Surfrider Connecticut Chapter campaigned for the ordinance, which passed 141-54 and took effect September 2018 to reduce plastic waste.

Ban Balloon Releases in Asbury Park, NJ. Jersey Shore Chapter successfully banned intentional balloon releases in Asbury Park, NJ to prevent marine debris. Ordinance passed Sept 2018 after advocacy work alongside plastic bag legislation.

Ban Balloon Releases in Long Beach Township, NJ. Surfrider Jersey Shore Chapter campaign to ban intentional balloon releases in Long Beach Township, NJ. Balloons pollute beaches daily. Ordinance passed June 5, 2017 with $500 fine for violators.

State Agencies Must Consider Environmental Harms Before Approving Use of State Lands. Surfrider Kaua'i won landmark ruling requiring environmental review before pesticide operations on state lands 400ft from ocean. Protects West Kaua'i coastline from chemical runoff, drift impacts to beaches, cultural sites.

Banning Balloon Releases in North Wildwood, NJ. South Jersey Chapter campaign to ban intentional balloon releases in North Wildwood, Cape May County. Latex/Mylar balloons and plastic ribbons threaten marine environment. First such ordinance in county.

Stop New Fossil Fuel Development in the Tacoma Tideflats. Coalition campaign to maintain moratorium on new fossil fuel facilities in Tacoma Tideflats. City Council passed interim regulations Nov 2017 blocking development until sub-area plan finalized, protecting Commencement Bay waters.

Beach Access Victory at Kahala Beach. Surfrider's Oahu Chapter successfully opposed Kahala Hotel's easement request that would have limited public beach access on Honolulu's South Shore, protecting community rights to pristine shoreline.

Plan Calls for Managed Retreat and Restoration of Ocean Beach. Restoring Ocean Beach SF through managed retreat & beach nourishment. Removes hard armoring exacerbating erosion south of Sloat Blvd. LUP amendment approved May 2018 after 3 decades of advocacy for wider beach access.

Say NO to a ban on plastic bag bans in Rhode Island!. Campaign to defeat H5946 bill that would ban local plastic bag bans in RI. Surfrider RI Chapter & partners successfully opposed plastics industry attempt to rescind municipal ordinances & protect local rights to address plastic pollution.

Trump Administration Withdraws Southeast Waters from Offshore Drilling. 10-year moratorium on offshore drilling in FL, GA, SC, NC waters. Surfrider advocates for permanent congressional ban to protect marine ecosystems and coastal economies from oil/gas development and seismic blasting.

Protect New England Coral Canyons and Seamounts Marine National Monument. Campaign to restore protections for Northeast Canyons and Seamounts Marine National Monument. Biden restored protections Oct 2021, prohibiting commercial fishing to protect unique underwater ecosystems, coral canyons, seamounts in New England.

Banning Intentional Balloon Release in Bradley Beach, NJ. Jersey Shore Chapter successfully advocated for Bradley Beach ordinance 2017-26 banning intentional balloon releases to protect marine environment. $500 fine for violations. Passed October 10, 2017.

Phasing Out Atlantic Salmon Net Pens in Washington. Washington banned open-water Atlantic salmon aquaculture in Salish Sea after net pen collapse released invasive fish. Protects wild Pacific salmon, improves water quality, preserves public trust waters and wave resources.

Save the Wave at Surfside Jetty!. Surfrider advocated for Alternative 1 in Navy's Seal Beach Ammunition Pier reconstruction to protect Surfside Jetty surf break. Navy selected this alternative, preserving the regionally-significant wave spot from destruction.

Marine Sanctuaries Protected from Potential Oil and Gas Development. Surfrider Foundation defended CA marine sanctuaries from oil/gas development. Generated 100k comments opposing Trump admin review. Biden terminated review Jan 2021, protecting Channel Islands, Monterey Bay, Cordell Bank, Farallones.

Stop Bad Beach Access Bill. Campaign to stop HB 735 blocking local governments from protecting public beach access via customary use ordinances in Florida. Bill threatened Walton County's beach access protections. Successfully defeated in 2017.

Protected Public Coastal Recreational Access in MI. Legal campaign supporting broad interpretation of Michigan's Recreation Land Use Act in Otto v. Inn at Watervale case, enabling private landowners to allow public beach and water access for recreation.

Prevent dumping of Humboldt Bay dredge spoils on Samoa Beach. Surfrider opposed City of Eureka & Harbor District's plan to dump 200,000 cubic yards of dredge spoils on Samoa Beach, impeding public access. EPA rejected the plan in 2017 - Victory!

St. Augustine Beach Single Use Plastics Ordinance. Campaign to ban plastic straws, bags, and styrofoam in St. Augustine Beach to prevent marine pollution. Ordinance passed July 1, 2019, making it one of first Northeast Florida cities to eliminate single-use plastics.

Clean Border Water Now Lawsuit Settlement. Surfrider's Clean Water Act lawsuit settlement addresses decades-long pollution at US-Mexico border. Aims to reduce 75% of contaminated flows, cut beach closures 95% in summer via infrastructure improvements and monitoring.

Save Capistrano Beach. Replace emergency armoring with nature-based adaptation at Capistrano Beach. North Reach pilot approved Nov 2022. South Reach has 7-year riprap permit. Goal: expand nature-based solutions coastwide.

Coral Gables Bag Ban. First Florida city to ban single-use plastic bags in May 2017. Addresses marine litter, clogged drains, recycling damage. Surfrider Miami Chapter collaborated with city and businesses to pass ordinance.

Support federal Save Our Seas Act to address plastic pollution. Federal legislation funding NOAA Marine Debris Program for single-use plastics & fishing gear removal, authorizing $10M/year through 2022. Enables severe marine debris event declarations for cleanup after tsunamis & weather events.

Dana Point Outdoor Smoking Ban. Ordinance prohibiting smoking in all public places in Dana Point to reduce cigarette butt litter in urban and beach areas, preventing plastic filters and toxins from entering waterways and ocean.

Mount Pleasant, SC Bans Single Use Plastic Bags, Containers. Surfrider Charleston eliminated single-use plastic bags & polystyrene foam in Mount Pleasant, SC to protect coastal waters from plastic pollution. Achieved April 2018 through town collaboration.

Stopped SC Bill that would Preempt Local Government from Regulating Bags, Containers. Defeated H 3529 in SC General Assembly to preserve local authority to regulate bags, containers & packaging that pollute waterways. Charleston & Grand Strand Chapters led opposition, postponing bill in 2017.

California Ocean Litter Strategy Adopted. CA Ocean Protection Council adopted 2018 Ocean Litter Prevention Strategy to guide 6 years of litter reduction along CA coast, focusing on land-based sources, microplastics, and beach cleanup data coordination.

No Balloon Releases in Ventnor, NJ. Surfrider South Jersey Chapter secured unanimous ban on balloon releases in Ventnor, NJ (Feb 2017) to protect marine animals and birds from entanglement/ingestion. Activists presented ordinance at town meetings.

Mallows Bay-Potomac River National Marine Sanctuary. Surfrider DC & Ocean City chapters helped approve first National Marine Sanctuary in 20 years, 40 miles south of DC. Protects shipwrecks, cultural heritage. Designated by NOAA 2019 for conservation, education, tourism.

No Balloon Releases in Atlantic City, NJ. Atlantic City banned balloon releases in Feb 2017 to prevent marine litter. Balloons entangle wildlife and are ingested by marine animals. Surfrider South Jersey chapter advocated for ordinance across coastal towns.

No Pay to Play Ordinance in York!. Surfrider Maine stopped York's 2016 fee proposal for paddlecraft access to York River. Advocated free public access, first-come policy vs $86 commercial fees. Board scrapped ordinance, will gather data before future proposals.

California Legislature Establishes Fund, Authorizes Funding, for Martins Beach Easement. CA legislature authorized $1M fund to acquire public access easement to Martins Beach. State Lands Commission can allocate funds from Land Bank Fund subaccount to restore permanent coastal access.

Fund Florida Water Quality Monitoring. Restore funding for Florida Healthy Beaches Program to monitor coastal water quality for fecal bacteria. State cuts in 2011 reduced testing frequency. Victory in 2019 with $500k restoration. Protects beachgoers from contamination.

Enforce Hollywood Beach Single-Use Plastic Ordinance. Campaign to enforce existing ordinance banning single-use plastics east of Intracoastal Waterway in Hollywood Beach, FL. Protects sea turtles, manatees, dolphins from plastic pollution. Victory: enforcement began Oct 2018.

Stop Venoco Offshore Oil Drilling Expansion. Campaign to stop Venoco's proposed expansion of Platform Holly oil drilling in California state waters off Goleta. Successfully ended when Venoco quitclaimed leases in April 2018, leading to platform decommissioning.

Banning Balloons in Longport, NJ. South Jersey Chapter campaign to ban balloon releases in Longport, NJ using Margate's model ordinance. Activists worked with Borough Council to protect marine life from balloon pollution. Ordinance passed in 2016.

Laguna Beach Smoking Ban. Expanded smoking ban passed May 2017 in Laguna Beach, CA to reduce cigarette litter. Covers beaches, parks, sidewalks, bike paths citywide. Cigarette butts are 1 in 5 items in beach cleanups.

Bag Legislation in Ventnor, NJ. South Jersey Chapter campaign for single-use bag ordinance in Ventnor, NJ. Conducted cleanups, merchant education from 2015-2018. Resulted in 5-cent fee on paper and plastic bags passed February 2018.

Protected the Atlantic from Offshore Oil Drilling. Permanent withdrawal of Atlantic & Arctic waters from oil/gas drilling announced Dec 2016. Grassroots campaign with 120+ local resolutions, 1000+ business signatures protected critical coastal habitats & economies from drilling risks.

Maui Foam Ban. Ban polystyrene foam food containers on Maui. Coalition worked with County Council, Ocean Friendly Restaurants program. Polystyrene is top 10 littered item, <1% recycled. Maui first in Hawaii to pass ban.

Big Island Foam Ban. Surfrider's Hilo & Kona Chapters led coalition to ban EPS foam food containers on Big Island. 7000+ petition signatures, Ocean Friendly Restaurants support. Bill 13 passed Sept 20, part of effort to make Hawaii first foam-free state.

Hawaii Dept. of Health Improves Public Notification of Water Quality Issues. Surfrider collaborated with Hawaii DOH to improve water quality public notification. Created website with data, maps, and updates for chronically polluted sites. Started 2016, launched after 1.5 years of stakeholder meetings.

Hawaii Passes Ban on all Cesspools and Extends Tax Credit for Replacements. Ban on new cesspools in Hawaii to protect groundwater and ocean from 55M gallons daily raw sewage. Gov. Ige signed rule changes Mar 2016. Tax credits support upgrades to septic systems near water sources.

Care For The Cove. Ensuring US Army Corps of Engineers follows 1998 settlement for sand replenishment at Half Moon Bay, Westport WA. Addresses erosion, safety concerns, and beach recreation impacts from jetty/groin construction since 2013.

Protecting Our Coral Reefs & Banning Oxybenzone. Hawaii banned sunscreens with oxybenzone & octinoxate to protect coral reefs from toxic chemicals causing DNA damage, bleaching & deformities. Surfrider Hawaii advocated since 2016. Law effective Jan 1, 2021 statewide.

Stopped the NY/NJ Williams Gas Pipeline. Stopped 23.4-mile fracked gas pipeline across Raritan Bay from Old Bridge NJ to Rockaway Point NY. Opposed due to impacts on water quality, marine habitat, and coastal recreation. Permits denied 2019.

Keep South Beach Safe. Resolve conflict between jet ski use and surfers at South Beach, Del Norte County through enforcement of CA laws protecting bathers from motorized watercraft within 200 feet of beach.

Ban the Bag, Boston!. Boston campaign to ban single-use plastic bags under 3ml and charge $0.05 for other bags. Passed unanimously 12-0 by City Council 11/29/17, signed into law by Mayor Walsh to reduce ocean plastic pollution.

Public Access Victory in Malibu - First Civil Penalty from California Coastal Commission. CA Coastal Commission fined property owner $4.185M for blocking public beach access in Malibu for 9 years. First use of civil penalty authority. Supreme Court upheld ruling in 2021, setting precedent for access enforcement.

Butts off Miami Beach. Installing 200 cigarette butt receptacles throughout Miami Beach to reduce beach litter. Partnership between Surfrider Miami Chapter and City of Miami Beach, funded by $10k city grant. Monitoring effectiveness since 2019.

Culver City Polystyrene Foodware Ban. Ban on polystyrene foam & rigid plastic foodware at restaurants to reduce Santa Monica Bay pollution. Adopted May 2017, effective Nov 2017. Prevents wildlife consumption of non-biodegradable plastic pieces.

Require Access Equity at Mavericks Surf Contest. Campaign demanding gender equity at Mavericks surf contest per CA Coastal Act Section 30210. Advocates for multi-heat women's division, equal pay, and access equity beyond physical barriers at Half Moon Bay.

Cherry Point Aquatic Reserve Expansion. Expanded Puget Sound reserve by 45 acres, protecting herring/eelgrass habitat vital to salmon. Prevented coal terminal development. Surfrider organized cleanups and advocacy. Lummi treaty rights cited. DNR management plan now protects site.

Malibu Expanded Polystyrene Ban. Surfrider advocated for Malibu to expand its EPS foam ban, prohibiting sale/use of foam food service ware, coolers, packing materials, and maritime products. Adopted November, creating one of strongest US EPS policies.

Keep Beaches Protected in Puerto Rico. Defeated Senate Bill 1621 to prevent legalization of private development encroachment on public beaches in southern Puerto Rico, protecting public beach access and coastal resources through petition and advocacy.

California Coastal National Monument Expansion Act. Congressional bill to designate 6,200 acres in Humboldt, Santa Cruz, and San Luis Obispo Counties under California Coastal National Monument, protecting coastal lands with historical, cultural, scientific, ecological value.

Kauai Chapter helps end polluted discharge along West Kauai. Surfrider sued Hawaii's ADC for Clean Water Act violations. Court ruled ADC must obtain permits, limit pollution from 40 miles of drainage ditches discharging pesticide-laden sediment into West Kauai waters at Polihale, Kekaha beaches.

Ban More Foam in San Francisco. Expanded SF's polystyrene ban to prohibit sale of foam food service ware, packing materials, beach toys, and marine equipment not encapsulated. Strictest US foam ordinance protecting ocean from plastic pollution.

Protect NC Public Trust Rights to Beach Access. Defended NC's public trust doctrine ensuring dry-sand beach access in Nies v. Town of Emerald Isle case. Surfrider filed amicus brief supporting Town. NC Supreme Court upheld public beach access rights Dec 2016.

Save the Indian River Lagoon. 10-year $302.8M cleanup plan for Indian River Lagoon addressing algal blooms, toxic muck, leaky septic systems. Funded by sales tax. Includes muck removal, septic upgrades, fertilizer management, education, living shorelines. Approved Nov 2016.

Protect Matunuck!. Surfrider opposed Ocean Mist bar's seawall expansion at Matunuck Beach, RI. Hard structures cause beach loss & block surf access. Forced withdrawal of faulty maintenance permit in 2016. Advocates managed retreat over armoring.

NY Bag Fee Prohibition. Campaign to stop NY state legislation prohibiting local bag fees. NYC passed 5¢ single-use bag fee; state senator introduced ban. Surfrider chapters mobilized grassroots pressure, preventing Assembly vote.

Miami-Dade Polystyrene Ban. Ban polystyrene in Miami-Dade County parks, beaches, marinas, trails. Passed June 2016, enforced June 2017. $50-$200 fines for violations. Protects marine environments from plastic pollution.

Enforcing the Clean Water Act on Kaua'i. Legal action to stop unpermitted agricultural drainage discharges polluting west Kaua'i waters. 2019 settlement requires NPDES permit, water quality monitoring for pesticides/toxins, and public data disclosure to protect Barking Sands Beach.

Folly Beach, SC Plastic Bag and Foam Cooler Ordinance. Ordinance banning single-use plastic bags and foam coolers/takeout wares at retail establishments to reduce ocean pollution and protect sea turtles and salt marshes at Folly Beach.

Defending San Diego County's Bluffs - One Piece at a Time. Surfrider San Diego defended Encinitas bluffs from hazardous development, securing 79ft setback, no basement, and seawall waiver to protect coastline resilience against sea level rise for future generations.

Oahu Passes Plastic Bag Ban & Fee. Surfrider led effort to close loopholes in plastic bag ban and place fee on paper/plastic bags. After 5 years, Honolulu City Council passed Bill 59 CD3 to phase out all plastic bags by 2020, reducing litter on Oahu.

Pres. Obama Expands Papahānaumokuākea Marine National Monument. Obama expanded Papahānaumokuākea from 139,800 to 639,300 sq mi in Sept 2016, creating world's largest marine protected area, protecting monk seals, green turtles, whales in Northwestern Hawaiian Islands

Shut Down Enbridge Line 5. Campaign to shut down 67-year-old oil pipelines crossing Straits of Mackinac. Why: prevent catastrophic oil spill threatening 700+ miles of Great Lakes coastline. What: terminate Enbridge Line 5 easement. Victory: Michigan revoked easement May 2021.

Stop Illegal Beach Obstructions. Campaign to remove misleading signs, ropes, chains & fences blocking public beach access in Walton County. Implemented Leave No Trace ordinance prohibiting beach obstructions, adopted June 2016.

Help Save the Surf at Tamarack. Monitoring sand dredge from Agua Hedionda Lagoon to protect Tamarack surf. Surfrider advocated to redirect dredged sand from over-wide North Beach to sand-starved middle/south beaches in Carlsbad, preserving surfing resources.

New England's Canyons and Seamounts Protected. Obama Admin created first Atlantic Marine National Monument protecting 3 canyons & 4 seamounts in Gulf of Maine from overfishing/mining, preserving biodiversity & recreation. Surfrider supported coalition effort.

Ban the Bag in York, Maine!. Surfrider Foundation Maine Chapter supported Bring Your Own Bag York to pass York's single-use plastic bag ban. Voters approved the ordinance 59% on Nov 3, 2015, making York the first Maine town to ban plastic bags.

Defeat of Prop 81 & Confirmation of Supreme Court Victory. Defeated Proposal 81 zoning amendment that would have allowed developers to bypass local laws in Waikiki. Protected coastal zoning after 2015 Supreme Court victory blocked high-rise condo development on beach.

Shell Beach Access - Bluff Drive Public Access Protection. Protected public pedestrian access along Bluff Drive to Pirates Cove Beach in Shell Beach, CA. CA Coastal Commission denied HOA appeal to lock gate, preserving 1960s easement for safe coastal access vs dangerous bluff climbing.

Oregon Marine Debris Action Plan. Statewide action plan with NOAA to reduce plastic pollution in Oregon's marine environment through volunteer cleanups, data collection, rapid response protocols, and policy advocacy including bag bans and plastic reduction initiatives.

Long Beach NY Bag Legislation. Coalition advocated for fee on plastic/paper bags in Long Beach, NY. Gathered 1000s of petition signatures, hosted screenings, rallied businesses. City Council passed bag legislation Oct 2016 to reduce ocean plastic pollution.

Folly Beach, SC Bans Bags, Foam, and Balloons from the Beach. Folly Beach banned plastic bags, foam containers, and balloons from the beach in 2016 to prevent marine litter and wildlife harm. Violators face $500 fine or 30 days jail. Builds on earlier retail distribution ban.

Protect public health in Nāwiliwili Stream. Surfrider Kaua'i posted warning signs at Kalapakī Bay where Nāwiliwili Stream discharges, alerting families to chronic high bacteria levels 4-8x state standards. Testing since 2016 shows sewage contamination from cesspools.

Protect The Columbia River. Surfrider opposed Tesoro Savage oil terminal on Columbia River. 279,000 comments submitted. WA Governor rejected project in 2018 citing earthquake, spill risks, and climate impacts. Victory for river and ocean protection.

Access to Tidal Waterways Statewide in NJ. NJ legislation codifying Public Trust Doctrine to ensure public access to beaches and tidal lands. Bill S.1074 signed into law May 2019, protecting coastal access rights after previous rules struck down by courts.

Stop CEMEX Sand Mining. Campaign to halt illegal coastal sand mining by CEMEX in Marina, CA. Mining ~270k cubic yards/year caused beach erosion at Marina Dunes, Fort Ord Dunes, Monterey State Beach. Victory: CA Coastal Commission shut down operations 2017.

World Oceans Day Resolution in Rhode Island!. Surfrider RI Chapter supported resolution HB6283 & S0965 to recognize June 8, 2015 as World Oceans Day, drawing statewide attention to ocean, wave & beach protection. Passed by House & Senate June 4, 2015.

Strengthen Barrington's Bag Ordinance. Surfrider RI urged Barrington town council to amend bag ban ordinance, closing loopholes exploited by plastics industry. Amendments passed 2016 increasing thickness definition to 4ml, reducing single-use plastic bags entering ocean.

Surfing is Not a Crime in Pacific City, OR. Defeated Oregon Marine Board proposal to restrict surfing in 1100-yard safety zone at Cape Kiwanda, Pacific City. Surfrider led grassroots campaign with 1600+ petition signatures. Board unanimously denied restriction June 2015.

Walton County's Obstructions on the Beach Ordinance. Surfrider Emerald Coast advocates for enforcement of ordinance prohibiting ropes, chains, signs on Walton County beaches. Protects public access, prevents injuries. Ordinance strengthened June 2016 after advocacy.

Isle of Palms, SC, Enacts Plastic Bag Ban. First SC city to ban single-use plastic bags. Prohibits retailers from distributing plastic carryout bags at city facilities and businesses. Protects coastal waters from plastic pollution. Enacted June 2015, effective 6 months later.

Ban Single-Use Plastic Bags in Oceanside. Surfrider San Diego Chapter campaigned to ban plastic shopping bags in Oceanside, CA. City Council approved ordinance in Aug 2016, requiring stores to stop using single-use plastic bags starting Jan 2017.

No New Beach Raking on Cocoa Beach!. Campaign stopped Cocoa Beach proposal to mechanically rake 1-mile beach section. Raking destroys wrack lines, harms sea turtle nesting habitat (2nd largest Loggerhead population), impacts dunes. Victory achieved.

Oregon Marine Debris Prevention. Legislative campaign establishing Submerged Land Enhancement Fund to remove derelict boats, docks & debris from Oregon inland waterways before reaching beaches. Passed July 2015, prevents disasters like Lighthouse Beach foam incident.

Atlantic Protected from Seismic Blasting. Campaign to stop seismic airgun blasting for oil/gas exploration off Mid- and South Atlantic coast. Victory in 2017 when BOEM denied all permits, protecting marine mammals including endangered Right Whales from noise pollution.
