Banned Plastic Bags in California. Surfrider Foundation led coalition to uphold California's statewide plastic bag ban (SB 270/Prop 67). Voters approved ban in Nov 2016 with 54% support, addressing ocean plastic pollution at grocery stores and retailers statewide.

Microbead-Free Waters Act. Federal ban on plastic microbeads in personal care products. Prevents tiny plastics from facial scrubs/toothpastes entering waterways and oceans via wastewater. Phased manufacturing/sales ban 2017-2019.

Parking & Access Preserved at Higgins Beach!. Surfrider Maine Chapter successfully defended free public parking at Higgins Beach, Scarborough against removal proposal. Ordinance Committee voted 2-to-1 to dismiss restrictions, preserving beach access for surfers and community.

Walton County Customary Use Ordinance. Protect public beach access in Walton County's Emerald Coast. Ordinance recognizes customary use rights to dry sand beaches for recreation, adopted Oct 2016, effective Apr 2017. 15-foot buffer from structures/dunes.

South Jersey - Longport, NJ Fee on Bags. Campaign to make Longport first NJ town with plastic bag ordinance. Educating merchants, showing 'Bag It' film to officials, conducting cleanups. Part of 'Downbeach' effort covering Ventnor, Margate, Longport.

San Diego Secondary Treatment Waiver. San Diego's wastewater treatment waiver enables Pure Water recycling project, reducing ocean discharge from Point Loma plant. Commits to 83MGD wastewater reuse by 2035 vs upgrading to secondary treatment.

Atlantic Coast Protected from Offshore Drilling. Campaign to stop offshore oil drilling on Atlantic Coast. Grassroots effort with 34 chapters, rallies, resolutions, thousands of comments. Successful March 2016 when BOEM canceled drilling plans for 2017-2022.

Loam not Foam - Oregon Schools Polystyrene Ban. Student-led campaign to ban polystyrene foam in Oregon schools. HB 2762 eliminates foam plates/trays from school meals to prevent marine litter. Signed into law June 16, 2015 after testimony by Sunnyside & Bandon students.

Mitigate Plastic Marine Debris in Maine. Maine legislation LD427 to reduce plastic marine debris & microdebris pollution. Surfrider Maine Chapter supported bill, passed House & Senate 2016. Protects ocean resources for coastal livelihoods & recreation.

Microbeads BANNED in Connecticut!. Connecticut banned plastic microbeads in personal care products via 2015 budget bill. Surfrider testimony closed industry loopholes. Phase-out protects marine waters from synthetic plastic pollution.

Support the Bag Ordinance in Falmouth!. Campaign to ban single-use plastic bags in Falmouth, Maine to reduce plastic marine debris. Ordinance passed Jan 2016 with 5-cent fee on all single-use bags, effective April 1, 2016. Led by Surfrider Maine Chapter since Oct 2014.

Protect Access at Higgins for Everyone, for Good!. Campaign to preserve public beach access at Higgins Beach, Scarborough, Maine. Fought ordinances limiting parking hours and beach use. Achieved victory maintaining 6AM parking and 1-hour limits despite parking meters installation.

California's Trash Policy Becomes Law. Statewide rule preventing trash from entering California waters. Requires stormwater permits to include trash provisions, reaching zero trash goal within 10 years. Targets plastic pollution in marine environment.

City of Huntington Beach Plastic Bag Ban Repeal. Campaign to keep Huntington Beach's plastic bag ban in place, preventing repeal attempt by city council members. Aimed to reduce plastic litter from beaches, streets, and rivers through reusable bag use.

Save the Helo - Newport Coast Guard Environmental and Recreational Response. Campaign to retain Coast Guard helicopter in Newport, Oregon for oil spill response and ocean safety. Relocation 90 miles south would delay environmental emergency response at high-traffic port. Victory: Congress funded 12-month extension.

Florida 2014 Balloon Release Bill. Campaign to stop Florida Legislature from increasing helium balloon release limit from 10 to 100 balloons for funerals/memorials. Balloons pollute ocean when released, harming marine life through ingestion and entanglement.

HI State Legislature Passes Stormwater Bill. Hawaii bill HB1325 allows counties to charge stormwater utility fees to reduce runoff into ocean. Surfrider Hawaii Chapters drafted bill with Rep. Chris Lee, formed coalition, educated public. Passed 4/26/15, signed into law.

California Bans Plastic Microbeads. Ban plastic microbeads in personal care products in California. Microbeads wash down drains, bypass wastewater treatment, and pollute waterways and ocean. AB 888 prohibits sale of products containing microbeads.

Miami Beach Foam Ban. Ban on EPS foam coolers and foodware in Miami Beach to reduce marine pollution. Started with beach ban, expanded citywide. Enforcement began with education, warnings, then fines by Nov 2016.

Climate Change Adaptation Incorporated into State Budget. Surfrider advocated for coastal protection resulting in $3M Climate Resilience Account for coastal agencies to address sea level rise and climate change adaptation. Signed into state budget June 2014.

Recreational Use Characterization Proposal. Surfrider led project mapping coastal/marine recreation in New England to fill data gaps for ocean planning. Characterizes spatial patterns of surfing, kayaking, diving, beach use to protect recreational areas in Regional Ocean Planning.

Polystyrene Foam Ban in City of San Luis Obispo, CA. Ban on polystyrene foam distribution and retail sale in San Luis Obispo, CA to reduce marine litter. Surfrider Foundation SLO Chapter and SLO FOAM Free coalition advocated. City Council unanimously passed ordinance June 2.

Melbourne Beach Voluntary Bag Ban. Voluntary plastic bag reduction program in Melbourne Beach, FL. Partnership between Surfrider's Sebastian Inlet Chapter and City Council to reduce plastic bags despite state preemption law. Modeled after St. Augustine Beach.

Save the Spit on Sea Island, GA. Prevented development on fragile, eroding south tip of Sea Island, GA. Lawsuit settlement preserved 90% of spit (80+ acres) in conservation easement, funded 5-year coastal erosion study. Protects ecologically sensitive coastline.

Encinitas EPS Foam Foodware Ordinance. Ban on expanded polystyrene foam food service items at Encinitas restaurants, city facilities and events. Addresses top-ten beach cleanup pollutant with health concerns. Surfrider San Diego advocated through workshops and hearings.

Town of Surfside Bag Ordinance. Surfside, FL banned single-use plastic bags in 2019 to reduce litter, protect storm drains, and address marine pollution. Collaboration between town, businesses, activists, and Surfrider Foundation Miami Chapter.

Oregon Lighthouse Beach Protection. Coastal erosion threatened cliff-edge home at Lighthouse Beach, Coos Bay. Surfrider advocated managed retreat over seawalls. Victory: home relocated in 2016, protecting beach and public safety while meeting homeowner needs.

Bag Ban Newburyport, Mass. Surfrider Chapter supported coalition to pass plastic bag ban in Newburyport, MA to reduce marine plastic pollution. Next step: add paper bag fee to strengthen ordinance protecting coastal waters.

Beach Access Litigation Victory in Rhode Island. Surfrider RI intervened in lawsuit over home built on Rose Nulman Park public land. June 2014 RI Supreme Court ruled for demolition, protecting public beach access near Point Judith Lighthouse, Narragansett.

A Plan for Our Ocean in the Mid-Atlantic. Surfrider works with Mid-Atlantic Regional Planning Body to secure spatial protections for priority ecological and recreational coastal areas in NY, NJ, DE, MD, VA through comprehensive ocean management plan.

Shoreline Master Program Updates for Pacific County. Surfrider advocated for updated Shoreline Master Plans in Pacific County, WA to protect ecosystems, improve shoreline resiliency, ensure public access, and plan for sea level rise. Approved Jan 2018.

Washington Marine Spatial Planning. Completed marine spatial plan protecting fisheries & sensitive marine ecosystems off Washington coast. Baseline data, improved coordination among tribes/agencies, project requirements for ocean use proposals. Finalized June 2018.

Shoreline Master Program Updates for Grays Harbor County. Surfrider Foundation led 7-year effort to update Grays Harbor's Shoreline Master Program, protecting 1,200+ miles of shorelines including Pacific Ocean, Grays Harbor, rivers. Approved July 2020, effective Aug 11, 2020.

Protect Grays Harbor from Massive Oil Terminals. Campaign to stop 3 oil export terminal proposals in Grays Harbor, WA. Victory achieved Aug 2017 when Port and developers abandoned plans, protecting Chehalis watershed and coast from oil spill risks via rail/vessel traffic.

Coastal Resilience Funding for FY 2015. Congress allocated $5M to NOAA's regional coastal resilience program supporting ocean planning via MARCO, NROC, WCGA partnerships under National Ocean Policy for ocean/coast stewardship

Kakaako Makai Saved—Again!. Coalition stopped luxury high-rise development on Kakaako Makai public coastland, Honolulu's last South Shore open space. Defeated 2014 exemption bill, upholding 2006 law banning residential development.
Clean Up Cowell's. Campaign to remove Cowell's Beach from the dirtiest beach list through water quality improvement efforts at this Santa Cruz, California coastal location.

Governor Includes Critical Funding for Coastal Commission. Surfrider advocated for $4M funding for CA Coastal Commission to update Local Coastal Plans addressing climate change impacts, sea level rise, storms, coastal erosion and flooding threats to infrastructure and resources.

Short Sands Water Quality Protection. Replaced failing septic system at Short Sands beach, Oregon to reduce bacteria levels in creeks and surf spot. New drain field handles 700k+ visits/yr. Ongoing monitoring via Blue Water Task Force near Cape Falcon Marine Reserve.

Restrict Vehicle Access near Naval Jetty in Cape Henlopen State Park. Campaign to exclude vehicles from beach area near Naval Jetty at Cape Henlopen State Park, Delaware. Addresses fake fishing to avoid walking, protects surfing/swimming areas. State created vehicle-free safety zone in 2014.

Protect Oregon's Marine Reserves. Advocacy for Oregon's Marine Reserve Program at Cape Perpetua, Cascade Head, Cape Falcon, Otter Rock & Redfish Rocks. Supporting funding, monitoring, community engagement & climate resilience since 2012.

Stop the Port Ambrose LNG Facility. Campaign to stop offshore LNG facility 17 miles off Jones Beach, NY. Opposed seafloor dredging, pipeline installation, and fracked gas export infrastructure threatening marine ecosystems and coastal waters. Vetoed November 2015.

Morro Bay Water Resources Center Moved Off The Coast. Relocated wastewater treatment plant inland in 2022, first in California to move off coast. Reduces waste release risk from floods, tsunamis, sea level rise. Upgrades treatment, produces recycled water.

Los Angeles County Bag Ban Defense in Court. Surfrider filed amicus brief supporting LA County's bag ban ordinance against plastics industry challenge. Court ruled Feb 2013 that paper bag charges aren't taxes under Prop 26. Protects ocean from plastic pollution.

Washington Campaign for Ocean Planning Fund. Ocean planning in Washington to identify sensitive coastal resources and popular activities, then plan new uses while minimizing impacts to marine life, recreation, and human uses on the Pacific coast.

Open Martin's Beach - Coastal Act Litigation. Restore public access to Martin's Beach near Half Moon Bay, closed in 2008. Surfrider won lawsuit under CA Coastal Act requiring beach remain open unless owner obtains permit. Protects generations of family beach access.

Solana Beach Seawall Policy Defended. 16-year campaign to manage seawalls protecting beach access and coastal health. Established 20-year permit reviews, mitigation fees for beach loss, and restrictions on armoring for accessory structures. Won in CA Court 2018.

Defeated Pismo Beach Seawall. Surfrider opposed seawalls at two Pismo Beach lift stations. Coastal Commission denied 2011 proposal, conditionally approved 2013 sculpted seawall requiring relocation plan within 5 years instead of permanent armoring.

NYC Bag Fee Legislation. 5-cent fee on single-use bags to reduce 9 billion plastic bags used yearly in NYC. Coalition campaign with BagitNYC, passed after 2 years. Merchant keeps fee. Modeled after successful DC program.

Oppose West Basin Desalination Plant. Campaign opposing ocean desalination plant in LA's West Basin. Advocated for recycled water & conservation instead. Project terminated Dec 2021 after 20yr fight, protecting coast from brine discharge & marine life impacts.

University of Hawaii Bans EPS Foam on Campus. UH Manoa banned EPS foam at dining locations through student petition and collaboration with administration. Policy encourages reusable/compostable products, bans foam for vendors. Approved April 2013.

Northeast Regional Ocean Planning. Surfrider advocates for holistic ocean management in New England. Successfully influenced 2016 Northeast Regional Ocean Plan certification. Focuses on protecting coastal ecosystems and recreation areas through stakeholder engagement.

Ruggles is Saved!. Protected Ruggles Ave surf break in Newport, RI from jetty construction during Cliff Walk repairs post-Hurricane Sandy. Community advocacy led to approval of surfer-friendly, lower-impact repair plans in July 2013.

Sea Breeze Estates Illegal Retaining Wall, Dune Destruction. Fought removal of illegal 12-14' retaining wall at Sea Breeze Estates, South Padre Island, TX. Wall violated 200' setback rule, threatened public beach access & dunes. Victory: wall removed, developer fined $429k, dune mitigation ordered.

Surfrider's Hawaii Chapters Help Repeal the PLDC. Hawaii Surfrider chapters led grassroots coalition to repeal Public Lands Development Corporation, preventing private development of public lands, harbors and coastal areas. Successful campaign ended April 22, 2013.

Bag Fee in Portland, Maine. Surfrider Maine Chapter helped pass 5-cent fee on checkout bags in Portland. Worked with City Council's Green Packaging Working Group. Ordinance effective April 2015 to reduce plastic pollution in ocean and beaches.

Culver City Plastic Bag Ban. Ban plastic bags & 10¢ paper bag fee at grocery/food retailers. Approved unanimously May 2013, effective Nov 2013. Based on LA County model. Protects coastal waters from plastic pollution.

Fruitstands Public Beach Access Restored. Surfrider Ventura County restored public access to Fruitstands surf break near McGrath State Beach, Oxnard CA, blocked by oil company fencing in 2012. Coastal Commission violation notice led to access restoration in 2014.

Stopped Expansion of Rock Revetment in Dana Point. Stopped Orange County's proposal to rebuild/expand 1300ft rock revetment at Niguel Shores that would impact shoreline processes, sand supply & beach access. No mitigation offered by county/homeowners. Dana Point, CA.

Rincón, PR Plastic Bag Ban. Rincón became first Puerto Rico municipality to ban single-use checkout bags in 2014. Surfrider activists drafted ordinance with local government and sewed reusable bags from donated fabric to provide alternatives.

Progressive Stormwater Permit for San Diego Region. San Diego Regional Water Board approved watershed-based MS4 stormwater permit in 2013, rejecting safe harbor clause. Uses Low Impact Development to reduce ocean pollution from contaminated stormwater runoff.

Seismic Testing on Central CA Coast Stopped. California Coastal Commission denied PG&E's seismic testing near Diablo Canyon Nuclear Plant. 400+ opposed due to marine harm vs marginal earthquake hazard benefits. Coalition of environmental groups succeeded.

City of Miami Beach Single Use Plastic Straw Ordinance. Ordinance banning single-use plastic straws citywide in Miami Beach to prevent marine pollution. Passed Sept 2019 after 7 years of advocacy. Complements existing beach property restrictions.

Defeated Bad Coastal Act Legislation in CA. Surfrider defeated AB 2211 that would have gutted California's Coastal Act protections. Partnered with organizations, lobbied Sacramento, testified at hearing. Bill killed 6-3 vote on May 7, preserving coastal development standards.

Singer Island Groin Proposal. Proposed erosion control project for 1 mile of Singer Island coastline using groins/T-groins to trap sediment and allow beach sand accretion. Project rejected Feb 2012 due to cost and effectiveness concerns.

First Coast Chapter Beach Access Restrictions. Campaign to restore beach park hours at Huguenot Memorial Park and Hanna Park in Jacksonville after budget cuts reduced access from 8pm to 6pm. City Council voted April 18th to restore summer hours starting April 28th.

San Luis Obispo County Bag Ban. Surfrider SLO Chapter supported countywide ordinance banning single-use plastic bags and adding 10¢ paper bag fee to reduce waste and prevent plastic marine pollution. Passed Jan 2012 after 6-year process.

Jenness Beach Parking Victory. Surfrider opposed permit-parking restrictions at Jenness Beach, Rye NH. Advocated for public beach access via signs & outreach. Residents voted down Articles 18 & 19 in March election, preserving non-resident parking.

Sanctuary Expansion in Northern California. Expanded Gulf of Farallones & Cordell Bank sanctuaries by 2,800 sq mi to Point Arena, protecting marine ecosystems from oil/gas drilling. Supports fisheries, recreation, tourism along Northern California coast.

Hermosa Beach Bag Ban. Ban single-use plastic bags at retail establishments in Hermosa Beach to reduce marine plastic pollution. City Council passed 4-0 vote on Aug 25, requiring recyclable paper or reusable bags at checkout.

Seismic Testing Defeated on the Atlantic Coast. Surfrider and coalition partners successfully halted seismic airgun testing for oil/gas exploration off Mid- and South Atlantic coast, protecting 130,000+ marine mammals from injury and disruption to feeding, mating, migration.

Rewild Surfers Point. Managed retreat project in Ventura, CA relocating eroding bike path and parking lot inland, restoring shoreline with cobble berm, sand dunes, and native vegetation. Nature-based solution preventing seawalls, enhancing resilience.

Marine Debris Reauthorization Act. Federal law reauthorizing NOAA's Marine Debris Program to identify, assess, prevent, reduce marine debris impacts on US economy, marine environment, navigation. Signed Dec 2012, addresses plastic ocean pollution nationally.

City of Santa Cruz Expanded EPS Foam Ban. Santa Cruz banned EPS foam products at retail/restaurants to prevent ocean pollution. Surfrider activists supported via petitions and council testimony. Prohibits foam cups, coolers, toys, packaging citywide since July 2012.

City of Los Angeles Plastic Bag Ban. LA County banned single-use plastic bags at supermarkets/pharmacies in unincorporated areas, affecting 1M+ people. 10 cent fee on paper bags. Largest municipal ban to date. Protects coastal waters from plastic pollution.

Wrightsville Beach NC Smoking Ban. Cape Fear Chapter campaigned for beach smoking ban to reduce cigarette butt pollution. After 2 years, passed as ballot initiative. One family collected 35,000 butts in a year as part of 'Hold On To Your Butt' campaign.

Settlement Protects Coastal Waters from Harms of Oil Spill Dispersants. Legal settlement requiring EPA and Coast Guard to consult marine experts before approving toxic oil dispersants, preventing harm to sea life and coastal resources after incidents like Deepwater Horizon.

Save Cherry Point. Coalition effort led by Lummi Nation defeated proposed coal export terminal at Cherry Point, Bellingham. Protected sacred waters, world-class recreation from environmental damage. US Army Corps denied permits May 2016.

San Elijo Lagoon Restoration Project. Lagoon restoration in San Diego SMCA to improve circulation, water quality & biological productivity. Includes 12-month surf monitoring to track dredging/sediment impacts on nearby waves. Addresses sea level rise & flooding.

Ban the Bag in Brigantine. Campaign to ban single-use plastic bags in Brigantine, NJ. Surfrider South Jersey Chapter collected postcards, advocated for legislation. Town introduced plastic bag ban ordinance August 15, 2018 after years of activism.

Solana Beach Bag Ban. Solana Beach became first San Diego County city to ban single-use plastic bags in April 2012. Unanimous city council vote advanced ocean conservation by preventing plastic pollution from reaching coastal waters.

Huntington Beach Reusable Bag Ordinance. Surfrider Foundation worked with Huntington Beach to ban plastic checkout bags and add 10¢ paper bag fee. Reduces ocean plastic pollution, protects wildlife, prevents drain clogging. Effective Nov 1, 2013.

Carpinteria CA - Bag Ban. Carpinteria banned single-use plastic/paper bags at retailers to reduce marine pollution. Surfrider Foundation Santa Barbara Chapter campaigned for this ordinance, approved March 12, 2012, making it CA's first South Coast city with such ban.

Laguna Beach Plastic Bag Ban. Ban on single-use plastic bags at Laguna Beach stores/facilities to reduce ocean pollution. Grocery stores/pharmacies may offer recycled paper bags for fee. Approved Feb 2012 with 6-month transition period.

Hilo Chapter Helps Pass Bill to Open Access to Papaikou Mill Beach. Surfrider's Hilo Chapter fought to restore public access to Papaikou Mill Beach after owners limited trail use. County passed Resolution 308-12 in Nov 2012 authorizing eminent domain of historic beach trail for surfing, fishing, education.

State Supreme Court Victory in the Kyo-Ya Case. Hawaii Supreme Court blocked Kyo-Ya Resort's 26-story hotel expansion into Waikiki Beach setback area. 5-year campaign by Surfrider & allies protected coastal setback laws, preventing 60-foot encroachment on Hawaii's most popular beach.

Stop Pollution of the Lahaina Wastewater Injection Wells. Lawsuit won to stop Maui County from injecting 3-5M gallons daily of treated sewage into groundwater that seeps into ocean, harming marine life and coral reefs. County must divert wastewater, fund reuse projects, obtain permits.

Attempt to Delay Implementation of 2008 Ocean Outfall Legislation Fails. 2008 FL legislation to close 6 ocean outfalls along Atlantic coast by 2025 to preserve reef ecosystem & reuse freshwater. 2011 bill attempting to extend deadline failed, keeping original timeline intact.

Barrington RI Plastic Bag Ban. First RI city to ban plastic checkout bags at stores/restaurants. Surfrider RI Chapter advocated through support letters and public meetings. Optional 5-cent paper bag fee encourages reusable bags. Adopted Oct 2012.

Nueces County Erosion Response Plan. Erosion Response Plan for Corpus Christi/Nueces County establishing 350ft coastal setback, protecting dune systems (14ft high, 50% vegetation), ensuring 100ft public beach access. Passed 2012 after advocacy by Surfrider Texas Coastal Bend Chapter.

Destin Customary Use Legal Access Case. Legal case defending public beach access rights in Destin/South Walton County, FL. Homeowners challenged customary use doctrine. Surfrider filed Amicus Brief. Court dismissed homeowners' claims in 2012, upholding public access.

Surfrider's Oahu Chapter Helps Pass Smoking Ban. Oahu Chapter lobbied for island-wide smoking ban in parks and beaches. Started with South Shore ban (Bill 72, 2013), expanded to all Oahu beaches/parks (Bill 25, July 2013). Reduces pollution, protects marine life.

RESTORE Act Passes. Dedicates 80% of Deepwater Horizon fines to Gulf Coast Restoration Trust Fund. Restores beaches, coastal marshes, barrier islands, wildlife damaged by BP oil spill. Supports economic development, tourism, recreation, commercial fishing.

Long Beach Polystyrene Ordinance. Ban on polystyrene plastic citywide in Long Beach, CA. Prohibits EPS foam containers, rigid polystyrene, and foam coolers. Phased implementation over 18 months starting May 2018 to reduce marine plastic pollution.

Defeated Pismo Beach/Shell Beach Seawalls. Surfrider's San Luis Obispo Chapter successfully opposed two proposed seawalls in Pismo Beach that threatened public beach access. Through surveys, documentation, and advocacy, the California Coastal Commission denied the project in 2011.

San Clemente Expanded Polystyrene Ban. San Clemente, CA banned expanded polystyrene (EPS) in food service ware citywide. Approved unanimously by City Council to reduce marine plastic pollution from foam containers entering coastal waters.

City of Monterey Bag Ban. Ordinance to ban single-use plastic/paper bags by retailers in Monterey, with fees on recycled bags. Aims to reduce plastic marine pollution. Supported by Surfrider Monterey Chapter in 2011.

Newport Ban the Bag. Newport, OR banned single-use plastic bags in 2019 after Surfrider Chapter and Sam Case Elementary students advocated to City Council. Ordinance requires retailers to charge for paper/reusable bags, phased implementation by business size.

Capitola Plastic Bag Ban. Capitola City Council passed plastic checkout bag ban with 25 cent paper bag fee. Led by Surfrider Santa Cruz, Save Our Shores, and Environment CA. Ordinance effective April 10, 2013 to reduce ocean plastic pollution.

Agate Beach, OR Access Improvement. Newport Chapter opposed road vacation to preserve public beach access at Agate Beach. 2+ years of stakeholder work secured $600k ODOT funding for parking, bathrooms, recreational facilities completed 2013.

Hermosa Beach Polystyrene Foodware Ban. Ban on polystyrene take-out food packaging in Hermosa Beach to reduce ocean pollution. Surfrider South Bay Chapter supports ordinance through public meetings, letters, and rallying businesses. Backed by Green Task Force.

Final Settlement for Access at Strands Beach in Dana Point. 6-year litigation securing public beach access at Dana Point Strands Beach. Settlement ensures 5am-10pm access, gate removal, new trails, educational programs on marine conservation, sea level rise impacts for Title 1 schools.

Strands Beach Access. Legal victory ensuring public beach access at Dana Point Headlands. Fought restrictions on central accessway after 2010 residential development. Court ruled city's access limits unlawful, arbitrary. Ongoing pressure on appeals.

Cannon Beach Water Quality Protection. Reducing bacterial contamination at Ecola Court Outfall through monitoring, advocacy, and infrastructure testing. Victory: City identified sewer failures and cross-connections, approved repairs after decade of Surfrider advocacy.

Redfish Rocks Marine Reserve Management Plan Adopted. Support implementation of Redfish Rocks Marine Reserve off Port Orford, Oregon. Designated 2009, community-developed management plan includes education, enforcement, biological/socioeconomic monitoring, economic development.

Big Wave Development Opposition. Surfrider Foundation opposed 225,000 sq ft mixed-use development at Pillar Point Marsh. Campaign stopped project threatening historical wetlands, water quality, and coastal ecosystem through advocacy with environmental partners.

Strands Gate Beach Access Campaign. Legal campaign to expand public beach access at Strands Vista in Dana Point. Challenged restrictive gate hours (8am-5pm) as Coastal Act violations. 2016 settlement achieved 5am-10pm access, gate removal, and $300k mitigation.

Santa Cruz World Surfing Reserve. World's 4th surfing reserve protecting 23+ surf breaks from Natural Bridges to Opal Cliffs. Designated Feb 2011, dedicated Apr 2012 to protect world-class waves like Steamer Lane & facilitate local stewardship.

Chumash Heritage National Marine Sanctuary. NOAA designated 4,500 sq mi sanctuary protecting marine habitats from oil drilling, seabed mining, pollution. First Indigenous-nominated sanctuary honoring Chumash culture, spanning 116 miles of central CA coast.

Honolua Bay Is Saved!. Protected 280 acres at Lipoa Point/Honolua Bay from golf course development. Coalition opposed luxury homes threatening world-famous surf spot, cultural area & marine reserve. HB 1424 authorized state acquisition for conservation.

Maine Beach Access Litigation. Litigation (2009-2019) protecting public beach access rights at Goose Rocks Beach, Kennebunkport. Court ruled beach is town-owned and held in public trust, ensuring access for all despite <10% public coastline ownership in Maine.

Improve Water Quality at Larrabee State Park. Multi-year effort to identify and fix pollution sources at Wild Cat Cove beach, Larrabee State Park, WA. Stakeholder collaboration and camper education reduced bacteria levels, removing swim advisory and restoring beach access.

Maui Bans Plastic Bags. Surfrider's Maui Chapter helped pass Hawaii's first county-wide single-use plastic bag ban in 2008, effective Jan 2011. Coalition effort resulted in cleaner island and broad public support, inspiring Kauai's ban.

Favorable Hawaii Navy Sonar Ruling. Court ruled Navy must implement mitigation measures to protect marine mammals from sonar exercises in Hawaii waters, including increased monitoring, lookouts, 500m safety zones, and gradual sonar power-up.

California Legislature Approves Statewide Bag Ban with SB 270. California bans single-use plastic bags statewide to reduce ocean pollution. SB 270 approved Aug 2014, signed by Gov. Brown Sept 2014. First US statewide ban after 6-year advocacy effort.

City of Marina Polystyrene Ban. Surfrider Monterey Chapter worked with coalition to ban polystyrene foam food containers in Marina, CA. Ordinance adopted Nov 2011 requires biodegradable/compostable alternatives for food providers and city events.

New Surfing Beach in NYC. NYC Chapter secured second legal surfing beach at Rockaway 67th Street in 2007. Advocacy convinced Parks Dept to designate surfing-only access after earlier victory at Beach 90th Street, expanding coastal recreation rights.

Encinitas Bag Ban Passed. Encinitas adopted single-use plastic bag ban with 10¢ paper bag fee. Effective March 2015 for grocery stores, Sept 2015 for all retail. Reduces plastic pollution entering ocean from coastal community.

Monterey Regional Water Supply. Surfrider advocated to reduce seawater desalination plant from 9,000 to 2,933 acre-feet/year, require slant wells to protect marine life, mitigate brine discharge impacts, and achieve net zero emissions in Monterey Peninsula.

City of San Diego Plastic Bag Ban. 8-year advocacy campaign to ban disposable plastic checkout bags in San Diego. Surfrider activists educated public, built coalition, pressured policymakers. Ordinance passed Aug 2016, making SD 150th CA jurisdiction to ban bags.

Long Island, NY Surfing Access Near Montauk Point Lighthouse. Surfrider advocates for legal surfing access near Montauk Point Lighthouse, restricted by NY State Parks. Successfully defended surfing tickets in court against surfcaster opposition to expand coastal recreation rights.

Stopped Singer Island Breakwaters. Surfrider opposed 11 breakwater segments planned 200ft offshore Singer Island to trap sediment. Project would cover 18.9 acres including hard bottom habitat, harm fish & sea turtles. County abandoned 2011 due to cost & concerns.

Morro Bay/Cayucos Wastewater Treatment Plant Siting. Campaign to upgrade wastewater treatment to Clean Water Act standards, relocate plant outside coastal hazard zones, maximize water reclamation, and eliminate ocean discharge of partially treated sewage in Morro Bay/Cayucos.

Trestles Saved Forever From Toll Road. Decade-long campaign stopped 6-lane toll road through San Onofre State Beach. Protected Trestles surf break, San Mateo Creek watershed, wildlife habitat. Settlement created $28M conservation fund, avoidance areas.

Better Public Notice of Beach Pollution in Hawaii. Campaign to require Hawaii Dept of Health to post warning signs at chronically polluted beaches and during Brown Water Advisories. EPA pressured state to comply with posting laws after Surfrider advocacy.

Eliminate Single Use Plastics from Beach Concessionaires in Miami Beach. Surfrider Miami advocates to eliminate single-use plastics from beachside concession stands. City ordinance passed Oct 2019 requires 100% reusable products by Oct 2020, preventing plastic pollution entering marine environment.

NJ Now Posting Warnings After One High Bacteria Test. Surfrider Foundation successfully advocated for NJ to post beach warnings after one high bacteria test, replacing the previous two-day testing requirement that rarely resulted in closures, improving public health protection.

Stop Muddying Kauai's Waters. Combat soil erosion from agriculture & development killing Kauai's coral reefs. Surfrider exposed illegal GMO farming practices lacking erosion controls, forcing adoption of Best Management Practices & permits to protect ocean waters.

Toll Road Stopped at San Onofre State Beach / Trestles. US Commerce Dept upheld CA Coastal Commission denial of 6-lane toll road through San Onofre State Beach near Trestles, protecting state park, natural resources, and surf break from highway impacts.

City of Santa Cruz adopts ban on polystyrene food service wares. Santa Cruz banned polystyrene food service wares in 2008 to protect coastal waters from plastic pollution. This ordinance prevents foam containers from breaking down into ocean microplastics.

Implementation of National Ocean Policy. US National Ocean Policy implementation plan released April 2013 with 50+ actions for ocean, coast, and Great Lakes protection. Focuses on ecosystem management, habitat restoration, climate adaptation, spatial planning, water quality.

Santa Cruz County Polystyrene Ban. Santa Cruz County banned polystyrene food service wares. Surfrider's Santa Cruz Chapter partnered with organizations to pass this ordinance protecting coastal waters from foam pollution in 2008.

Hawaii, Oahu, North Shore—Preservation of Pupukea-Paumalu (Save Sunset Beach). Prevented development of 300-home gated community on bluffs above Sunset Beach, Pipeline & Rocky Point. Coalition raised $8M to purchase land for public preservation. Ongoing stewardship protects North Shore surf breaks.

Polystyrene Banned in Monterey. Monterey banned polystyrene to reduce marine debris in coastal waters and Monterey Bay National Marine Sanctuary. Surfrider's Monterey Chapter led community coalition, garnered business support, achieving unanimous city council approval.

Coastal Commission Receives Authority to Fine Coastal Act Violators. CA Coastal Commission gains authority to fine violators blocking beach access. Addresses 2,000 violations, mainly illegal no parking/access signs by private landowners. Protects public coastal access rights.

Prevented Damaging Energy Project on Oregon Coast. Surfrider intervened with FERC to stop Oceanlinx's Florence Wave Energy facility. After 9 months with no public outreach, company withdrew permit. Protected surfing, fishing, and beach access at south jetty.
Lake Worth Surf Saved. Surfrider Foundation successfully protected Lake Worth surf break by stopping a beach fill project that threatened this coastal surfing area in 2006.

Town of East Hampton, NY Approves New Coastal Legislation. East Hampton prohibits new hard erosion structures on ocean beaches, creates Coastal Erosion Hazard Overlay District. Prioritizes non-structural measures like vegetation, sand fencing, building setbacks to protect beaches.
Beach access in South Florida. Protected beach access to local surf spot from condo development in South Florida. Campaign ensures public coastal access rights against private development threats.

Governor Signs Rapid Water Quality Testing Bill. SB 1395 enables rapid beach water quality testing, delivering results in hours vs 24-48hrs. Provides real-time pollution alerts to ocean users, strengthening protection and public safety at California beaches.

Plastic Bag Ban in Malibu. Surfrider's West LA/Malibu Chapter worked with Heal The Bay to ban plastic bags in Malibu retail stores, addressing plastic pollution in marine environments through the Rise Above Plastics campaign in 2008.

Jones Beach and Moses Park opened to surfing access. Surfrider Foundation successfully opened Jones Beach State Park and Robert Moses State Park to surfing access in 2006, expanding coastal recreation opportunities for surfers in New York.

A Win for Diversity In the Surfing Line Up In Pacifica!. Pacifica approved Community Access Partnership Permit program allowing Brown Girls Surf and City Surf Project to operate at Pacifica Beach, promoting diverse community access to coastal recreation. Approved Aug 2020.

Marin County Bag Ban. Surfrider Marin & partners persuaded Marin County to ban single-use bags. Over 1M bags enter Bay annually. Initiative reduces plastic pollution harming marine ecosystems outside Golden Gate. County defended ban in court.

Westport Connecticut Votes to Ban Plastic Checkout Bags. First East Coast town to ban plastic checkout bags. Westport CT, on Long Island Sound, voted Sept 2008 to prohibit disposable plastic bags at retail stores, giving retailers 6 months to comply. Protects marine environment.

New beach access for the First Coast. Surfrider First Coast Chapter secured perpendicular beach walkway at Escambia Right of Way, St. Johns County, FL. Approved May 4th by County Commission to improve public beach access in undeveloped area.

Southern California Establishes Marine Protected Areas. CA Fish & Game Commission approved network of MPAs in Southern California after years of negotiations. Part of Marine Life Protection Act (1999). Surfrider worked with diverse groups for balanced input in MLPA process.

Dana Point Plastic Bag Ban. Single-use plastic bag ban at stores and city facilities to reduce plastic litter in beaches, parks, roads and waterways. Passed March 2012, effective April 2013. Second Orange County city after Laguna Beach.

Massive Playa Vista Development Stopped. Surfrider's South Bay Chapter stopped Phase 2 development threatening Ballona Wetlands. Settlement reversed permits, enabling potential public acquisition for wetland restoration in Southern California's coastal network.

Improved Beach Access in Walton County, FL. Defending public beach access on Miramar Beach against condo owners' opposition. County creating 100+ parking spaces on public easement near Whale's Tail Restaurant to formalize beachgoer access previously limited to roadside parking.

NJ/NY LNG Victory. Defeated Liberty Natural Gas offshore LNG facility off Asbury Park, NJ. Project would have used seafloor turret & pipeline for tanker re-gasification. Victory achieved through coalition opposition led by Jersey Shore Chapter.

Landmark Court Decision to Protect Marine Species. US Court of Appeals struck down EPA rule on 'once through' cooling systems by coastal generators. Surfrider Foundation co-plaintiff victory enforcing Clean Water Act protection for marine species.

Protect Southeast Florida's Coral Reefs. Established Southeast Florida Coral Reef Ecosystem Conservation Area near Biscayne National Park to study and protect reefs from disease and bleaching, with water quality monitoring program funding.

Rincoeños Stop Condos and Save Beach Access in PR. Stopped condo construction threatening beach access & fishermen's area in Rincón, PR. Legal battles led to permit freeze (2008) due to flood zone violations. Illegal fence removed, restoring public access near Elkhorn coral reefs.

Turtle Bay Kuilima Resort Required to do SEIS. Surfrider's Oahu Chapter filed amicus brief and donated $10,000 to lawsuit forcing Turtle Bay Resort to conduct Supplemental EIS for massive North Shore Oahu development, protecting coastal environment from outdated 1985 plan.

Bellingham, WA Plastic Bag Ban. Community campaign led by Surfrider Foundation to ban plastic bags in Bellingham. Gathered 3,000+ signatures, passed 7-0 by City Council in July 2011. Ordinance bans carry-out plastic bags, adds 5¢ paper bag fee to reduce ocean impact.

New Water Quality Measures for Santa Monica Bay. Adoption of bacteria Total Maximum Daily Load (TMDL) into Regional Water Quality Control Board Storm Water Permits for Santa Monica Bay to improve coastal water quality and protect ocean health.

Encinitas Plastic Bag Ban Ordinance. First San Diego County city to ban plastic bags & fee paper bags to reduce single-use plastics. Surfrider SD Chapter collected 2,000 signatures, worked with City Council on phased implementation with education for residents & businesses.

Surfing access to Deerfield Beach FL. Surfrider Foundation secured surfing access at Deerfield Beach, Florida where beach access was previously restricted. Campaign completed in 2006 to protect coastal recreation rights.

World Surfing Reserve at Malibu's Surfrider Beach. First World Surfing Reserve designation preserving iconic Malibu surf break and coastal heritage. UNESCO-inspired program protects surfing areas through community-driven conservation of important surf breaks worldwide.

Plastic Bags Banned in Edmonds, WA. Seattle Chapter campaign achieved plastic shopping bag ban in Edmonds. Community and local businesses supported the initiative to reduce marine plastic pollution in Puget Sound coastal waters.

Goleta Beach Saved - Groin Defeated. California Coastal Commission denied Santa Barbara County's groin project at Goleta Beach on July 8. Project would have trapped sand, causing erosion to eastern beaches and damaging habitats.

Rockpile seawall stopped. Surfrider stopped a 300-foot seawall at Rockpile, Heisler Park, Laguna Beach in 2006. Campaign protected coastal area from hardening infrastructure that threatens beaches and marine ecosystems.

Governor signs bill that will help fund conservation programs. AB 754 creates tax check-off box for CA Coastal Commission WhaleTail Grants funding nonprofits doing ocean conservation: water testing, beach cleanups, Ocean Friendly Gardens. Signed Sept 2013.

Governor signs Sea Level Rise Planning Bill. Surfrider lobbied for AB 691 requiring California public trust lands to analyze and plan for sea level rise impacts, protecting coastal natural and manmade resources through climate change adaptation planning.

Pacific Grove Polystyrene Ban. Pacific Grove banned polystyrene food service wares to reduce non-biodegradable waste reaching local beaches and ocean. Partnership with Sustainable Pacific Grove and Monterey Green Action achieved ordinance passage in 2008.

Temporary seawall ban in Solana Beach. Ban on new seawalls in Solana Beach until new ordinance is devised. Campaign to protect coastal areas from hardened shoreline structures that damage beaches and marine ecosystems.

Morro Bay/Cayucos Wastewater Treatment Plant Upgrade. Upgrade wastewater plant from partial to full secondary+tertiary treatment, ending 301(h) waiver. Cleaner ocean discharge, water reclamation opportunity. Morro Bay/Cayucos, CA. Approved May 2024.

Oregon Oil and Gas Drilling Moratorium. Oregon Legislature passed HB 3613 restoring moratorium on offshore oil/gas drilling in territorial waters (0-3nm) through 2020. Coalition of conservationists, fishing groups, businesses supported ban to protect ocean ecosystems.

Solana Beach Public Recreation Fee. Advocacy campaign to establish fair mitigation fees for coastal armoring impacts on beach access in Solana Beach. Surfrider SD Chapter successfully pushed for 67% wage rate in travel cost methodology, doubling recreation fees.

Prevent Defacto Seawall in Solana Beach. Surfrider successfully opposed filling 90ft of seacaves with concrete to protect homes not threatened by erosion. Prevented defacto seawall loophole that would harm beach access and set bad precedent for coastal armoring.

Ban Polystyrene in Imperial Beach. Imperial Beach banned polystyrene in food establishments to prevent plastic pollution. Restaurants phased out EPS over 6 months. Protects coastline and ocean from thousands of styrofoam items.

San Diego Plastics Ordinance. Ban on polystyrene foam containers, beach toys, coolers at San Diego restaurants and retailers to reduce ocean plastic pollution. Approved Dec 2022 after 3-year legal delay. Grassroots campaign led by Surfrider volunteers.

Stopped Reclassification of Shoreline in Rhode Island. Surfrider prevented Rhode Island CRMC from reclassifying Matunuck Beach shoreline as man-made, blocking future seawall expansion. Small wall approved for road protection only. Advocates natural erosion management over hard structures.

Puerto Rico's Northeastern Ecological Corridor Saved. Protected wave-rich ecological corridor from mega-resort development through executive order designating it as nature reserve. Coalition effort led by Initiative for Sustainable Development in Puerto Rico's northeast coast.

Marine Reserves Designated in Oregon. Oregon designated Cape Perpetua, Cascade Head, and Cape Falcon marine reserves protecting 9% of territorial sea from fishing, drilling, and development through no-take zones and protected areas.

Save Trestles. Campaign to stop toll road development threatening Trestles surf break and coastal ecosystem. Surfrider and partners successfully blocked road segments through water quality protection, defeating developer appeals at State Water Board.

Central Long Island Pro Park Campaign. Surfrider campaign to preserve seascape vistas at Jones Beach, Robert Moses, Gilgo State Parks & Fire Island National Seashore by opposing offshore wind turbines in viewshed. Successfully cancelled LIPA proposal.

Governor Signs Bill to Improve Coastal Commission Transparency. AB 474 improves transparency of California Coastal Commission by requiring disclosure of all participants in ex parte communications, not just initiators. Ensures open, impartial coastal protection decisions.

Tidepool awareness and educational success in Los Angeles. Compelled State Parks to implement Tidepool Awareness Program at Malibu and Point Dume with educational signage protecting intertidal marine life. Completed 2006.
Santa Monica Bag Ban. Santa Monica banned single-use plastic bags at retail stores to reduce ocean pollution. Passed Jan 2011, enforced Sept 2011. Paper bags sold for 10 cents. Restaurants exempt.

No LNG Island in NY & NJ. Surfrider chapters successfully opposed Atlantic Sea Island Groups' proposal to build a 60-acre artificial LNG terminal island 13 miles offshore Long Beach, NY on Cholera Banks reef through petitions, hearings, and paddle-outs.

Washington State Year-Round Rescue Tug. Year-round rescue tug stationed at Neah Bay to prevent oil spills in Strait of Juan de Fuca and Washington's outer coast. Funded by shippers/tankers. Signed into law March 24th after years of advocacy following Exxon Valdez.

Long Beach Bag Ban. Long Beach banned plastic checkout bags and imposed 10-cent fee on paper bags at supermarkets, pharmacies, farmers markets. Ordinance signed May 2011 to reduce marine plastic pollution in this California port city.

Jetty Island Water Quality. Improving public notification of wastewater spills (2-4/year) at Everett Treatment Plant near Jetty Island to protect swimmers, kite/wind surfers. Surfrider added to alert list for immediate beach closure warnings May-Oct.

Long Beach NY Beach Fill. City of Long Beach, NY voted against poorly designed beach fill plan by Army Corps of Engineers. Campaign to protect coastal integrity and prevent harmful beach engineering project in Long Beach.

VICTORY - San Francisco Votes No on Prop I. Defeated Prop I to enable Great Highway Extension retreat at South Ocean Beach. Avoided $80M seawall that would consume beach. Advancing coastal resilience project with managed retreat to protect against sea level rise.

Removal of Rincon, CA septic tanks. Surfrider Foundation partnered with Heal the Ocean to compel state agency to force removal of septic tanks at Rincon, CA coastal area to prevent ocean pollution from wastewater contamination in 2006.

Defeat of Pro-Oil Drilling Legislation in California. Defeated Assembly Bill 2719 to prevent offshore drilling in California state waters. Surfrider Foundation led 5-town road show educating communities on drilling dangers, mobilizing chapters for legislative victory.

Budget Victory for Coast. California 2015 budget allocated $3M for Coastal Commission to partner with local governments to complete and update Local Coastal Programs (LCPs), protecting coastal resources at local level after Surfrider advocacy.

Stopped Coastal Armoring at Sloat, San Francisco. Surfrider SF stopped unpermitted rock revetments at Ocean Beach. Worked with partners to deny 600ft armoring permit, protect beach, allow Ocean Beach Master Plan for community-supported erosion strategies.

Capitola Polystyrene Ban. Santa Cruz chapter mobilized support for Capitola ordinance banning polystyrene foam disposable food service ware, promoting biodegradable alternatives. Passed 3-2 after community testimony and letters.

Dana Point Foam Foodware Ban. Dana Point banned polystyrene foodware at vendors & city events on Feb 21, 2012. Surfrider South OC Chapter mobilized activists to support the ordinance after foam was found as top beach cleanup item.

Ocean Protection Law in NJ. NJ law requiring ecosystem-based ocean management. Establishes Ocean Protection Council to study, coordinate & develop management plans. Surfrider & Coastal Ocean Coalition of NJ advocated for passage.

Year-Round Water Quality Testing in Delaware. Delaware Chapter convinced DNREC to expand beach water quality monitoring beyond tourist season to year-round testing, protecting surfers and beachgoers who use beaches during off-season and winter swells.

7-Year Ban on Domestic Drilling. Obama Administration halted new offshore drilling leases along continental US for 7 years. Reversed March 2010 plans for south Atlantic, eastern Gulf of Mexico, Alaska. Protects coastal waters from drilling expansion.

Stopped Destructive Development Project at the Fitzgerald Marine Reserve. San Mateo County rejected oversized residential development at Moss Beach's Fitzgerald Marine Reserve. 3,159 sq ft addition threatened sensitive coastal habitat and would require shoreline armoring. Board voted 4-1 to deny permits in 2024.

WA Legislature supports coastal Marine Resources Committees. Washington Legislature passed bill establishing citizen advisory Marine Resources Committees on outer coast to address beach health, pollution, invasive species, habitat loss. $250k funding provided for coastal ecosystem protection.

Lee County Fertilizer Ordinance. Limits fertilizer use within 10ft of waterways Jun-Sep to reduce red tide & algal blooms affecting Lee County's beaches & $2B tourism. Violations up to $500. Partners: Sierra Club, SCCF, Nature Conservancy.

Protected Beach Access at Bonaire Beach. Secured public beach access to 900ft of beachfront at former Coast Guard property in Jupiter Island through inter-local agreement. Added 20 parking spaces at nearby Hobe Sound Beach for conservation and recreation.

Texas Opens It's Beaches with a Constitutional Amendment!. Texas passed Prop 9 constitutional amendment (75% voter approval) protecting public beach access rights along Gulf of Mexico's 367-mile coast, strengthening 1959 Open Beaches Act against development challenges.

Oregon Marine Reserves. Oregon Legislature passed HB 3013 to implement marine reserves at Redfish Rocks (Port Orford) and Otter Rock (Depoe Bay), with evaluation of additional sites at Cape Falcon, Cascade Head, Cape Perpetua, and Coos County area.

Stopped Sewage Outfall at Delray Beach. Surfrider partnered with local groups to close Florida's first sewage outfall at Delray Beach in 2006, protecting endangered corals and reef ecosystems from sewage dumping.

Florida Beach Test Funding Protected. Surfrider Florida Chapters successfully prevented state budget cuts to beach water quality monitoring programs, protecting public health and safety in a state where 85% of tourism depends on coastal resources.
Stopped gold mining on WA coast. Surfrider Foundation partnered to stop gold mining operations at beaches on Washington's outer coast in 2006, protecting coastal ecosystems from mining impacts.

CA Beach Monitoring Funding Restored. Surfrider restored California beach water quality monitoring funding cut in 2008. Mobilized 2400+ activists, lobbied with partners. State approved Prop 13 Beach Grant funds for 2008-2009, seeking long-term solution.

Florida Inlet Management Bill. Addresses beach erosion from 60+ artificially deepened inlets. Jetties interrupt sand flow causing erosion. Campaign seeks state management to mitigate inlet impacts and establish cost-sharing for restoration solutions.

Smoking Banned on All Beaches in Santa Monica Bay. Redondo Beach banned smoking at beaches/parks, completing Santa Monica Bay coverage. Reduces cigarette litter, protects marine life from toxic butts, improves water quality and beachgoer health.

Ventura City Council Adopts Green Street Policy. Ventura adopts green streets policy allocating 20% of paving funds to incorporate stormwater management elements in repaving projects, with pilot demonstration to reduce urban runoff impacting ocean health.

Treasure Coast destructive restoration project stopped. Surfrider stopped a destructive, non-compliant emergency dune restoration project on Florida's Treasure Coast in 2006, protecting coastal ecosystems from harmful development practices.

Protected Coral Reef from Pollution in Lake Worth, FL. Stopped Lake Worth's plan to discharge 4M gallons/day of nutrient-laden wastewater onto coral reef. Public outcry & 1000+ letters led FDEP to change permit from ocean discharge to injection, protecting reef ecosystem.

Florida Access Legislation. Legislation to protect both lateral and perpendicular beach access in Florida by amending Chapter 161 Beach Management statute, addressing coastal overdevelopment impacts on public beach access.

Clean Oceans Act in Florida. Stops gambling boats dumping 44M gallons chlorinated waste yearly. Requires DEP registration, waste treatment systems, and federal dumping prohibition. Led by Sebastian Inlet Chapter.

Access Restored in South Florida. South Florida chapter restored public beach access closed by developers during construction. Campaign successfully reopened indefinitely closed beach with no temporary access provided during project.

Save surfing access at Cocoa Beach Pier. Surfrider Foundation campaign that successfully saved surfing access at Cocoa Beach Pier, Florida. Protects coastal recreation rights and public beach access for surfers and ocean users at this iconic Atlantic coast location.

Derelict Crab Pots Cleaned from Southern Oregon Coast. Removed 283 derelict commercial crab pots from Brookings beach and nearshore. Pots spilled Dec 2006, threatened surfing access and safety. Activists cleaned Southern Oregon coast to protect marine environment.

Bill passes to improve WA oil spill response programs. WA law requires Dept of Ecology to train volunteers, mandate oil spill drills, equip fishermen as first responders, improve tanker requirements & stockpile response equipment. Passed on Gulf Oil Spill anniversary.

Beach Water Quality Notification in Corpus Christi, TX. Corpus Christi City Council unanimously approved beach water quality posting signs per Texas Beach Watch Program, enabling residents and tourists to make informed decisions about swimming and water activities in bay and Gulf waters.

Governor Lifts Suspension on Coastal Act. After Refugio State Beach oil spill, coalition urged Governor to restore Coastal Act jurisdiction. Successfully advocated for lifting suspension to maintain regulatory oversight of California coast.

Prevention of Shoreline Structure Expansion at Herring Point, DE. Prevented groin expansion/new structures at Herring Point, Cape Henlopen State Park to address erosion. Protects surf and natural resources drawing thousands regionally.

Oppose Offshore Oil Drilling in Hermosa Beach. Campaign to stop E&B Oil's offshore drilling proposal in Hermosa Beach. Voters rejected slant wells 78.9% in March 2015. Surfrider South Bay Chapter led opposition with Heal the Bay through forums, ads, and voter outreach.

Public Hearings required for Beach Fill Projects in NJ. NJ legislation requiring public hearings before beach replenishment projects. Addresses disastrous consequences of beachfill projects through community input and oversight of coastal protection efforts.

Shoreline Preservation in Cannon Beach, OR. Surfrider successfully opposed Measure 37 claim to build motel on protected sand dunes. City ruled against development west of vegetation line, upholding Oregon Beach Bill protections for ocean beaches.

Enhanced Water Testing and Notification in Imperial Beach. Daily water quality testing at 9 Imperial Beach beaches to monitor sewage pollution from Mexico. Results posted publicly to protect health along southern San Diego coast affected by 150+ closure days in 2020.

Treasure Coast protection of the offshore sand shoals. Protected nearshore sand shoals off Florida's Treasure Coast from Army Corps of Engineers dredging. Campaign safeguards critical coastal sediment resources and marine habitat from extraction activities.

Increased Protection for the Monterey Bay National Marine Sanctuary. 7-year plan expanded sanctuary by 775 sq mi to include Davidson Seamount, prohibited cruise ship discharges, limited motorized watercraft, added Maverick's tow-in surfing zone, reduced invasive species introduction.

South Padre Island - Plastic Bag Ban. South Padre Island banned non-compostable plastic bags at point of sale. Allows reusable bags, recycled paper bags (40% post-consumer content), and compostable bags. Voluntary ban started Feb 2011, mandatory Jan 2012.

Marine Protected Areas on the Central Coast, CA. Network of MPAs enacted on CA Central Coast under Marine Life Protection Act. Surfrider worked with activists and stakeholders statewide to protect special coastal places and marine life.

Governor Brown Signs Legislation Strengthening Enforcement of Marine Protected Areas. AB 298 allows CA Fish & Wildlife officers to issue tickets for MPA violations, streamlining enforcement against poaching and illegal fishing in protected coastal waters. Signed Oct 2015.

National Ocean Policy. Established July 19, 2010 by President Obama. First comprehensive U.S. ocean policy protecting ocean, coastal & Great Lakes ecosystems. Uses marine spatial planning, regional cooperation, and National Ocean Council for implementation.

Texas Open Beaches Act Defended by Courts. Legal victory ensuring public beach access in Surfside, TX. Court ruled 16 houses on public beach must be removed under Texas Open Beaches Act. Surfrider provided key evidence through beach photos and adoption.

Manhattan Beach Passes Ordinance to Ban Plastic Carry-Out Bags. Manhattan Beach City Council unanimously banned plastic carry-out bags. Phased implementation: 6 months for groceries/restaurants, 1 year for other retail. Supported by Surfrider Foundation and local residents.

Martin's Beach Access Bill Signed. SB 968 requires State Lands Commission to negotiate public access to Martin's Beach after landowner blocked entry. One-year negotiation period, with alternative acquisition mechanisms if unsuccessful. Signed Sept 2014.

Topanga water quality. Convinced State Parks to test and clean up water quality issues from leaking septic systems at Topanga Lagoon and Beach. Protects coastal water quality and beach health for ocean users and marine ecosystems.
Surfer's Point. Surfrider Foundation campaign focused on Surfer's Point coastal protection and preservation. Details on specific objectives, timeline, and location not available from page metadata.

Texas Coastal Bend Building Setback Campaign. Surfrider activists successfully advocated to maintain 350-foot building setback from ocean in Texas Coastal Bend to protect against erosion, hurricanes, and sea-level rise threatening ports and coastal communities.

Stopped LNG Terminal in Long Island Sound. Surfrider CT & environmental groups stopped Broadwater LNG terminal in Long Island Sound. NY Governor Patterson rejected project in April after sustained citizen advocacy & state government pressure protected coastal waters.

Styrofoam Banned in Scotts Valley. Scotts Valley banned polystyrene food containers to protect sea creatures that mistake foam pieces for food. Ordinance passed Dec 2008, effective 6 months later. Part of coalition effort for county-wide ban.

Sonar Testing in Southern California Rejected. California Coastal Commission unanimously rejected Navy explosives and sonar training off Southern California coast due to insufficient evidence of negligible impact on marine ecosystems and endangered mammals in MPAs.

Port Orford Stormwater Ordinance Strengthened. Port Orford amended stormwater ordinance to protect water quality in streams and nearshore. 2+ year collaboration included research, education, outreach. Goal: protect water quality per Community Stewardship Area objectives.

Neah Bay Rescue Tug Funded. Year-round rescue tug at Neah Bay to prevent oil spills from tankers/cargo vessels. Protects Puget Sound wildlife & beaches. Responds to vessels in distress. $3.7M funded by WA Legislature after advocacy campaign.

VA Gov Kaine Reject Oil drilling Bill. Governor Kaine rejected bill seeking to end moratorium on natural gas/oil exploration, development, and production off Virginia coast. Campaign to protect coastal waters from offshore drilling impacts.
El Morro returned to Crystal Cove. El Morro section of Crystal Cove State Park returned to public access. Surfrider Foundation campaign to restore public coastal access at Crystal Cove, California.

Save Holualoa and Lyman's Surf Break in Kona. Stopped 4-story condo development 40ft from reef at sacred Lyman's surf spot, Holualoa Bay, Kona. Community rallies & hearings led developer to withdraw permit application, protecting coastal access & Hawaiian cultural site.

Ventura Approves Curb Cuts to Reduce Runoff. Ventura County Surfrider worked with City of Ventura to create no-cost permits for parkway curb cuts and bio-basins. Cuts allow street runoff to be absorbed and filtered, reducing urban pollution flowing to ocean via stormdrains.

Beach Access Bill Passed in HI. Hawaii law requires DLNR to maintain beach transit corridors, prohibiting landowners from blocking public shoreline access with vegetation, fences, or walls. Enforcement action after 21-day notice period.

Oahu Bans Plastic Bags!. Surfrider's Oahu Chapter passed plastic bag ban in Honolulu City Council (April 2012, effective 2015). Coalition effort made Hawaii first US state with county-wide bans, reducing ocean plastic pollution.

Lake Worth Surf and Reefs Protected. Surfrider challenged Palm Beach's permit to dredge 1.8 miles of beach with 700k cubic yards of sediment that would bury 7 acres of reefs, harm sea turtles, and damage surfing/fishing. Judge ruled against project in 2008.

Blue Carbon Solutions for Mangrove Restoration in Tañon Strait. Restoring mangroves in Tañon Strait through blue carbon credits to fund community development, address overfishing/pollution, and enhance climate resilience after Typhoon Odette damage.

Jekyll Island Protected. Surfrider's Coastal Georgia chapter successfully advocated to protect Jekyll Island State Park beachfront from commercial development, securing public park designation with improved beach access and an Environmental Conservation Center.

Charleston, SC Single-Use Plastics Reduction Ordinance. Charleston banned plastic bags, styrofoam, and straws to reduce pollution in waterways. Passed Nov 2018, enforced Jan 2020. Chapter helps businesses transition to protect coastal health.

Oceanside Beach Fill Modified to Meet Coastal Preservation Standards. Surfrider San Diego worked with Oceanside and Coastal Commission on beach nourishment program, advocating for dual sand placement sites, enhanced surf monitoring, and corrected impact language to protect surfing areas.

Mangrove and Seagrass Protection, Misool Island, Indonesia. 30-year initiative protecting Raja Ampat's marine ecosystems through mangrove conservation, seagrass restoration, and biodiversity monitoring. Develops carbon/biodiversity credits to finance conservation across Misool's coastlines.

Coastal Commission Requires Proof of Erodible Concrete. Surfrider San Diego stopped untested erodible concrete installation at Solana Beach Tennis Club sea cliffs. Commission required proof material erodes before installation, protecting coastal resources. Jan 2016.

Building Heights Limited in Kill Devil Hills, NC. Surfrider's Outer Banks Chapter successfully preserved oceanfront building height restrictions in Kill Devil Hills to protect eroding shorelines and prevent increased pressure for beach fill and dredging projects.

Access 33 Kept Open. Surfrider's Cape Fear Chapter secured permanent public beach access at Wrightsville Beach Access 33 after 40+ years of use was threatened by property dispute. Town purchased easement through advocacy and negotiation.

Kauai Bans Plastic Shopping Bags. Kauai banned non-biodegradable plastic grocery bags after 2-year campaign. Retailers face $250-1000/day fines. 25,000 reusable bags distributed. Effective Jan 11, 2011 to reduce ocean plastic pollution.
Ponte Vedra FL beach access. Surfrider Foundation campaign securing favorable ruling to open beach access in Ponte Vedra, Florida, protecting public coastal access rights.

Restored Access for Surfers in Miami. Challenged Miami Beach's ban on launching vessels from public beaches. City Commission attempted global prohibition on surfboards/vessels except in designated rental areas, restricting public beach access.

Community Mangrove Protection New Ireland Papua New Guinea. Protects 18,000ha mangroves in New Ireland Province from mining threats through community-led monitoring, carbon measurement, and blue carbon credits. Establishes coastal management plan with local governance (2023-2025).

Building a model for mangrove restoration under Indonesia's new carbon legislation. Restores 1,729 hectares of abandoned fishponds to mangroves in Southeast Sulawesi. Tests Indonesia's 2023 forest carbon regulation on village land. Funded by Blue Carbon Accelerator Fund to enhance coastal resilience and carbon storage.

Safeguarding the biodiversity of Malaysia's Rajang-Belawai Delta. Restoring 77,600 hectares of mangrove forests in Rajang-Belawai Delta threatened by logging and palm oil. Blue carbon project with community benefit-sharing, carbon credits, and biodiversity protection. 2024-2025.

Building sustainable aquaculture in the Sesayap River delta. Integrates mangrove restoration with shrimp farming in Sesayap Delta, Indonesian Borneo. Aims for 5,000 ha aquaculture with 50% mangrove coverage by 2030. Combines sustainable seafood production with blue carbon credits.

West Africa Coastal Areas Resilience Investment Project 2. World Bank project investing in coastal resilience across West Africa, addressing erosion, flooding, and climate adaptation through infrastructure and community-based solutions.

Restoring mangrove and seagrass ecosystems to safeguard Indonesia's coastlines. Restoring mangrove & seagrass in Central Java & West Nusa Tenggara to combat climate change, protect against sea level rise, enhance blue carbon capture & support coastal communities. 30-month project (2023-2025).

Tanzania Scaling-up Sustainable Marine Fisheries and Aquaculture Management Project (TASFAM). Scales up sustainable marine fisheries & aquaculture mgmt in Tanzania. Enhances coastal resource management, improves livelihoods of fishing communities, strengthens governance of marine resources along Tanzanian coast.

Resilient Tourism and Blue Economy Development in Cabo Verde Project. Develops sustainable blue economy and resilient tourism in Cabo Verde through coastal management, marine resource protection, and tourism infrastructure to support economic growth while preserving marine ecosystems.

Accelerating Blue Economy Development in the Kingdom of Morocco. World Bank project to accelerate blue economy development in Morocco, focusing on sustainable marine resource management, coastal development, and ocean-based economic opportunities.

Oceans for Prosperity Project - LAUTRA. World Bank marine conservation project LAUTRA focused on ocean prosperity. Details on specific objectives, implementation methods, timeline and location not available from page content.

Belize Blue Cities and Beyond Project. World Bank project supporting Belize's coastal cities with marine conservation, sustainable development, and blue economy initiatives to protect coastal and marine ecosystems while promoting economic growth.

West Africa Coastal Areas Erosion and Blue Economy Multi-Phased Program. Multi-phased program addressing coastal erosion and promoting blue economy development across West African coastal areas through integrated coastal zone management and sustainable marine resource utilization.

Unleashing the Blue Economy of the Caribbean (UBEC). World Bank project developing Caribbean blue economy through sustainable marine resource management, fisheries, coastal tourism, and ocean-based economic opportunities across Caribbean island nations.

Safeguarding Biodiversity and Livelihoods on North-Western Coast of Madagascar. WWF & UNIMA restore 2,088 hectares of mangroves across 3 sites. Planting, training locals, carbon credits. Sequesters 530k tonnes CO2, protects against cyclones, enhances fisheries & crab farming. 2022-2025.

Guinea - Kounki project - Climate resilience, fisheries and aquaculture. World Bank project in Guinea focusing on climate resilience, fisheries and aquaculture development in the Kounki region to enhance sustainable marine resource management and coastal community livelihoods.

MARINE BIODIVERSITY ASSESSMENT AND PREDICTION ACROSS SPATIAL, TEMPORAL AND HUMAN SCALES. Pan-European marine biodiversity study from viruses to mammals, Mediterranean to Arctic. TREC expedition 2023/24 across 21 coastal countries, 35 marine labs. Creates open-access data hub, ecosystem health indicators.

National Sanctuary Manglares de Tumbes, Peru. Conservation of Peru's largest mangrove forest (29.72 km²) through carbon market certification. Protects 148 bird, 105 fish species. Generates income via carbon credits for local communities. 18 months, 2022-2024.

Human History of Marine Life: Extraction, Knowledge, Drivers & Consumption of Marine Resources, c.100 BCE to c.1860 CE. Global assessment of marine resource exploitation's role in human societies from 100 BCE to 1860 CE. Interdisciplinary study examining when/where marine harvest mattered, socio-economic/environmental drivers, and impacts on development.

Atlantidae: Predators at the Ocean SurfacE as InDicators of chaNge. Studies atlantid heteropods as bio-indicators of ocean acidification and warming. Investigates past, present, future effects on these aragonite-shelled planktonic gastropods to understand surface ocean changes.

Climate relevant interactions and feedbacks: the key role of sea ice and snow in the polar and global climate system. Studies polar sea ice decline & ocean-ice-atmosphere interactions. Improves climate models through satellite/in-situ observations. Quantifies feedback mechanisms & teleconnections for better climate projections.

OBSERVING AND MAPPING MARINE ECOSYSTEMS – NEXT GENERATION TOOLS. Develops toolbox integrating remote sensing, eDNA, optical instruments & citizen science with existing monitoring to map marine ecosystems & biodiversity at higher resolution across 4 European seas for better resource management

OCEAN CITIZEN - Marine forest coastal restoration: an underwater gardening socio-ecological plan. Restores marine forests (seagrasses, seaweeds, corals, sponges) across 3 sites (subtropical, tropical, cold temperate) via 'sea gardeners', ecoengineering, carbon sequestration, citizen involvement, depths to 100m.

MARCO-BOLO. Strengthens European coastal/marine biodiversity observation using eDNA, robotics, acoustics. Develops autonomous monitoring tech, establishes protocols across ecosystems. Links to global ocean health efforts via MBON, GOOS, UN Ocean Decade.

Blueprint for Atlantic-Arctic Agora on cross-sectoral cooperation for restoration of marine and coastal ecosystems and increased climate resilience through transformative innovation. Demonstrates nature-based solutions for marine ecosystem restoration in Atlantic-Arctic coastal areas. Uses ecosystem-based management to boost climate resilience through blue reforestation and pressure reduction at demo sites in Portugal, Ireland, N

The critical role of sedimentary trace element fluxes in ocean biogeochemistry. Investigates trace elements (iron, neodymium, zinc) and isotopes in ocean sediments to understand carbon/oxygen cycles and improve climate predictions through global biogeochemical modeling.

MARINE CARBON PUMP - Chromium isotopes as a tracer of the marine biological carbon pump. Develops Chromium isotope proxy to trace marine biological carbon pump strength, investigating biogeochemical processes regulating ocean CO2 exchange and export productivity through phytoplankton cultures, water-column studies, and sediment analysis.

Beyond the Iron Curtain: Trace Metal Co-limitation of Phytoplankton Growth. Models trace metal co-limitation (iron, cobalt, copper, manganese, zinc) of phytoplankton growth to understand ocean productivity, carbon cycle, and marine food webs. Combines data synthesis with numerical modeling.

Ultimate Paleo-Ocean Records from Biogenic Calcites. Creates accurate paleo-ocean records by analyzing biogenic calcite fossils using ultra-high-resolution isotopic imaging to understand ocean's role in climate evolution, correcting diagenesis bias in sediment records.

Southern Ocean Silicon Cycling: combining views of the past and present using silicon isotopes. Studies Southern Ocean silicon cycling and isotopes to understand nutrient dynamics, carbon export, and climate change over glacial cycles. Analyzes seawater and sediment cores to track silicon transport and diatom activity.

The global ocean carbon cycle after peak emissions: Dynamics and process attribution in a seamless model framework from coastal shelves to the open ocean. Develops forecasting tool to predict global ocean CO2 uptake in low emission scenarios using multi-resolution model. Quantifies ocean carbon sink from coastal to global scales for Paris Agreement monitoring.

BlueActionBANOS. EU Mission Ocean project scaling solutions for biodiversity, pollution reduction, climate-neutral blue economy in Baltic & North Sea. Provides financial & technical support to communities for ocean restoration.

ObsSea4Clim. EU project improving ocean observing for climate assessment through EOV/ECV framework, regional indicators, AI data quality control, and FAIR data standards. Addresses sea ice, ocean warming, marine heat waves globally.

Co-Creating Transformative Pathways to Biological and Ecosystem Ocean Observations. Develops Blueprint for Integrated Ocean Science to improve biological/ecosystem ocean observation. Co-creates with stakeholders to advance data collection, monitoring, and models for Essential Ocean Variables globally.

Next generation multiplatform Ocean observing technologies for research infrastructures. Develops autonomous sensors for ocean CO2 monitoring on moving/fixed platforms. Advances biogeochemical observing systems to track ocean acidification and carbon fluxes, supporting climate policy and blue economy goals.

Support to SET Plan Implementation Working Group and European Technology and Innovation Platform for Ocean Energy. EU project enhancing cooperation in ocean energy sector. Supports ETIP Ocean & SET Plan IWG through coordination, knowledge exchange, sustainability focus. Aims to integrate renewable ocean electricity into European energy systems.

Promoting ocean and water literacy in school communities. ProBleu expands the Network of European Blue Schools to improve ocean/water literacy through open schooling, citizen science, and scientist interaction, protecting marine/freshwater ecosystems and preventing pollution across Europe.

New Copernicus capability for trophic ocean networks. Enhancing Copernicus Marine Service to monitor European marine ecosystems through innovative models fusing satellite, acoustic, pollution & omics data. Simulates higher-trophic-levels, benthic habitats, pollutants for biodiversity conservation.

Blue Carbon production, export and sequestration in emerging polar ecosystems. Studies emerging polar ecosystems in high-latitude seas to assess blue carbon sequestration potential, marine biodiversity impacts, and climate role. Field surveys and models quantify carbon stocks in coastal/pelagic/benthic systems.

SHORE: EmpOweR Students as the agents of cHangE. 36-month ocean literacy project engaging students/teachers across Baltic, Black, Mediterranean seas & Danube/Rhine rivers. Grants to 100 schools, workshops, exhibitions. Digital platform tracks progress. Annual awards.

EDITO-Model Lab - European Digital Twin Ocean Virtual Model Lab. Develops next-gen ocean models & Virtual Ocean Model Lab enabling stakeholders to create ocean management scenarios. Uses AI & HPC to support sustainable blue economy & explore what-if scenarios for ocean hazards. Part of EU Digital Twin Ocean.

Polar Ocean Mitigation Potential. Assesses blue carbon mitigation in Arctic/Antarctic ecosystems. Studies CO2 capture by primary producers, carbon flow, sequestration. Develops models, remote sensing to guide marine protected areas. Pan-Arctic focus.

COmmunity Ocean farms and Local Business cLUstErs (COOL BLUE). Northern European network empowering coastal communities to develop low-impact ocean farming systems in Baltic & North Sea. Creates resilient socioecological systems through sustainable seafood practices, targeting ocean recovery by 2030.

European Hydrography Support Programme. Supports European oceanographic networks with shared facilities, training, equipment pools, and data curation for water column measurements serving marine policy and climate science across coastal countries.

Marine SABRES - Marine Systems Approaches for Biodiversity Resilience and Ecosystem Sustainablity. Co-designing Simple Social-Ecological Systems approach to enable Ecosystem-Based Management across Europe. Reversing marine biodiversity decline through sustainable blue economy integration in Tuscan Archipelago, Arctic NE Atlantic, Macaronesia.

Marine Coastal Ecosystems Biodiversity and Services in a Changing World. Studies climate change impacts on seagrass, kelp, coral reefs, mangroves, salt marshes. Develops models, vulnerability assessments, nature-based solutions for EU marine coastal ecosystem conservation from tropics to sub-polar regions.

MARine Biodiversity and Ecosystem Functioning leading to Ecosystem Services. 23 institutes from 15 EU countries evaluate links between marine biodiversity, ecosystem functioning & services across Arctic to Mediterranean. Develops ecological & economic valuation tools for policy.

DiverSea - Integrated Observation, Monitoring and Prediction Architecture for Functional Biodiversity of Coastal Seas. Develops DNA-based marine monitoring using eDNA/eRNA, autonomous systems, satellite data, and AI-ML to map coastal habitats, predict biodiversity, and link ecosystem functions to services via interactive dashboard for policymakers.
